title: PLC Application Development Intern 100% (m/f/d
description:
Ultra-Pure Water+ division of Ecolab (former Ovivo Electronics), is a global provider of advanced equipment, technology, and systems to produce ultrapure water (UPW). We are dedicated to innovation, offering energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable solutions to the world’s most challenging water and wastewater issues.

As a PLC Application Development Intern, you will support our automation engineers in developing and validating a Siemens S7-400 control application for a continuous water treatment process.

Joining Ecolab means being part of a global team of innovative and passionate professionals who are committed to preserving water, our planet's most critical resource. It also means combining our efforts and talents towards a more sustainable future – together.


How You’ll Make an Impact:

· PLC application development: Develop control software for a Siemens S7-400 platform used in a continuous water treatment process.

· Sequence control: Implement process sequences using GRAFCET-based principles, operating modes, interlocks, and permissives.

· Alarm and diagnostics: Configure alarms, hardware diagnostics, and clear fault-handling logic for operators and maintenance teams.

· I/O and configuration: Integrate field I/O, equipment configuration, and process interfaces within the PLC application.

· Testing and simulation: Prepare and execute platform tests and simulations to validate real-time control behavior before deployment.

· Documentation and collaboration: Produce technical documentation and work closely with the local automation team during design reviews and testing.


Qualifications:

· You are completing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in automation, industrial computing, electrical engineering, computer science, robotics, or a related field.

· Knowledge of real-time PLC programming principles, sequential control or GRAFCET, and scripting is expected.

· Initial experience with Siemens SIMATIC Manager, TIA Portal, S7-300/400, or comparable PLC platforms is an advantage.

· You enjoy diversified tasks and hands-on work in technical workshops and on industrial systems.

· You show initiative and creativity, and you are flexible, structured, and able to work independently with guidance from experienced engineers.

· You have strong team-working and communication skills and can collaborate with international departments, suppliers, and customers.

· You have English skills suitable for daily business use. German, French, or other languages are an advantage.


What we offer:

· Working in our young and international Automation Team, with new challenges to solve every day.

· An opportunity to contribute widely and develop your skills in an agile company.

· Dealing with the cutting edge in ultrapure water technology in the electronic industry.

· Technical training in the position related field as well as the possibility for professional development in Switzerland.

· Expected start date: March 2027, or by mutual agreement.

· A modern workplace in Witterswil.

· At Ecolab we are committed to providing working environments where everyone is included and treated fairly and with respect


About Ecolab:

At Ecolab, we prioritize our talent-first philosophy by creating the most capable and diverse team to excel at our nearly three million customer sites. Building on a century of innovation, our 48,000 associates help deliver comprehensive science-based solutions, data-driven insights and world-class service to advance food safety, maintain clean and safe environments, and optimize water and energy use, and improve operational efficiencies and sustainability for customers in the food, healthcare, life sciences, hospitality and industrial markets in more than 170 countries around the world. Our solutions not only enhance operational efficiency but also contribute to sustainability and public health, making a positive impact on the world. We are committed to eliminating unnecessary complexities and embracing a beginner's mindset, continuously seeking new perspectives and innovative solutions to stay ahead in a rapidly changing world.


Ecolab’s commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I) reflects our longstanding value of working together to integrate diverse perspectives to challenge ourselves, reach our goals and do what’s right.


Apply today and join one of the most ethical companies with over a hundred years of history.


Join Ecolab and help us protect what’s vital.

title: Stock Receiver
description:

title: Maintenance Apprentice (Plant)
description:

The Apprentice Maintenance Mechanic works with the assistance of a Maintenance Technician, Lead Maintenance Technician, Maintenance Supervisor or Maintenance Manager when performing technical and diagnostic type repairs.

  • Prepare work areas for Mechanics: transfer tools, parts, equipment, and supplies to and from work areas
  • Examine and test machinery, equipment, components, and parts for defects to ensure proper functioning
  • May complete repairs and replacements under the direction of a Mechanic or Maintenance Manager

  • May, once certified, operate a forklift or other material handling equipment.
  • Maintain accurate and complete records, document all work performed appropriately and location.
  • Assist in maintaining parts and supplies inventory by reporting low supply levels to supervisors.
  • Ensure all paperwork is clear, complete, legible and accurate in accordance with SOPs.
  • Utilizing continuous improvement mindset, assist in identifying opportunities to improve processes.
  • Follow Good Manufacturing Processes.
  • Maintain a clean, sanitary and safe work area.

  • Career growth opportunities – we promote from within!
  • Comprehensive healthcare benefits
  • Service recognition and employee rewards*
  • Employee referral program

*varies by company

T.G. Lee Dairy is a farmer-owned brand of Dairy Farmers of America (DFA), a dairy marketing cooperative owned by more than 12,500 family farmers. DFA manufactures a variety of dairy products, including cheese, butter, fluid milk, ice cream, dairy ingredients and more, under well-known and established regional brands. Our fingerprints touch thousands of brands across the marketplace, and we’re passionate about delivering the simple pleasures of dairy to people everywhere, straight from our family farm-owners.

title: Electronics Repair Technician II
description:
Location: Orlando, United States of America

Thales people architect solutions that enable two-thirds of planes to take off and land safely. We create in-flight entertainment systems that engross 50 million fliers every year and we develop the avionics that control the world’s largest commercial aircrafts. In an increasingly fast paced world, we make the unpredictable, predictable by connecting and entertain passengers to make your life better. Combining a diversity of talents, we master the decisive moments that matter to passengers and airlines. Whatever it takes.

Electronics Repair Technician II

Orlando, FL (Fully Onsite)

Position Summary

Thales is looking for an Electronics Repair Technician II whose role involves performing intermediate-level electronic maintenance, testing, repairs, servicing, and modifications of electronic equipment in accordance with FAA regulations.


In this position, you will troubleshoot and repair electronic equipment, perform required testing and maintenance activities, and ensure all work is completed in accordance with applicable technical procedures, quality standards, and regulatory requirements. Your technical skills and attention to detail will help support safe, reliable equipment performance and overall production goals.


Referral Bonus Eligibility: Tier 1 - $2,500


Key Areas of Responsibility


  • Troubleshoot and repair electronic equipment to the component level in accordance with FAA regulations, company inspection procedures, ISO requirements, and applicable technical documentation.
  • Modify and maintain equipment using service bulletins, manufacturer documentation, layout drawings, and schematic diagrams for assemblies such as power supplies, oscillators, amplifiers, and related electronic subunits.
  • Perform assigned repair and maintenance procedures independently or in collaboration with experienced technicians, following established schedules, detailed instructions, and approved troubleshooting processes.
  • Review work orders and completed repairs to confirm customer-requested activities have been performed prior to release, with work subject to review by senior technicians, supervisors, and inspectors.
  • Complete required quality and production documentation, prepare repair estimates, and maintain accurate maintenance records in accordance with current quality assurance requirements and company procedures.
  • Communicate with cross-functional teams to support the repair process, participate in technician cross-training, and complete required training on specialized test equipment and advanced troubleshooting techniques.

Minimum Qualifications


  • High school diploma or GED, with a minimum of two years of experience in electronics repair and/or maintenance.
  • Working knowledge of Federal Aviation Regulations and other applicable regulatory requirements, with the ability to accurately document incoming product condition and maintenance activities.
  • Intermediate understanding of electronic theory, troubleshooting techniques, and standard electronic components, with familiarity in both analog and digital electronics, hardware, and software.
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, wiring diagrams, schematics, and related technical documentation.
  • Experience using PCs and electronic test equipment, including manual and automatic test benches, oscilloscopes, multimeters, and other basic and advanced test instruments; ability to perform adjustments as required.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to think creatively when addressing operational and technical issues.


Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer at the time of hire. This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship or for assuming sponsorship of an employment visa now or in the future.


Special Position Requirements


  • Prior military or commercial avionics Level 3 component repair experience is preferred.
  • FAA Repairman Certificate or other relevant FAA certification is a plus.
  • Working knowledge of Federal Aviation Regulations and other applicable government regulatory requirements, with the ability to accurately document incoming product condition and maintenance activities.
  • Ability to perform moderate physical activity, including occasionally lifting and handling objects up to 50 pounds and frequently lifting and handling objects up to 20 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Fine motor skills and manual dexterity are required to handle small components and operate hand tools on a frequent basis.
  • Ability to work in a repair station environment with elevated noise levels and a flexible schedule that may include different shifts, weekends, holidays, and overtime as required.

title: Technical Field Claim Specialist - Property
description:
MSIG USA continues to grow!

Company Overview:

MSIG USA is the US-based subsidiary of MS&AD Insurance Group Holdings, Inc., one of the world’s top P&C carriers and a global Class 15 insurer, with A+ ratings and a reach that spans 40+ countries and regions. Leveraging our 350-year heritage, MSIG USA brings the financial strength, expertise, and global footprint to offer commercial insurance solutions that address your business’s unique risks.

Responsible for the independent investigation, field evaluation, coverage analysis, strategy, negotiation and resolution of highly complex and high-severity commercial property claims across a national footprint. The role handles primary and excess property claims involving significant real and business property damage, time-element loss, business interruption, equipment breakdown, inland marine and catastrophe exposures. Serves as MSIG USA's senior field representative at loss locations, working directly with insureds, brokers, independent adjusters, public adjusters, experts and support vendors to establish facts, control the adjustment process, develop sound reserves and drive timely, equitable claim outcomes in accordance with policy terms, delegated authority, company claim handling guidelines, regulatory requirements and applicable fair claims practices laws.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Claims Handling, Field Investigation and Technical Management

  • Independently manages highly complex and high-severity commercial property claims from assignment through resolution, including primary and excess matters, catastrophe losses and claims presenting significant financial, coverage, operational or reputational risk.
  • Deploys to loss locations throughout the United States when applicable, including on short notice when business needs or catastrophe response requires, and conducts on-site inspections to assess damage, causation, scope, mitigation, salvage, repairability and business continuity concerns.
  • Establishes and executes a written claim strategy addressing coverage, causation, valuation, scope of damage, time-element exposure, experts, vendors, reserves, recovery opportunities, negotiation and resolution; updates the strategy as material facts develop.
  • Analyzes commercial property policies, forms, endorsements, schedules, deductibles, sublimits, valuation provisions, coinsurance, exclusions and conditions; prepares or supports timely and well-reasoned reservation of rights, partial disclaimer and coverage position communications.
  • Handles claims involving buildings, machinery and equipment, stock, contents, improvements and betterments, extra expense, business income, contingent business interruption, equipment breakdown, inland marine, builder’s risk, cargo, fidelity and crime exposures, as assigned.
  • Evaluates primary and excess attachment, underlying limits, exhaustion, allocation, other insurance, subrogation and contribution issues; coordinates with underlying or excess insurers and promptly escalates potential tower-impacting developments.
  • Establishes and maintains timely, supportable indemnity and expense reserves based on the available facts and probable exposure; communicates material reserve changes and recommends authority with clear supporting analysis.
  • Negotiates complex property and time-element claims directly with insureds, independent adjusters, public adjusters, brokers and other authorized representatives while maintaining professional, transparent and disciplined claim handling.
  • Identifies, preserves and pursues subrogation, salvage, contribution and other recovery opportunities; coordinates evidence preservation, destructive testing and expert activity when appropriate.
  • Recognizes matters requiring leadership, coverage counsel, special investigation, reinsurance or other escalation and communicates significant developments promptly.

Vendor, Expert and Adjustment Management

  • Selects, assigns, directs and evaluates independent adjusters and approved support vendors across a national footprint, including engineers, forensic accountants, building consultants, equipment specialists, cause-and-origin experts, environmental consultants, restoration firms, salvage vendors and counsel.
  • Defines assignment scope, deliverables, reporting cadence, budget and decision authority; monitors quality, timeliness, cost and compliance and redirects assignments when performance or claim strategy requires.
  • Leads field meetings, inspections, scope discussions and claim reviews involving insured representatives, independent and public adjusters, contractors, consultants and other stakeholders.
  • Coordinates catastrophe and large-loss field response, including vendor deployment, site access, loss mitigation, initial exposure assessment, reporting and handoff or continued ownership as directed.

Customer and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Serves as a primary technical point of contact for insureds and brokers on assigned matters, providing proactive, accurate and professional communication regarding claim status, coverage process, information needs, exposure, strategy and next steps.
  • Partners with underwriting, account management, Claims leadership, Home Office and other internal stakeholders to address coverage intent, account considerations, claim trends and material developments while preserving claim-handling independence.
  • Participates in claim reviews, stewardship meetings and account discussions and presents complex claim issues in concise, business-focused terms suitable for senior stakeholders.

Operational, Regulatory and Quality Responsibilities - approximately 10%

  • Maintains complete, timely and accurate claim system documentation, including inspection findings, coverage analysis, reserve rationale, action plans, vendor direction, negotiation history and material developments.
  • Complies with delegated settlement and reserve authority, company claim handling guidelines, fair claims practices requirements, licensing and continuing education obligations, information-security standards and applicable state and federal requirements.
  • Completes required management, Home Office, reinsurance, audit and quality-assurance reporting accurately and on time.
  • Acts as a senior technical resource to property claim colleagues and may support file consultation, training, catastrophe readiness, vendor governance, process improvement and special assignments.

SU

Education and Experience

  • High school diploma or G.E.D. required; bachelor’s degree in insurance, business, risk management, engineering, construction or a related field preferred.
  • 8+ years of progressively responsible commercial property claim experience, including demonstrated handling of highly complex, high-severity or large-loss claims.
  • Demonstrated field experience conducting on-site inspections and managing losses involving insureds, independent adjusters, public adjusters, contractors, experts and other claim professionals.
  • Demonstrated experience with primary and excess property claims, complex coverage analysis, reserving, negotiation and vendor or expert management.
  • Experience handling significant business interruption, time-element, equipment breakdown, inland marine or catastrophe losses strongly preferred.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Advanced knowledge of commercial property claim investigation, building and equipment damage evaluation, estimating concepts, repair and replacement methods, mitigation, valuation and time-element analysis.
  • Ability to interpret complex commercial property policies, endorsements, schedules, engineering reports, estimates, inventories, financial records, forensic accounting analyses and other technical documentation.
  • Strong field judgment and situational awareness, including the ability to identify safety concerns, preserve evidence, assess site conditions and coordinate multiple parties at an active loss location.
  • Ability to challenge assumptions, reconcile competing scopes and estimates, evaluate proof-of-loss submissions and reach well-supported claim decisions.
  • Strong negotiation, conflict-management and relationship skills, including the ability to work effectively with sophisticated insureds and public adjusters while protecting MSIG USA’s contractual and financial interests.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including executive-level claim reporting and the ability to explain complex coverage, damage and financial issues clearly.
  • Ability to prioritize and manage multiple high-severity claims, field assignments, vendors, deadlines and stakeholders with limited supervision.
  • ·Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, claim management systems and property estimating or related technical tools used in commercial property adjustment.

title: Materials Management Senior I
description:

Accountable to coordinate the specification and procurement of materials and equipment for capital projects involving major gas storage/transmission facilities.   • Work with project manager/engineer to specify capital material and equipment

title: Health Unit Coordinator
description:
Kaweah Health is a publicly owned, community healthcare organization that provides comprehensive health services to the greater Visalia area in central California. With more than 5,000 employees, Kaweah Health provides state-of-the-art medicine and high-quality preventive services in our acute care hospital, specialized health centers and clinics. Our eight-campus healthcare district has 613 beds and offers comprehensive health services across a broad continuum of care.

It takes a special person to work for Kaweah Health. We serve a region where the needs are great, which makes the rewards even greater. Every day, we care for people facing unique challenges and in need of healing. Throughout it all, our focus is to make a difference, and we do — in the health of our patients, our loved ones, and our community.

Benefits Eligible

Full-Time Benefit Eligible

Work Shift

Night - 12 Hour Shift (United States of America)

Department

6380 OB Postpartum

A liaison to the medical nursing unit who provides communication between all disciplines as well as patients, families, and visitors. Health Unit Coordinators are responsible for accurate order entry and management of patient medical chart.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education
Preferred: High school diploma or equivalent


Experience
Preferred: Healthcare experience

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities
Able to exhibit a courteous and friendly manner to others
Organizational and computer skills necessary to support the needs of the department


JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Essential

Greets visitors and interdisciplinary team members with a smile and provides assistance as appropriate within the scope of their training.

Collaborates and communicates with the nursing staff to maintain accurate records during the patient's hospitalization. Communicates effectively with different departments and people. Assists staff with communication within and between departments.

Keeps charge nurse informed or admissions, discharges and transfers by frequent communication. Performs electronic updates to appropriate systems for admissions, discharges and transfers (i.e. patient disposition, assignment management application, throughput application). Accurately enters patient data into computer on all admissions, discharges, and transfers. Accurately and legibly maintains staffing assignment sheets.

Utilizes appropriate resources for clarification of orders. Transcribes orders as directed by unit procedures or downtime processes. Follows all departmental downtime procedures. Able to perform all regular duties when the hospital computer system is not available.


Prepares and maintains patient's charts. Reviews charts at the end of every shift to ensure adequate supply of forms are filed in the chart and that the chart is maintained in proper order. Ensures that after discharge the patient's chart is completely assembled for Medical Records. Prepares teh chart in proper order for patients transferred to another unit.

Accurately and legibly maintains staffing, record of admissions and discharges, sick calls, floating, and docking per established unit process.

Notifies Case Management (when on unit), when orders are written for discharge or discharge planning (i.e. placement, durable medical equipment, home health, acute transfers).

Obtains Medical Records for physicians from other facilities.

Arranges for a follow-up appointment with Primary Care Physicians (PCP). Refers to Case management if they do not have a PCP.

Files all hard copy medical records appropriately in the patient chart, i.e. lab results, progress notes, operating room records, EKG strips, downtime order forms.

Copies chart and all materials as directed and distributes to appropriate people.

Is an active participant in achieving quality patient care.

Refers complaints and problems to the Nurse Manager, Assistant Nurse Manager or Team Leader. Holds self and other team members accountable to maintain standards.

Maintains confidentiality with all patient care issues.

Answers patient or family questions or refers them to the appropriate personnel.

Answers patient call light and directs requests to the appropriate person. Ensures the patients request is received by a person who can assist them timely. Answers phone within four rings.

Keeps work area and nurses’ station clean and well organized.

Orients students, new unit staff, and student volunteers to the unit's clerical function. Mentors new hires on computer usage appropriate to their position/unit.

Assists nursing staff in achieving quality patient care by transporting specimens and retrieving items needed for patient care. Is certified to pick up blood from the Lab.

Performs data collection for audits and other performance improvement initiatives as delegated by the unit leader or charge nurse. Utilizes the electronic health record reports and dashboard (i.e. Clinical Leader Organizer) to monitor and collect information as assigned.

Reads and complies with current hospital/patient care procedures and policies as applicable.

Code of Ethics: They shall conduct themselves in such a manner as to gain respect and confidence of the patients, health care personnel, and community, as well as respecting the human dignity of each individual. They shall protect the patients' rights, including the right to privacy. They shall strive to achieve and maintain a high level of competency. They shall strive to improve their knowledge and skills by participating in educational and professional activities and sharing the benefits of their attainments with their colleagues. Unethical and illegal professional activities shall be reported to the appropriate authorities.

Additional


Demonstrates the knowledge and skills necessary to provide care and services appropriate to the population served on the assigned unit or work area.

Performs other duties as assigned.

$20.38 -$30.57

If you want to use your talents alongside people who face each day with courage and purpose, in an environment that empowers you to do your absolute best, this is where you belong.

title: Waste Reduction Manager
description:
Compensation Range

$54,146.40 - $73,491.11

Please note: This job opening may close earlier than the stated date, due to high candidate volume. If interested, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Who We Are:

At the City of High Point, we celebrate the creator in everyone. Building on our rich cultural history steeped in industrialism and innovation, our employees seek not only to transform themselves, but the world around us. We are collaborators, we are makers, we are visionaries.

We invite you to explore the many opportunities to serve our community, by sharing your talents, skills, and expertise. You'll join a diverse team of over 1300 individuals dedicated not just to making a career, but a difference; because what we create in High Point, changes the world!


Our Core Values:

  • Stewardship: We manage the city’s resources responsibly and make decisions that sustain High Point’s future. In other words, we take care of what we have today to build what we’ll need tomorrow
  • Welcoming: We create a friendly, open environment where residents, partners, and visitors feel valued and embraced. We want everyone who connects with High Point to feel welcomed, like they belong here.
  • Integrity: We act with honesty, transparency, and ethical responsibility in everything we do. That means doing what’s right – even when no one’s watching. This is how we earn our community’s trust.
  • Productivity: We stay focused on results, fostering creativity, innovation, and outside-the-box thinking. We don’t just get things done – we find smarter, better ways to do them.

What We Offer:
The City of High Point offers a competitive salary commensurate with education and experience. We also offer generous benefit package for full-time employees which include but are not limited to:

  • A guaranteed life-long monthly pension, once vested after 5 years of service
  • 401K and 457B Retirement Plans
  • PTO earned within first year
  • 13 Paid Holidays per year
  • Tuition Reimbursement Plan
  • Competitive medical, dental, and vision plans effective day one

What You'll Do:

To supervise recycling programs, waste reduction and sustainability, and illegal dumping enforcement to ensure that the plans, coordination of activities and administering waste reduction programs, issues and concerns impacting the community and other City departments are accomplished.

Work is performed under the general supervision of the Environmental Services Superintendent.

Essential Tasks & Responsibilities:

Essential Tasks

  • Oversee programs like Keep High Point Beautiful, Bee City and Adopt-A-Street that promote positive behaviors for the environment and in the handling of waste as allowed and directed by the City of High Point ordinance and guidelines;
  • Supervisor for Environmental Services Code Enforcement Officer & Recycling Programs Coordinator; Coordinate and monitor all training for assigned staff. Ensure all work plans and objectives are achieved. Administer and monitor all special projects that may be assigned
  • Work with Local Code Enforcement Division on a case-by-case basis to ensure ordinance compliance within the city with regards to illegal dumping
  • Attend and participate in professional group meetings, stay abreast of solid waste trends and innovations
  • Performs cost analysis and feasibility studies for waste diversion process improvement and program designs
  • Serves as an information resource on waste reduction for the city including city departments, and throughout the community of High Point; Respond to requests and complaints from citizens, other city divisions/departments,
  • Works with Environmental Services staff to regularly check on the materials within recycling collection containers, including recycling carts, dumpsters, compactors, trailers, etc.;
  • Manages grant application processes and administration of received grants, identifies grant opportunities to support waste reduction programs, research various sources to identify grant funding opportunities;
  • Prepares and maintains records on waste reduction programming programs and reports findings to appropriate entity or individual;
  • Works with direct reports to assist with marketing information and enforcement of illegal dumping code violations;
  • Coordinates programs and projects with outside agencies with a waste reduction focus;
  • Organize and manage litter cleanup efforts across the city including existing programs as well as development of new programs, work to increase volunteer base and board engagement;
  • Oversee social media and website content for waste reduction programs including coordination efforts with the city’s PIO Department;
  • Ensures that all waste reduction and illegal dumping enforcement programs are performed in accordance with OSHA and City Safety Standards and Policies;
  • On-going professional development will be required; including waste reduction-based industry training/classes and networking;
  • Approve leave time for personnel and complete performance evaluations;

title: Congressional Reporter (5-month contract)
description:
Application Instructions

Please list all professional experience and explain any gaps in employment history. All of your application materials, which may include PDF files of work samples and/or links to audio, video, photography or graphics, must be uploaded to the field labeled Resume/Cover Letter/Work Samples to be considered for the position.

Join the future of news


We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

The Washington Post is seeking a sourced, creative and high-energy reporter to cover the U.S. Senate on a temporary basis.


This is a full-time, approximately five-month assignment filling in for a member of our Congress team who will be on parental leave. The temporary contract position is expected to begin Nov. 30.


We are looking for an aggressive and versatile journalist who can hit the ground running on one of Washington’s most competitive beats. The successful candidate will know how to cultivate sources, break news, explain complex policy fights and demystify the sometimes arcane workings of the Senate — from reconciliation and the filibuster to holds, confirmations and floor procedure — for a broad audience.


The ideal candidate has a proven ability to deliver agenda-setting reporting and a clear sense of how to tell stories about Congress that resonate well beyond Washington. This reporter will illuminate the personalities, power struggles and policy battles shaping the Senate, bringing authority and insight to consequential developments while finding opportunities for enterprise and accountability reporting. We are looking for someone who can deploy seriousness, wit and narrative flair as the story demands.


This position is based in our Washington, D.C., newsroom.


What Motivates You

  • You are driven to break news and compete aggressively on one of Washington’s most consequential beats.
  • You thrive on cultivating sources and uncovering what is happening behind the scenes.
  • You enjoy making complicated legislative and procedural fights clear and compelling for a general audience.
  • You are fascinated by the personalities, alliances and power dynamics that shape the Senate.
  • You are collaborative and eager to contribute immediately to a high-performing team.

How You’ll Support the Mission

  • Work collaboratively with The Post’s Congress team to make what happens in the Senate — and how it affects people across the country and around the world — interesting and accessible to a broad audience.
  • Break news on senators, Senate leadership, key committees and the political and policy dynamics driving the chamber.
  • Quickly develop and maintain sources among senators, aides, committee staff, administration officials, activists, lobbyists and others seeking to influence the Senate.
  • Cover major policy and procedural fights, including legislation, nominations and confirmations, explaining both the political stakes and real-world consequences.
  • Track the relationship between the Senate and other centers of political power, including the House, White House and federal judiciary.
  • Identify opportunities for enterprise and accountability reporting, including potential conflicts of interest, misconduct and abuses of power.
  • Produce fast, authoritative journalism as news develops while pursuing original reporting that distinguishes The Post’s coverage.
  • Adhere to the highest ethical standards, ensuring fairness, rigor and meaningful opportunities for subjects of our reporting to respond.
  • Think creatively about the best formats for our journalism, collaborating with data reporters, graphics journalists, photographers, designers and video journalists to maximize impact.

The Skills and Experience You Bring

  • At least five years of experience covering Congress, another legislature or a similarly competitive political or government beat, with a track record of breaking impactful stories.
  • Experience covering the Senate is strongly preferred.
  • Existing Senate sourcing and familiarity with Senate rules, institutions and procedure that would enable you to contribute quickly are significant advantages.
  • Demonstrated ability to report and write breaking news with speed, clarity and precision.
  • Strong source-building skills and an instinct for original and consequential reporting.
  • An ability to explain complicated policy and procedural matters without resorting to insider language.
  • Excellent news judgment and the ability to balance the demands of daily coverage with enterprise and accountability reporting.
  • An eagerness to collaborate with colleagues across a competitive, fast-moving newsroom.
  • A commitment to accuracy, fairness and the highest standards of journalism.

Interested candidates should upload a cover letter, résumé and three examples of their work (as PDFs) to our jobs portal. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled, but those received by Nov. 1 will be prioritized. The cover letter should be addressed to Deputy Congress Editor Sean Collins, Congress Editor John Wagner, Deputy Politics & Government Editor Jen Liberto and Politics & Government Editor Nick Baumann.


This is a full-time contract position expected to begin Nov. 30 and last approximately five months while a member of the Congress team is on leave. It pays between $8,000 - $10,000 per month, depending on experience level and qualifications.

Your story awaits. Apply today!

Learn more about The Post at careers.washingtonpost.com.

The Senior Architect Systems Engineer is a highly influential technical leadership role that helps shape the future of advanced X-ray tube platforms used in medical imaging. Your work will directly contribute to technologies that support healthcare professionals and patients around the world.

In this position, you will define and advance system architecture, technology roadmaps, and product strategy for X-ray tube platforms. You will lead high-impact projects and complex assignments with long-term business implications while providing technical guidance across multiple engineering disciplines.

You will partner with colleagues in product management, engineering, manufacturing, service, and customer-facing teams to ensure designs meet performance, reliability, manufacturability, regulatory, and customer requirements.   • Provide technical leadership to an X-ray generation engineering team across all product design aspects of the assigned system.

  • Coordinate with partner organizations, including manufacturing and customer field engineering teams.

  • Master’s degree in Engineering or a related field.

Job Purpose:

The Director, Business Office Planning is a leadership role within the Business Office, accountable for driving effective operation of Business Office planning, prioritization and governance. This position ensures strategic alignment, prioritization, and resource optimization, and delivery transparency across the business office to support achievement of business segment financial targets and objectives.

The Director leads a team responsible for portfolio planning, roadmap management, governance, and investment decision support. The role oversees the development and maintenance of the business office 12–18-month delivery roadmap, facilitates portfolio prioritization and planning processes, and provides data-driven recommendations regarding funding decisions, resource tradeoffs, initiative readiness, and portfolio performance. The Director collaborates closely with segment leaders, strategy, finance, and technology leaders, to ensure successful execution of business priorities.


Job Responsibilities:

Business Office Planning & Governance Leadership:

  • Facilitate business office planning forums to align on priorities, dependencies, and resource allocation with segment leadership.
  • Establish, maintain and continuously improve business ofifce planning governance frameworks to ensure strategic alignment, prioritization, and effective execution of portfolio investments.
  • Collaborate with key stakeholders (e.g., strategy, finance, technology) to align portfolio decisions with strategic objectives and outcomes.
  • Partner with Portfolio Lead to ensure governance standards are consistently applied across portfolio initiatives, including initiative readiness, quality assurance, dependency management, and execution monitoring.
  • Drive transparency and accountability for portfolio decisions, delivery commitments, and execution outcomes.

Portfolio Planning & Prioritization:

  • Business Office Portfolio Roadmap: Oversee the development and maintenance of the 12-18 month delivery roadmap, providing a clear view of priorities, milestones, dependencies, sequencing, and resource needs.
  • Lead annual, quarterly, and ongoing portfolio planning processes that translate segment strategy into executable priorities; represent the Business Office at enterprise technology intake and sequencing meetings to ingest this work.
  • Provide recommendations on portfolio investments, funding decisions, and resource allocation to optimize business outcomes.
  • Monitor portfolio demand and capacity to ensure alignment between planned initiatives and available resources.
  • Drive execution planning discipline across portfolio initiatives to improve predictability and delivery success

Portfolio Performance and Delivery Oversight:

  • Monitor portfolio health, delivery progress, risks and execution challenges across the business office portfolio.
  • Facilitate the escalation and resolution of portfolio issues and cross functional dependencies.
  • Provide insights and recommendations to the business office leadership team, enabling proactive decision-making.

Performance Monitoring and Reporting:

  • Develop and maintain portfolio performance reporting, roadmap dashboards, funding analytics, and governance reporting to support Business Office decision-making.
  • Deliver accurate, timely, and actionable insights on portfolio health, resource utilization, roadmap progress, and investment performance.
  • Establish reporting standards that enable consistent portfolio visibility and informed prioritization decisions.

Team Leadership and Accountability:

  • Lead, mentor, and develop Business Office portfolio management leads, Portfolio Planning Consultants, and Portfolio and Process Analysts.
  • Provide strategic leadership for portfolio planning, roadmap management, governance, prioritization and business performance reporting.
  • Live into and role model TruStage leadership expectations.
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, data-driven decision making and execution excellence.
  • Conduct regular performance reviews and provide coaching and feedback to team.
  • Identify training needs and opportunities for team members, providing support and encouragement for continued growth and professional development.

  • Business Office Delivery Roadmap: A 12–18-month view of initiatives, milestones, dependencies, resource requirements, and sequencing.
  • Portfolio Prioritization and Investment Recommendations: Data-driven analyses supporting funding, resource, and prioritization decisions.
  • Portfolio Health and Performance Reporting: Visibility into portfolio progress, capacity utilization, risks, and execution effectiveness.
  • Business Office Planning & Governance Frameworks: Standards for initiative readiness, quality assurance, prioritization, and execution.
  • Strategic Planning Insights and Tradeoff Analyses: Recommendations supporting achievement of segment objectives and optimal resource allocation.

title: Software Engineering Intern, Developer Tools - 2027
description:
At NVIDIA, we build groundbreaking products for the following businesses: Automotive, Gaming, Deep Learning, and High-Performance Computing. Make a significant impact and contribute to the development of tools and software components used to debug, profile, and analyze GPU accelerated applications through the developer tools product line. Learn and innovate as you develop across any layer of the software stack, from user workflows, graphics user interfaces design, tools software systems, compute or graphics driver code bases, to the lower level of the GPU registers and microcode - develop the most powerful tools to enable next-gen GPU accelerated application breakthrough. As a Developer Tools Software Engineering intern, you will help developing software that empowers GPU application developers to build GPU applications that are known throughout the world – from graphics to compute to deep learning. We are seeking a passionate software developer to join our effort to advance the state of software performance tuning and debugging for the GPUs on NVIDIA platforms.

What you'll be doing:

  • Develop the Compute Sanitizer (which is a suite of memory checker) tools for GPUs running on Linux, Windows, and embedded operating systems

  • Work with developer tools, driver and architecture teams to contribute to the design, implementation, and verification of product features and components that are part of the Developer Tools product portfolio

  • Develop user workflows and user interface solutions to empower the user of the products

  • Innovate and improve our GPU profiling and debugging libraries with new features to allow NVIDIA's customers to extract the best performance out of their applications

  • Working on validation and hardware bring up of NVIDIA GPU developer tools features that are utilized by compute-sanitizer

What we need to see:

  • Pursuing a B.S. EE/CS, MS, or PhD

  • Passionate about the GPU - compute - and learning how complex systems work

  • Passionate about quality and driven by results

  • Strong programming ability in C, C++

  • Knowledge of computer architecture (e.g.: x86, ARM CPUs, GPUs)

  • Experience working in device drivers, real-time systems, game console middleware, or other low-level library development

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Background including experience with shipping commercial applications, contributing code to device drivers or system software

  • Knowledge of a GPU API such as: Direct3D, Vulkan, OpenGL, OpenCL, CUDA and simulation or Emulation experience - writing and debugging tests

  • Experience with code patching and ELF/DWARF knowledge

  • Understand core technologies as it applies to GPU hardware and ability to read and write assembly language for multiple processor architectures

  • Knowledge or experience in compute architecture, operating systems, and compilers and for candidates interest in GUI work – experience with Qt

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most brilliant and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you are creative and autonomous, we want to hear from you. The GPU, our invention, serves as the visual cortex of modern computers and is at the heart of our products and services. Our work opens up new universes to explore, enables amazing creativity and discovery, and powers what were once science fiction inventions from artificial intelligence to autonomous cars. NVIDIA is looking for phenomenal people in multiple disciplines to help us accelerate the next wave of computing.

Meadow Gold Dairy is a farmer-owned brand of Dairy Farmers of America (DFA), a dairy marketing cooperative owned by more than 12,500 family farmers. title: Senior Project Manager
description:
About DayOne Data Centers

DayOne Data Centers is a Singapore-headquartered global digital infrastructure platform that develops and operates next-generation data centers across Asia Pacific and Europe. Trusted by leading hyperscalers and businesses, the company engineers, builds, and operates high-capacity, AI-ready campuses with speed, scale, and reliability.



About DayOne Data Centers

DayOne Data Centers is a Singapore-headquartered global digital infrastructure platform that develops and operates next-generation data centers across Asia Pacific and Europe. Trusted by leading hyperscalers and businesses, the company engineers, builds, and operates high-capacity, AI-ready campuses with speed, scale, and reliability.


Why DayOne?
The Chonburi campus is one of the most significant data center builds in Southeast Asia right now, and this role has full end-to-end ownership of it — from initiation through to live handover. You’ll work inside a technically demanding, multi-contractor environment, on infrastructure that will run for decades. DayOne is a well-funded company at an active growth stage — the people who deliver well here build their careers here too.

About the Role
You’ll lead data center construction projects end to end, from initiation through commissioning and handover — owning scope, budget, schedule, and the full contractor and vendor ecosystem on site. This is a senior delivery role for someone who has run mission-critical construction before and can operate fluently within a technically demanding, multi-contractor environment from day one.

Project Leadership

• Lead end-to-end data center construction projects from initiation through commissioning and handover.
• Develop detailed project scopes, budgets, schedules, and resource plans.
• Manage internal teams, external vendors, contractors, engineers, and consultants across the full project lifecycle.

Delivery and Quality Control

• Monitor construction progress against design specifications, codes, and standards.
• Oversee quality control, health and safety, and change management processes throughout the build.
• Ensure all permitting, inspections, and regulatory requirements are met on schedule.

Commissioning and Handover

• Coordinate commissioning and integration of electrical, mechanical, and IT systems.
• Track and report on project milestones, deliverables, and risk factors.
• Manage financial tracking, budget adherence, and cost optimization across the project.
• Ensure project documentation, closeout reports, and handover to operations are completed to standard.

Requirements

Technical Skills

• 8 or more years of project management experience in data center, semiconductor, or comparable high-precision, high-availability construction environments — this is a hard requirement, not a preference.
• Proven experience managing large-scale construction projects with significant mechanical and electrical complexity.
• Experience working with Japanese contractor or EPC firms is required given the contractor ecosystem in Thailand’s Eastern Economic Corridor.
• Strong working knowledge of MS Project, Primavera P6, AutoCAD or Revit, and BIM tools.
• PMP or equivalent certification is preferred.
• Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, or a related field.
• English required. Thai strongly preferred for site-level coordination and local authority engagement.

Soft Skills

• Explains their own project experience with enough technical specificity to be assessed on it, not just described in general terms.
• Leads multi-contractor teams with the authority to resolve conflicts and keep schedule without escalating every issue upward.
• Manages competing project priorities in a fast-paced, high-stakes construction environment without losing quality discipline.

Nice to Have

• Experience with hyperscale or colocation data center construction specifically.
• Understanding of IT, networking, and cabling requirements in data center environments.
• Experience managing multiple concurrent projects in parallel.

DayOne is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

If you're ready to grow with one of the fastest-moving companies in the data center industry, apply now and be part of our global journey.

title: Patient Service Representative
description:
Job Description:

The Patient Service Representative (PSR) serves as the first connection between Intermountain and patients. This role embodies Intermountain values and focuses on establishing collaborative relationships with patients and fellow caregivers to deliver the highest level of customer/patient satisfaction. The PSR ensures a superior customer experience by identifying and resolving patient needs related to patient intake and care, which may include greeting and checking-in/out patients, as well as verifying information supplied by patients.

Essential Functions.

  • Provides courteous and professional connections with patients over the phone, in person or via secure messaging. Resolves patient needs skills to ensure a superior customer experience by identifying and resolving patient needs related to patient intake and care.
  • Documents all phone calls accurately and completely in the electronic medical record (EMR).
  • Schedules patient appointments for visits, procedures, diagnostic tests, referrals, and/or consultations.
  • Registers patients over the phone or in person by confirming, entering, and/or updating all required demographic data on patient and guarantor on the registration system. Follows procedures when identifying patients.
  • Obtains copies of insurance cards, forms of ID, and signatures on all required forms. May verify information on appropriate accounts to determine insurance coordination of benefits, may include pre-certification/prior authorization .
  • Assists patients in completing necessary forms to meet regulatory and billing needs prior to receiving clinical care. Scans necessary paperwork and educates patient on financial assistance. Proactively requests payments from patients on current and past medical services. Receives and processes those payments following appropriate procedures for handling payments.
  • Stays current on role/responsibilities, updates etc. which may include reviewing monthly email/newsletter, ambulatory epic dashboard, patient access, work ques, attend clinic/service line meetings, review emails each shift, etc. to ensure the highest standard of performance is achieved.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Six months of customer service experience involving interactions with customers.
  • Demonstrated basic computer skills involving word processing and data entry.
  • Professional manner and strong interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with patients and fellow caregivers to deliver the highest level of customer/patient satisfaction.
  • Ability to protect privacy, confidentiality, and Protected Health Information (PHI) of patients, members, and caregivers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • One year of customer service experience involving interactions with customers in person and by phone.
  • Billing and collections experience.
  • Computer literacy in using electronic medical records (EMR) systems and other relevant software.
  • High school diploma or GED preferred.
  • Multilingual

Physical Requirements

  • Ongoing need for caregivers to see and read information, labels, documents, monitors, identify equipment and supplies, and be able to assess customer needs.
  • Frequent interactions with providers, colleagues, customers, patients/clients and visitors require employee to verbally communicate as well as hear and understand spoken information, needs, and issues quickly and accurately.
  • Manual dexterity of hands and fingers to manipulate complex and delicate supplies and equipment with precision and accuracy. This includes frequent computer use for typing, accessing needed information, etc.
  • Position may require standing for long periods of time, lifting supplies
  • May assist patients into/out of the clinic.

title: Senior Credit Quantitative Specialist
description:
Let's Write Africa's Story Together!

Old Mutual is a firm believer in the African opportunity and our diverse talent reflects this.

Job Description

The Senior Credit Quantitative Specialist is GCI's senior technical specialist responsible for the ownership, governance and application of credit risk modelling across OMLACSA shareholder credit exposures. The role leads quantitative analysis of investment credit transactions, modelling of retail and investment credit exposures, consolidated portfolio risk assessment and management interpretation to support investment, capital and risk decisions. It also supports implementation of related systems and is responsible for validation of GCI-owned credit models.

The incumbent is accountable for the effective operation and ongoing suitability of GCI's credit risk modelling framework, including approved model applications, transaction analysis, modelling of shareholder credit exposures in Moody’s RiskFrontier, portfolio aggregation, stress testing and management interpretation. This requires deep theoretical knowledge and practical quantitative expertise to understand model construction, interrogate methodologies, data and outputs, and identify limitations or unsupported judgements.

The role additionally performs validation of GCI-owned credit models, covering risk-based scoping, testing, reporting, governance engagement and remediation follow-up. Model owners remain accountable for model development, implementation, monitoring and remediation.

The role is GCI's primary subject matter expert on credit risk modelling and portfolio analytics, engaging with investment teams, relevant business units, Group Risk, Group Actuarial, Finance and technology stakeholders. For its validation mandate, the role engages with model owners, developers, Internal Audit and the Models & Methods Committee.


Key Result Areas:


Credit Risk Modelling and Investment Portfolio Support


  • Own GCI's credit risk modelling framework, including its methodology inventory, approved applications, data requirements, operating controls, documentation and ongoing fitness for purpose.
  • Assess whether model performance, portfolio changes, new risks or changes in use require model recalibration, enhancement, redevelopment or replacement, and refer the required work to the accountable model owner or developer for action.
  • Apply approved models within GCI's risk modelling software to proposed investment credit transactions, producing quantitative analysis to support credit assessment, pricing, structuring, risk-adjusted return analysis, capital assessment and investment decision-making.
  • Use retail credit exposure data owned and provided by the relevant business units, together with investment credit exposure data, to model shareholder credit exposures in Moody’s RiskFrontier and produce a coherent, consolidated view of credit risk across OMLACSA portfolios.
  • Interpret model outputs, portfolio concentrations, capital consumption, risk-adjusted returns and emerging risk trends for management and governance forums.
  • Execute the ORSA credit stress scenarios, assess the impact on GCI’s investment credit exposures, and provide management with clear interpretation of the results, key drivers, assumptions and limitations.

Credit Model Validation

  • Plan and execute risk-based validations of GCI-owned credit models.
  • Assess conceptual soundness, assumptions, data, implementation, controls and fitness for use.
  • Document independent conclusions, limitations, conditions of use and required remediation.
  • Report material findings to governance forums and monitor remediation to closure.

Systems Development and Implementation Support

  • Support the design and development of GCI systems, tools and data solutions by translating quantitative, model risk and control requirements into clear functional and technical requirements.
    • Engage with business users, model owners, developers, data teams and technology stakeholders throughout requirements definition, solution design, testing, implementation and post-implementation review.
    • Review system designs, data flows, calculations, interfaces and controls to assess whether approved methodologies and validation requirements have been implemented accurately and are auditable.

  • Measurable Role Outcomes
    • Maintain an effective, well-governed GCI credit risk modelling framework that remains fit for purpose and supports timely management decisions.
    • Deliver accurate, timely and decision-useful quantitative analysis of investment credit transactions, supported by appropriate checks, reconciliations and transparent documentation.
    • Produce reliable and timely Moody’s RiskFrontier outputs that provide a consolidated view of credit risk across OMLACSA portfolios, subject to the quality and completeness of data supplied by the relevant business units.
    • Execute approved ORSA credit stresses within agreed timelines and provide clear management interpretation of results, key drivers, assumptions and limitations.
    • Deliver agreed quantitative, model risk and control requirements for systems initiatives and support successful testing and implementation.
    • Complete the approved validation plan for GCI-owned credit models within agreed timelines and quality standards.
    • Issue clear validation findings and monitor remediation to timely closure, escalating overdue or inadequately addressed matters through the appropriate governance forums.

Qualifications and Experience Required

  • Honours or Masters degree in Actuarial Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Quantitative Finance, Financial Engineering, Econometrics, Operations Research or Engineering.

  • Minimum of 8–12 years' experience in quantitative credit analysis, portfolio and capital modelling, structured credit, model application, model development, model validation or related fields. Prior model-development experience is advantageous because it provides the practical depth required to understand and challenge existing models.

  • Strong experience applying quantitative models to investment transactions and analysing retail, corporate, structured and portfolio-level credit exposures, including cash-flow analysis, stress testing, risk-adjusted returns, economic capital, exposure aggregation and concentration risk.

  • Experience using Moody’s RiskFrontier or a comparable credit portfolio modelling and economic capital platform will be advantageous.

  • Advanced Excel capability and practical proficiency in Python, SQL or comparable quantitative data-analysis tools will be advantageous.

  • Experience supporting systems development or transformation initiatives involving quantitative models, data integration, requirements definition, testing, reconciliation, implementation assurance or risk reporting is strongly preferred.

  • Experience independently validating quantitative credit models and presenting material findings through formal governance processes is preferred.


Competencies


  • Strong quantitative and credit risk modelling expertise.

  • Commercially relevant interpretation of model outputs.

  • Sound independent judgement and professional scepticism.

  • Constructive, evidence-based technical challenge.

  • Consistent modelling and validation governance discipline.

  • Clear communication of complex analysis and risk implications.

  • Effective prioritisation and reliable delivery.

  • Effective stakeholder engagement and management of validation independence.

Skills

Adaptive Thinking, Change Management, Data Compilation, Engineering Standards, Executing Plans, Legal Practices, Managerial Accounting, Numerical Aptitude, Policies & Procedures, Policy Development, Portfolio Management

Competencies

Builds Effective Teams

Business Insight

Collaborates

Communicates Effectively

Drives Results

Drives Vision and Purpose

Ensures Accountability

Financial Acumen

Every day, millions of people live without clean water, decent toilets and good hygiene. WaterAid exists to change that – for everyone, everywhere. Join us, and your energy will help unlock people’s potential and create a fairer future.

About WaterAid

We’re a global federation driven by one vision: a world where everyone, everywhere has clean water, sanitation and hygiene by 2030. Powered by our values of Respect, Accountability, Courage, Collaboration, Integrity and Innovation, we work alongside communities, partners and supporters to make change happen.

About the team

This position will be based in WaterAid’s Global Policy and Research Team (part of the Global Policy & Campaigns Department, GPAC) and will report to the Head of Policy – WASH and Public Health. The Policy and Research Team plays a lead role across the WaterAid Federation in setting WaterAid’s policy change agenda.

About the role

As our Policy Analyst Health, you will develop innovative policy research and evidence solutions and products to inform WaterAid's advocacy strategies and campaigns relevant to health and act as the lead on thematic health portfolio areas. You will work closely with colleagues in the health global health sector and across WaterAid to deliver our strategic aim on Prioritising WASH for public health and to drive sustainable change.

In this role, you will:

Support the development and implementation of research, policy and lobbying on health as part of the health policy and advocacy work (60%):

  • Conduct policy analysis, commission research, critically analyse the policy landscape and identify key decision-maker targets.
  • Identify policy changes and strategies on health that will deliver a step change in the political profile of WASH in healthcare settings. Write briefings and reports and influence key decision-maker targets to deliver these changes. .
  • Build influential relationships with technical decision-makers and develop and maintain a network of influential allies.

Provide policy advice and support to country programmes (20%):

  • Incorporate learning, research and policy analysis from our country programmes (CPs) into our global work and provide policy analysis, advice and support to country programme staff

Provide general policy advice, coordination, reporting and logistics support (20%):

  • Research, writing and policy briefings on general climate and WASH issues. Organise meetings, support reporting processes and coordination and logistics

To be successful, you will need:

  • Well-developed understanding of the role of different advocacy tactics in bringing about change and experience of working on public policy and/or advocacy on issues related to health and WASH, especially in Africa or Asia. Strong understanding of the impact of WASH on health and the relationship to people in poverty, particularly women and girls
  • Good political economy, analytical and research skills and ability to implement impactful research and policy influencing strategies and to monitor a complex internal and external context and advise on what tactics will be most effective and impactful
  • Experience of working with networks and coalitions to progress a compelling change agenda and ability to build impactful relationships with decision makers and partners
  • Well-developed verbal and written skills in English with proven experience of authoring high-impact policy briefs and ability to work and communicate effectively with and across key internal stakeholders across different geographies
  • Project management and organisational skills Strong IT skills in Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint
  • Commitment to WaterAid’s values and a working style that reflects these. Willingness and ability to travel internationally to fulfil requirements of the role

Although not essential, we’d prefer you to have:

  • Experience of working on gender and women’s health and empowerment or health financing or infectious diseases – such as cholera and AMR.

  • Fluency in European, African or Asian languages

title: Senior Associate Valuations Control
description:

Job Description


Job Summary:**

The Senior Associate Valuations Control will play a crucial role in ensuring the accuracy and integrity of valuations for a variety of financial instruments. This position involves performing independent price verification, reconciling valuations, and supporting the overall valuation control framework.

---

Job Responsibilities:**

* Perform independent price verification (IPV) on a diverse range of financial instruments, including but not limited to fixed income, equities, derivatives, and alternative investments.

* Participate in special projects and ad-hoc analysis as required by management.

---

Job Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related quantitative field. Master's degree or professional certifications (e.g., CFA, FRM) are highly desirable.
* 4-7 years of experience in valuation control, product control, or a similar role within the financial services industry, preferably with exposure to a variety of asset classes.
* Strong understanding of financial instruments, valuation techniques, and market conventions.
* Proficiency in financial modeling and strong analytical skills with meticulous attention to detail.
* Advanced Excel skills are essential; experience with VBA, SQL, Python, or other programming languages is a plus.

* Excellent communication (written and verbal) and interpersonal skills, with the ability to articulate complex concepts clearly.
* Ability to work effectively under pressure, manage multiple priorities, and meet tight deadlines.
* A proactive and inquisitive mindset, with a strong commitment to accuracy and data integrity

title: Research Assistant, FACE Lab
description:
Join our community and experience Emerson College!

We are hiring a Research Assistant for an NIH-funded project at the FACE Lab at Emerson College. The project’s aims are to identify language and communication markers that can predict conversational success and satisfaction among autistic and non-autistic adolescents. The Research Assistant will report to the FACE Lab Director and will support day-to-day operations of the project, including interactions with our partners on this grant at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) and the University of Connecticut (UConn). The primary research focus at the FACE Lab will be data collection in online (Zoom) conversations between autistic and non-autistic adolescents. The RA will acquire expertise in several software programs, including ELAN, manage student research assistants, and support all aspects of data collection and processing. The RA will provide a full range of administrative, logistical, and scheduling support to the Lab Director and Post-Doctoral Fellow, as well as coordinate activities and communication with our partners at CHOP and UConn. This is an important role that requires high organizational ability, strong communication and technological skills, as well as a high level of emotional intelligence. Minimum commitment is two years. This is a grant-funded position. Future commitments beyond the initial two years are contingent on continuation of grant funding.

The FACE Lab is a small, collegial environment dedicated to engaging in high quality, relevant, and ecologically valid research on social communication through respectful, honest, and open communication. We aim to collaborate with and be informed by the autism and autism research communities and remain accountable to all stakeholders, including providing active mentorship and growth opportunities to all lab members.

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES

  • Lead recruitment and data collection with autistic and non-autistic individuals and their families. Certified training in human subjects research regulations is provided by the College.
  • Participate in regular meetings between FACE Lab and partner labs at CHOP and UConn to provide status updates and adjust priority list of research tasks.
  • Implement data processing methods, priorities, and timelines established by the research team.
  • Create online surveys, implement data processing or exporting pipelines, and create associated documentation.
  • Organize and maintain data, IRB protocols, backup systems, and documentation
  • Supervise and coordinate the work of student research assistants and maintain the lab schedule.
  • Provide general administrative support for project.
  • Growth opportunities in writing abstracts and presenting research at conferences.
  • Perform other miscellaneous duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS – Qualifications are deemed required or preferred and represent what is needed to effectively perform job.

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Psychology, Child Development, Cognitive Science, Communication Disorders, or a related field required
  • Experience using statistical and other research software, such as R/R Studio, Redcap, and Qualtrics or QuestionPro strongly preferred
  • 1-3 years of previous experience working with children with autism or other developmental disorders strongly preferred

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES – May be representative, but not all-inclusive, of those knowledge, skills, and abilities commonly associated with the job.

  • High level of emotional intelligence and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team
  • Self-starter with excellent interpersonal communication and organizational skills
  • Exceptional accuracy and attention to detail, as well as strong communication skills required

PHYSICAL ABILITIES – Activities commonly associated with the performance of the functions of this job. The physical demands described below are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

  • This position is generally sedentary in nature, movement throughout the area is required from time to time.
  • Ability to have continuous oral and written communication with co-workers and supervisors is essential.
  • Repetitive movements, occasional lifting of up to 10 pounds, reaching, lifting, stooping and the ability to read a computer screen, detect color-coding and read fine print will be expected.

WORK ENVIRONMENT – Environmental or atmospheric conditions commonly associated with the performance of the functions of this job.
