title: Manager, Product Development
description:
Job Description Summary:

The Manager, Product Development/Management is responsible for leading product innovation, portfolio growth, and business performance within the Lash, Brow, and Lash/Brow Care categories. This role oversees the development and commercialization of new products, manages category and retailer strategies, and drives portfolio planning to support long-term business objectives.
The Manager leads a team of Product Development professionals and is accountable for product lifecycle management, retailer planning, cost optimization, commercialization execution, and strategic business planning. Working closely with Marketing, Creative, Sales, Supply Chain, R&D, Packaging, Regulatory, Quality Assurance, Finance, and external manufacturing partners, this position develops and executes product strategies that support profitable growth and strengthen retailer partnerships. The role also owns category roadmaps, innovation pipelines, and 3-year business planning initiatives aligned with organizational objectives.

Job Description:

Product Development, Portfolio & Innovation Leadership

• Lead the development and commercialization of new products within the Lash, Brow, and Lash/Brow Care categories.

• Own category innovation roadmaps and product portfolios to support long-term growth objectives.

• Manage product lifecycle strategies, including new launches, portfolio optimization, product refreshes, line extensions, phase-outs, and discontinuations.

• Establish annual innovation priorities and align development resources to support business objectives.

• Oversee multiple development projects and ensure timely execution across the product pipeline.

Business Planning & Cost Management

• Develop and manage annual business plans and 3-year category growth strategies.

• Create long-range innovation roadmaps, category expansion plans, and portfolio architecture strategies.

• Lead product profitability initiatives through pricing optimization, cost-reduction programs, sourcing improvements, and operational efficiencies.

• Monitor business performance, margins, forecasts, inventory risks, and operating costs.

• Partner with Finance, Supply Chain, and Operations teams to improve profitability and support business targets.

• Identify opportunities to improve product cost structures through supplier negotiations, packaging improvements, product engineering, and process improvements.

Retailer & Channel Business Management

• Own product planning and business management across multiple retailer accounts and distribution channels.

• Develop retailer-specific assortment strategies, innovation recommendations, and category growth plans.

• Lead retailer line reviews, product presentations, innovation discussions, and annual planning meetings.

• Partner with Sales leadership to identify growth opportunities and develop retailer-specific business strategies.

• Serve as the primary product-management representative for key retailer initiatives and strategic partnerships.

Team Leadership & Talent Development

• Directly manage Product Assistants, Product Specialists, and Assistant Managers as assigned.

• Establish team goals, priorities, workload allocation, and performance expectations.

• Coach, mentor, and develop team members to strengthen product-development and business-management capabilities.

• Lead onboarding, training, career development, and succession-planning activities.

• Foster a collaborative culture focused on innovation, accountability, continuous improvement, and business results.

Commercialization, Marketing & Cross-Functional Leadership (10%)

• Lead commercialization planning in partnership with Marketing, Creative, Sales, Retail Engagement, and Supply Chain teams.

• Review and approve product positioning, claims, launch strategies, selling stories, and marketing support plans.

• Ensure alignment between product strategy, retailer objectives, marketing execution, and commercial goals.

• Present category strategies, innovation pipelines, business updates, and growth recommendations to senior leadership.

• Drive cross-functional alignment to ensure successful product launches and retailer execution.

Vendor & Technical Development Oversight (5%)

title: Software Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
description:
Cohesity is the leader in AI-powered data security. Over 13,600 enterprise customers, including over 85 of the Fortune 100 and nearly 70% of the Global 500, rely on Cohesity to strengthen their resilience while providing Gen AI insights into their vast amounts of data. Formed from the combination of Cohesity with Veritas’ enterprise data protection business, the company’s solutions secure and protect data on-premises, in the cloud, and at the edge. Backed by NVIDIA, IBM, HPE, Cisco, AWS, Google Cloud, and others, Cohesity is headquartered in Santa Clara, CA, with offices around the globe.

We’ve been named a Leader by multiple analyst firms and have been globally recognized for Innovation, Product Strength, and Simplicity in Design , and our culture.

Want to join the leader in AI-powered data security?




ABOUT THE INTERNSHIP

At Cohesity, interns do more than observe. They build.


As a Software Engineering Intern, you'll join a highly collaborative engineering team working on products that protect and manage exabytes of customer data worldwide. From day one, you'll contribute to meaningful technical projects that directly impact production systems used by some of the world's largest organizations.


You'll collaborate with engineers, technical leaders, and mentors to design, develop, test, and deliver scalable solutions across our cloud, platform, infrastructure, security, and data management products while gaining hands-on experience with modern distributed systems, cloud-native technologies, and the full software development lifecycle.


HOW YOU'LL SPEND YOUR TIME HERE:

  • Design, develop, test, and deploy software components that support Cohesity's enterprise data security and management platform
  • Contribute to production-quality code using modern engineering best practices
  • Collaborate with engineers, product managers, and architects to solve complex technical challenges
  • Work on large-scale distributed systems, cloud-native services, storage technologies, cybersecurity solutions, or platform infrastructure
  • Participate in code reviews, design discussions, sprint planning, and technical brainstorming sessions
  • Analyze system performance and help improve scalability, reliability, and operational efficiency
  • Build tooling, automation, or product features that create measurable impact for customers
  • Present your final project and accomplishments to engineering leaders and executives at the conclusion of the internship

WE'D LOVE TO TALK TO YOU IF YOU HAVE MANY OF THE FOLLOWING:

  • Currently pursuing a BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical discipline
  • Expected graduation date between December 2027 and June 2028
  • Strong foundation in computer science fundamentals, including Data Structures, Algorithms, and Systems Design
  • Experience developing software through coursework, research, internships, open-source contributions, or personal projects
  • Proficiency in one or more programming languages such as C++, Go, Java, or Python
  • Familiarity with software development tools, version control systems, and Linux/Unix environments
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills
  • Intellectual curiosity, passion for technology, and enthusiasm for solving complex technical challenges

WE ARE EXTRA EXCITED IF YOU HAVE ANY OF THE FOLLOWING:

  • Coursework, project experience, or exposure to one or more of the following areas:
  • Distributed systems and large-scale software architecture
  • Networking, systems programming, or operating systems
  • Concurrent or asynchronous programming
  • Cloud computing and containerized environments
  • Data security, cryptography, ransomware protection, or secure coding practices
  • Experience with technologies such as AWS, Azure, GCP, Docker, Kubernetes, TensorFlow, PyTorch, or similar tools
  • Participation in research projects, hackathons, open-source contributions, technical clubs, or previous internships
  • Exposure to artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, or emerging technologies through coursework, research, internships, or personal projects

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN:

  • How production-scale distributed systems are designed and operated
  • Modern software engineering best practices and development workflows
  • How cloud-native technologies power enterprise software platforms
  • How cross-functional engineering teams collaborate to deliver products used by global customers
  • How AI and cybersecurity are shaping the future of data protection

TEAM MATCHING

Software Engineering Interns are hired into a general talent pool and matched with a team during the recruitment process. Opportunities may span areas such as cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, data management, cybersecurity, storage systems, platform engineering, and emerging technologies.

We'll consider your interests, experience, and technical strengths as we work to identify the best fit for both you and the overall team.


CAREER GROWTH OPPORTUNITIES

High-performing interns may be considered for full-time new graduate positions upon graduation. You'll gain exposure to Cohesity's engineering culture, mentorship from experienced technical leaders, and a strong foundation for a career in software engineering.

title: Principal Software Engineer — Commerce, Payments & Connected Platforms, Agentic AI
description: Overview Who We Are: Ever wonder who brings the entertainment to your flights? Panasonic Avionics Corporation is #1 in the industry for delivering inflight products such as movies, games, Wi-Fi, and now Bluetooth headphone connectivity! How exciting would it be to be a part of the innovation that goes into creating technology that delights millions of people in an industry that’s here to stay! With our company’s history spanning over 40 years, you will have stability, career growth opportunities, and will work with the brightest minds in the industry. If you want to learn more about us, visit us at www.panasonic.aero. And for a full listing of open job opportunities go to https://careers.na.panasonic.com/avionics/jobs. The Avionics Way: The Avionics Way captures the essence of what makes our employees special, and by extension, our organization. It’s comprised of 5 core identifiers - Pioneers, Problem Solvers, Accountable, Collaborative, and Customer Focused - that together form a robust, working framework for our continued success. Beyond a philosophy, the Avionics Way is our guide to daily practices. It provides a clear, actionable model to help employees, at all levels, realize their ambitions through outsized contributions to their teams and the company. This model clearly defines expectations for performance at all levels of the organization, as well as establishes specific actions and modes of working that reinforce our philosophy on the path to achieving our goals. Responsibilities We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer to define the technical direction for platforms that connect e-commerce, payments, and data across cloud services and connected hardware. You will solve complex engineering problems spanning digital experiences, distributed transactions, device integration, and environments with intermittent connectivity. This is a senior individual contributor role with influence across multiple engineering teams. You will combine architectural leadership with hands-on engineering, turn ambiguous business needs into clear technical strategies, and raise the quality of systems delivered to customers. You will also guide practical applications of agentic AI to improve engineering productivity, operational reliability, and customer experiences. What you will do: Set technical direction. Own the architecture and technical roadmap across commerce, payments, and connected platforms. Align teams around clear system boundaries, interfaces, and engineering standards. Build reliable commerce and payment systems. Guide the design of catalog, pricing, checkout, order management, payment orchestration, and reconciliation capabilities, with strong attention to transaction correctness, security, and failure recovery. Connect hardware and software. Design cloud-to-device workflows that account for constrained compute, intermittent connectivity, software and firmware compatibility, remote configuration, and fleet observability. Establish trusted data foundations. Define event models, data contracts, and pipelines that support operational intelligence, analytics, personalization, and traceability across customer and transaction journeys. Engineer for real-world conditions. Address offline operation, synchronization, retries, duplicate events, partial failures, and recovery across cloud and edge environments. Make quality an engineering responsibility. Establish measurable reliability and performance targets, automated validation, representative integration testing, and release readiness criteria. Partner with teams to reduce escaped defects and improve detection and recovery. Apply agentic AI with measurable value. Identify and deliver focused use cases such as test generation, incident investigation, and operational assistance. Establish evaluations, permission boundaries, human oversight, and auditability appropriate to each use case. Lead through implementation. Build prototypes, contribute production code, review critical designs, and resolve the most difficult technical problems. Multiply engineering effectiveness. Mentor senior and staff engineers, develop technical leaders, and drive decisions across organizational boundaries through clear reasoning and evidence. Connect technical choices to business outcomes. Communicate tradeoffs involving customer experience, delivery speed, reliability, cost, and long-term maintainability. The salary range of $171,000 - $268,000 is just one component of Panasonic’s total package. The final offer amount may vary based on factors including but not limited to individual’s knowledge, skills, experience, and location. Base pay offered may vary depending on skills, experience, job-related knowledge and location. Qualifications What we are looking for: Basic qualifications Significant experience building and operating production software systems, typically 12+ years, including technical leadership across multiple teams or major platform initiatives. Demonstrated ability to define architecture, lead adoption, and remain accountable for production outcomes. Deep expertise in distributed systems, APIs, event-driven architectures, data modeling, and cloud platforms. Strong experience in commerce or payments, with a working understanding of transaction lifecycles, consistency, idempotency, and reconciliation. Experience integrating software with connected devices, embedded platforms, or other hardware-dependent systems. Strong programming skills in one or more production languages, such as Java, Kotlin, Go, Python, C++, or TypeScript. Experience improving reliability through observability, performance engineering, automated testing, and incident analysis. Ability to influence without direct authority, navigate ambiguity, and communicate clearly with engineering, product, operations, and business leaders. Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Preferred qualifications Experience with payment gateways, processors, tokenization, fraud controls, and systems operating within PCI DSS scope. Experience with edge computing, offline transaction workflows, device telemetry, remote software updates, or large connected-device fleets. Experience designing data platforms that support analytics, experimentation, personalization, or machine learning. Practical experience building LLM-powered applications or agentic workflows, including tool integration, evaluation, and production monitoring. Experience in travel, aviation, mobility, retail, or other environments where digital services depend on physical infrastructure. A track record of simplifying complex platforms and delivering incremental modernization without disrupting customers. What success looks like Teams execute against a clear technical strategy with well-defined ownership and interfaces. Commerce and payment journeys remain correct and reliable under real-world connectivity and device constraints. Releases demonstrate measurable improvements in quality, performance, and operational readiness. Data is trustworthy and usable across engineering, product, and operations. title: Content Strategy & Governance Manager, Customer Experience Center
description:
Job Description Summary

The Content Strategy & Governance Manager is the storytelling architect of the CEC. You will own the planning, creation, governance and lifecycle of every content experience in the center, so that each visit delivers one unified enterprise narrative that is accurate, compelling, compliant and tailored to the customer in the room.

You will be the strategic integrator between clinical subject matter experts, product teams, sales leadership, creative agencies and regulatory stakeholders, orchestrating input from 200+ SMEs and governing 130+ net-new content modules and interactive experiences across care pathways, modalities, software, AI and services.

Job Description

Position Summary

GE HealthCare is creating a 30,000-square-foot Customer Experience Center (CEC) flagship at its Waukesha campus, targeted to open in September 2027. The CEC will bring the full enterprise portfolio to life through care pathways, clinical workflows, multimodality solutions, digital and AI capabilities, software, services and lifecycle value. It is a strategic account platform, not a product showroom: a place where health system leaders experience what GE HealthCare can do for their patients, clinicians and business.


The Content Strategy & Governance Manager is the storytelling architect of the CEC. You will own the planning, creation, governance and lifecycle of every content experience in the center, so that each visit delivers one unified enterprise narrative that is accurate, compelling, compliant and tailored to the customer in the room.


You will be the strategic integrator between clinical subject matter experts, product teams, sales leadership, creative agencies and regulatory stakeholders, orchestrating input from 200+ SMEs and governing 130+ net-new content modules and interactive experiences across care pathways, modalities, software, AI and services.


Why This Role Matters

  • Enterprise narrative made real. The CEC is the physical proof point for GE HealthCare’s shift from product-led communications to outcomes-based, care-pathway storytelling across Advanced Imaging Solutions, Patient Care Solutions (PCS), Pharmaceuticals Diagnosis Product (PDx), Services and Software Solutions.
  • Direct commercial impact. Executive briefing environments are among the highest-converting assets in B2B healthcare selling. The CEC will be measured on influenced pipeline, deal velocity, win rate and customer satisfaction.
  • Built from day one. You join the founding team alongside the Senior Director, shaping how the center works before its doors open, not inheriting someone else’s playbook.
  • One enterprise, one room. The CEC is one of the few places where every business unit shows up together, as one enterprise offering, in front of the customer.

Scope and Working Relationships

  • Team: Founding member of a CEC team of ~7 at opening, growing to 14 roles at full scale. Partners daily with the Journey Consultants and Briefing Manager; future Content Creation Lead expected to join the content function.
  • Content scope: Lobby, Journey Hub, theater, care pathways (Oncology, Neurology, Cardiology), Cloud/AI/Software, Services & Lifecycle and PDx experiences.
  • Key partners: Segment and Product Marketing, Clinical and Medical Affairs, Sales and Strategic Accounts, Brand, Legal/Regulatory, Digital, and experiential design and content agencies.

Phase 1 — Pre-Opening: January through September 2027

The mandate is to bring the CEC’s content and narratives to launch, approved, modular and ready to personalize.


Content Architecture and Strategy

  • Define and implement the CEC content architecture, aligned to GE HealthCare’s enterprise narrative and care pathway strategy.
  • Build the framework for how products, software, services and AI-enabled capabilities come together in cohesive customer journeys.
  • Set the standards for how content is structured, tagged, maintained and evolved, with modular "shelf" content designed for reuse.

SME Orchestration and Launch Content

  • Orchestrate clinical, product and segment SMEs to finalize care pathway narratives, interactives and launch content with the experience design agency.
  • Ensure content reflects accurate clinical, product and market positioning; own the logic that connects product capabilities to clinical outcomes and health system challenges.
  • Validate content in the physical space during installation, testing and dry-run visits.

Governance and Approvals

  • Lead regulatory, legal, brand and compliance validation workflows; manage approvals through established review systems.
  • Establish content lifecycle governance: versioning, refresh cadence, retirement and CMS administration.

Phase 2 — Post-Opening: September 2027 Forward

The mandate shifts to personalizing every visit and keeping the CEC current.


Visit Personalization

  • Translate each visit’s objectives into a customized content journey, assembling roughly 60–70% approved shelf content with 30–40% personalized for the account visit.
  • Join discovery and pre-visit planning calls with Sales, the Briefing Team and Journey Consultants; tailor content and presentations for executive audiences.
  • Serve as ongoing content steward and agenda architect for the CEC.

Continuous Improvement

  • Use post-visit surveys, debriefs and engagement data to measure which content resonates; refresh or retire what does not.
  • Introduce new narratives and experiences as the portfolio and launch calendar evolve, with Marketing, Product and Clinical teams.
  • Develop reusable modular content that also supports broader sales enablement.

How Success Will Be Measured

  • Launch readiness: all CEC experiences approved and live for opening.
  • Content reuse: share of each visit built from approved shelf content, and turnaround time for personalized content.
  • Quality and compliance: approval cycle time and zero compliance issues in customer-facing content.
  • Customer impact: content-related CSAT and feedback, and content performance by care pathway.

Qualifications


Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in healthcare, marketing, communications, life sciences or a related field.
  • 8+ years of experience in healthcare content strategy, product marketing, clinical communications or related roles.
  • Experience with healthcare technologies, medical devices, digital health platforms or diagnostics.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex clinical or technical information into clear, compelling narratives.
  • Experience managing content governance and regulatory review workflows in a healthcare or regulated environment.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, including coordinating large stakeholder groups.
  • Strong writing, storytelling and presentation development skills.
  • Willingness to be based in the Milwaukee / Waukesha area with regular on-site presence.

Preferred

  • Experience supporting executive briefing centers, customer experience centers or strategic customer engagement programs.
  • Experience managing content for digital, interactive or immersive environments; familiarity with CMS and digital experience platforms.
  • Experience coordinating content development with external creative agencies.
  • Knowledge of healthcare care pathways and hospital operational workflows.

What We Value

  • Turns complexity into clarity without losing clinical credibility.
  • Builds governance that enables speed rather than slowing it down.
  • Brings many voices to one story, and holds the line on quality.

Quality and Compliance

  • Comply with GE HealthCare’s Quality Manual, Quality Management System and all applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Complete all required training within defined timelines.
  • Proactively identify, document and report any quality or compliance concerns.
  • Ensure all customer-facing content and demonstrations meet regulatory, clinical and legal approval requirements for each audience and geography.

We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job opening.



Additional Information

GE HealthCare offers a great work environment, professional development, challenging careers, and competitive compensation. GE HealthCare is an Equal Opportunity Employer. description:

About this opportunity:

Reporting to the Team Lead, Market Fundamentals and Pricing, this role provides short- and long-term energy market analysis to support commercial and strategic decision-making. The successful candidate will combine strong commodity market and pricing expertise with data-driven analysis to develop meaningful market insights, maintain forward price outlooks, and translate market views into practical recommendations. This role requires strong analytical and communication skills, a passion for energy markets, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment while leveraging data analysis and visualization tools to support business decisions.

What you’ll do:

  • Conduct short- and long-term market analysis to support commercial, strategic, and business development decisions.
  • Build and maintain supply and demand models across key regional hubs and commodities, including crude oil, natural gas, NGLs, and refined products.
  • Maintain the corporate price deck model and provide accurate, timely forward price estimates to key stakeholders.
  • Monitor North American and global commodity markets to develop independent perspectives on market trends, industry developments, commercial drivers, and risks.
  • Develop market insights and translate analysis into practical recommendations that support strategy, commercial activities, and business development initiatives.
  • Develop and enhance data analytics, automation, visualization, and supporting data infrastructure for commodity pricing, supply and demand balances, and other key market indicators.
  • Provide timely market intelligence, analysis, and clear presentations to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders, including Strategy, Planning, Commercial, Business Development, Trading, and Marketing.
  • Deliver ad hoc analysis to support business needs and evaluate the market backdrop, risks, opportunities, and commercial implications of strategic initiatives.

Who you are:

Our ideal candidate will have the following minimum requirements:

  • Legally authorized to work in Canada
  • Post-secondary degree in a quantitative or related field such as Statistics, Finance, Economics/Econometrics, Computer Science, Geophysics, or Engineering.
  • Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in commodity markets, with a strong understanding of market fundamentals and experience in crude oil, natural gas, and/or refined products analytics; advanced knowledge of natural gas markets is preferred.
  • Strong quantitative and analytical skills, with the ability to interpret complex market data and translate findings into meaningful insights.
  • Proficiency with data analysis and visualization tools such as Excel, Databricks, Power BI, Spotfire, RStudio, Python, or similar platforms.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively engage with a broad range of stakeholders and corporate professionals.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently, apply sound judgment, and learn new analytical tools and approaches.
  • Creative and solutions-focused mindset, with the ability to adapt and problem-solve in a dynamic and evolving market environment.

title: WPM Analyst or Senior Analyst
description:
We are looking for talented individuals who are passionate about making an impact in the company and the community. Apply now and become part of the dynamic energy industry!

Position Description:

Member of the Wholesale Power Marketing team that supports the Wholesale Marketing Department, SPP Markets+ and the Energy Imbalance Market, where you will leverage data analytics to drive operational excellence and market efficiency. In this role, you will be part of the Market’s Strategy and Analytics Team, performing quantitative analysis of market results, dispatch, forecasts and settlements, and maintaining the data, models and reporting behind SPP Markets+ optimization and system modeling. You will also analyze large, complex datasets to uncover patterns and insights, provide data-driven solutions to enhance market operations, and advance organizational processes through data management, including ETL operations and exploratory analysis. You will create and maintain comprehensive documentation for reporting and recurring analyses, and improve the efficiency and effectiveness of Wholesale Power Marketing operations through advanced data analytics and market insights.

Position-Related Responsibilities:

  • Performs quantitative and statistical analysis of market, dispatch, settlement and forecast data, including forecast-to-actual variance analysis, and communicates findings to WPM personnel and management.
  • Monitors and analyzes wholesale market performance and trends in SPP Markets+ and the WEIM, and provides analytical support for market working group and protocol reviews.
  • As part of the team, develops WPM wholesale market strategies, including LMP and price-spread analysis, bidding strategy evaluation, and assessment of market opportunities and risks, using quantitative analysis of market, dispatch and settlement data.
  • As part of the optimization team, validates model inputs and outputs, such as unit commitment, dispatch constraints, cost curves and transmission limits, against market rules and settlement results.
  • Builds and maintains data pipelines, data models and automated reporting that feed market analysis, forecasting and optimization tools (e.g., PCI front office suite, OATI, EMS data).
  • Develops analytical tools and scripts (Python, SQL) to automate recurring analyses and support troubleshooting of market systems.
  • Works with clients to develop and maintain current business process maps and documentation.
  • Supports metrics efforts for WPM, including data collection and validation, data presentation, and evaluation of results.
  • Facilitates the interaction between clients and technology providers (internal and external) to implement and maintain reliable solutions.
  • Works closely with technical resources and System Administrators as needed to troubleshoot problems or investigate proposed enhancements and determine solutions.
  • Documents problem analysis findings and corrective measures for ongoing support and audit purposes.
  • Performs other job-related duties as assigned by management.
  • Participates on project teams, assisting in requirements definition and process design while also ensuring that testing and training align with the defined requirements and processes to meet business area needs.
  • Identifies and defines opportunities and strategies to use information technology to simplify, integrate, and otherwise improve the organization’s business and workflow processes.
  • Drives creative solutions and helps business areas challenge their own assumptions of how they will successfully execute their plans.
  • Provides a point of contact for business area relationships. Establishes effective client relationships by developing trust, integrity, credibility, and reliability with each client/business area.

Position-Related Responsibilities specific to Senior Analyst:

All responsibilities of Analyst apply plus the following:

  • Gathers requirements from WPM business areas for moderate to complex enhancements and translates those requirements into functional designs used by technical resources to develop solutions.
  • Analyzes, documents and maps “As-Is” business processes. Prepares “To-Be” process maps, fit/gap analysis, change impact analysis, and/or other business process change related documentation.
  • Develops system, integration, and regression test plans. Leads system, integration, and regression testing activities. Includes validation of data feeds and optimization model outputs.
  • Develops and runs ad hoc query reports as needed to troubleshoot problems, fulfill audit requests, and support other client requests.
  • Proactively evaluates application functions and features against business processes to support current and evolving business practices.
  • Manages assigned tasks of large projects under the leadership of a Project Manager or Business Lead. Leads small projects, preparing all required documentation for delivery of project objectives, as assigned.
  • Performs detailed analysis of market outcomes and recommends improvements to models, forecasts and reporting.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

(Equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.)


Analyst - Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree or 4 years of experience in a related business area or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Effective communication skills, both verbal and written and proficiency in conducting productive meetings.
  • Effective critical listening, analysis and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to articulate thoughts and ideas to others, including facilitating communication between business and technical personnel.
  • Effective time management with demonstrated ability to multitask priorities and deliver assignments on schedule.
  • Strong analytical and conceptual skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and to effectively participate in a team project to achieve required functionality within budget and timeframe.
  • Ability to establish and maintain a high level of customer trust and confidence.
  • Ability to effectively adapt to rapidly changing technology and business.
  • Strong knowledge of applicable PC programs and O365 tools (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).
  • Responsible for individual projects under the oversight of a more senior analyst.
  • Assists in business process initiatives and continuous improvement efforts.
  • Demonstrates general understanding of one or more business areas and technology used in those areas.
  • Can serve as point of contact for several business areas.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Knowledge of the SPP Markets+, Energy Imbalance Market (WEIM) or other ISO/RTO type operations
  • Proficient with advanced Excel concepts
  • VBA, Power Query, PivotTables, VLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, etc
  • Microsoft Power BI
  • Data Visualization, Report design, DAX Functions, Measures, etc.
  • Python and basic data analysis packages Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn, skLearn, etc.
  • Database technologies and data manipulation
  • SQL Knowledge, Table Structures, Data Types, Stored Procedures, etc
  • Maintaining Complex Generation and Market Data Model/Data Pipeline
  • Quantitative methods: statistics, forecasting, regression and optimization concepts (e.g., linear/mixed-integer programming)
  • Knowledge of utility-scale and renewable generation and power market modeling

Senior - Minimum Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications for Analyst plus:

  • Superior analytical, relationship management, facilitation, project management, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to develop management style reporting and presentations (e.g., PowerPoint, Excel).
  • Demonstrated ability to work with all levels of management and workforce.
  • Project management skills including ability to multitask, prioritize, set and meet deadlines, work independently, and perform tasks with emphasis on accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Demonstrates deep understanding of at least a few business areas and technology used in those areas.
  • Successfully engages in multiple initiatives simultaneously.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5 years of utility experience in a related business area.
  • Working experience in SPP Markets+, the Energy Imbalance Market (WEIM) or other ISO/RTO operations, including analysis of market results, dispatch and settlements.
  • Advanced proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience building and maintaining automated data pipelines, data models and reporting (e.g., Power BI).
  • Hands-on experience with the PCI front office suite (GenTrader, Insights, Forecaster), OATI or similar energy market systems.
  • Applied experience with quantitative methods, including forecasting, regression and forecast-to-actual variance analysis, and validating optimization model inputs and outputs.

title: Sales Floor Dept Supervisor - Hardware-Tools
description:

All Lowe’s associates deliver quality customer service while maintaining a store that is clean, safe, and stocked with the products our customers need. As a Sales Floor Department Supervisor, this means:
• Providing resources and tools to support those directly helping customers provide the best service.
• Assisting with down stocking and area recovery as well as providing input into merchandising decisions.
• Monitoring use of store power equipment and coaching employees on safe behaviors and lifting techniques.
The Sales Floor Department Supervisor is primarily responsible for leading and enabling a team of associates to deliver the best possible customer experience in the store. This includes coaching and training associates, delegating, following-up on daily tasks, managing performance, and ensuring adequate department coverage. Sales Floor Department Supervisors are responsible for customer-facing activities (e.g., greeting customers, clarifying needs and identifying solutions, closing sales), non-customer-facing activities (e.g., down stocking, inventory management, area recovery) and store safety (e.g., conducting safety walks, reporting hazards, understanding safety and lifting directions).

The Sales Floor Department Supervisor works with his/her leaders to identify approaches and behaviors that best meet sales and service objectives, then communicates those best practices to the team in a way that inspires engaging, customer-focused behavior and goal attainment. Further, the Sales Floor Department Supervisor must supervise associates in other departments, as needed, to meet the demands of the store. This requires broad product knowledge and the ability to engage associates and customers across departments. It is important that this associate communicate upward to keep management informed of concerns, issues, praises, and morale.

title: Enterprise Regulatory Compliance Audit & Monitoring Program Admin I
description:
Job Description:

Summary:

The Enterprise Regulatory Compliance Program Administrator evaluates new and evolving federal and state regulatory guidance and assesses their impact on enterprise-wide business processes, products, and operational strategies. This role partners closely with functional business areas to translate complex regulatory guidance into practical risk-based compliance solutions and supports the ongoing administration of an effective regulatory compliance program.


The Administrator plays a key role in monitoring regulatory change, performing impact assessments, supporting audits and examinations, and advising business partners to ensure compliance with applicable requirements issued by regulatory and oversight agencies, including but not limited to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), New York State Department of Health (DOH), Department of Financial Services (DFS), Department of Labor (DOL), Office of Inspector General (OIG), and Office of the Medicaid Inspector General (OMIG).


Essential Accountabilities:


Level I

  • Supports oversight and execution of regulatory compliance activities for assigned business areas, including implementation, monitoring, and documentation of regulatory requirements within the Enterprise compliance framework. This may include system research and analysis and data gathering and evaluation through interactions with internal business area staff throughout the organization.
  • Responsible for interpreting federal and state regulatory guidance and responding to compliance-related inquiries, providing clear, practical guidance to business partners regarding company products, services, and operations.
  • Monitors changes in regulations both at the state and federal level which may affect the operations of the Health Plan and its subsidiaries. Assesses for any impact to programs, operational procedures, policies, and systems supporting the organization’s Medicare, Medicaid, Commercial, and retail market programs.
  • Collaborates with cross-functional teams including but not limited to Customer Service, Product and Operations, Marketing, Sales, Claims, Enrollment, Pharmacy, Quality Office, Utilization Management, and Advocacy to support regulatory compliance readiness and implementation, including gathering evidence of compliance.
  • Participates in regulatory risk assessments by identifying potential compliance vulnerabilities, assisting with root cause analysis, and supporting development of corrective actions and remediation plans.
  • Collaborates with assigned internal business areas to support adherence to regulatory compliance key performance indicators (KPIs) and related reporting and remediation when metrics are not met.
  • Contributes to and supports the development of compliance communication tools, training and monitoring activities to promote awareness and understanding of regulatory requirements.
  • Attends business and project meetings to proactively identify compliance considerations and mitigate regulatory risk.
  • Participates in Compliance Oversight Committees (COCs).
  • Assists in preparing accurate documentation, reports, and responses for regulatory filings, surveys, audits, and information requests.
  • Supports Federal, State, and accreditation audits and examinations.
  • Consistently demonstrates high standards of integrity by supporting the Lifetime Healthcare Companies’ mission and values, adhering to the Corporate Code of Conduct, and leading to the Lifetime Way values and beliefs.
  • Maintains high regard for member privacy in accordance with the corporate privacy policies and procedures.
  • Regular and reliable attendance is expected and required.
  • Performs other functions as assigned by management.


Level II (in addition to Level I Accountabilities)

  • Operates with increased autonomy and serves as subject matter expert and resource to operational areas regarding compliance, governance, and risk matters.
  • Independently coordinates and facilitates cross-functional work groups, when necessary, to support implementation of new or revised regulatory requirements.
  • Leads or co-leads regulatory change management initiatives, including communication planning, implementation tracking, and effectiveness monitoring.
  • Represents the organization on external calls with vendors, business partners, industry groups, or the BlueCross BlueShield Association, as applicable.
  • Support the coordination and oversight of audits or reviews conducted by third parties or external vendors.
  • Shares regulatory knowledge and best practices with peers and business partners.


Level III (in addition to Level II Accountabilities)

  • Manages highly complex, high-risk, or enterprise-wide regulatory compliance issues and provides expert guidance to senior leadership, stakeholders, and operational teams.
  • Serves as a key point of contact with regulatory agencies and represents the organization during regulatory discussions, audits, or examinations.
  • Represents leadership in Compliance committees, governance forums, and enterprise workgroups.
  • May lead or oversee internal audits or external regulatory audits, examinations, or corrective action efforts, including regulator engagement and response strategy.
  • Provides mentorship and guidance to less experienced team members and acts as a trusted advisor.
  • Contributes to the ongoing maturity and effectiveness of the enterprise compliance program.


Minimum Qualifications:


NOTE: We include multiple levels of classification differentiated by demonstrated knowledge, skills, and the ability to manage increasingly independent and/or complex assignments, broader responsibility, additional decision making, and in some cases, becoming a resource to others. In addition to using this differentiated approach to place new hires, it also provides guideposts for employee development and promotional opportunities.


Level I

  • Seven or more years’ experience in health insurance or health care delivery, or bachelor’s degree in related area with four or more years of related experience.
  • Working knowledge of federal and state health care regulatory frameworks affecting Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial products.
  • Extensive knowledge of regulatory initiatives and legislation that impacts the health insurance industry. Understanding of regulations and ability to administer compliance for all areas across an organization.
  • Familiarity with utilization management, authorization, and claims and enrollment processing workflows and systems.
  • Strong project coordination skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Demonstrated ability to conduct regulatory research, analyze guidance, and translate requirements into business-ready recommendations.
  • Strong research, analytical, and creative critical thinking skills. Capacity to identify and understand business objectives and associated risks of the operational area under review in order to make recommendations to improve the effectiveness or efficiency of regulatory operational processes.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills and ability to communicate regulatory concepts clearly to diverse audiences.
  • High degree of accountability, follow-through, and attention to detail.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and enterprise systems.


Level II (in addition to Level I Qualifications)

  • Nine or more years of relevant experience, or bachelor’s degree with six or more years of related experience.
  • Advanced knowledge of health insurance regulations and compliance program operations.
  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple complex regulatory initiatives or compliance projects.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgement and operate independently with minimal supervision.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and influence skills.


Level III (in addition to Level II Qualifications)

  • Eleven or more years of relevant experience, or bachelor’s degree with eight or more years of related experience.
  • Professional certification preferred (i.e., CPCO, CHC, CHPC, HCCA-related credentials).
  • Proven expertise in resolving highly complex regulatory compliance issues and projects and management of regulatory audits.
  • Ability to operate with the highest degree of initiative, leadership, and strategic thinking.
  • Recognized as a trusted compliance advisor across the organization.


Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to work prolonged periods sitting and/or standing at a workstation and working on a computer.
  • Ability to travel within the service region for meetings, audits, or trainings as needed.
  • Role requires extensive review, analysis, and interpretation of regulatory documentation.

description:
28800 Ida St Valley Nebraska 68064-8016

This internship offers hands-on experience across Analytics, Product Management, and Engineering, with opportunities to build reports and visualizations in Databricks, Power BI, and Excel while supporting data quality, governance, and automation initiatives.

The ideal candidate is curious, analytical, detail-oriented, and comfortable collaborating across technical and business teams.   • Strong understanding of enterprise infrastructure, cyber resilience, data security, cloud, and/or data management markets.

title: Associate Manager, AI Security Engineer
description:
SC Johnson has been leading with purpose for 140 years, building high-quality products and iconic brands found in homes, schools and businesses in virtually every country worldwide – including OFF!®, Raid®, Glade®, Windex®, Scrubbing Bubbles®, Ziploc®, Mrs. Meyer’s Clean Day®, method®, Autan®, Baygon®, Mr Muscle®, Duck®, Lysoform® and more.

The 13,000 people of our global, fifth-generation family company are committed to making the world a better place today and for future generations.

ABOUT THE ROLE
The Associate Manager, AI Security Engineer helps enable the rapid, responsible, and secure adoption of artificial intelligence across the business. This hands-on engineering and development opportunity is intended for an application, data, cloud, AI/ML, infrastructure, or cybersecurity professional who wants to grow into the emerging field of AI security.

The successful candidate is not expected to begin as an expert in every area of AI or cybersecurity; through hands-on experience, collaboration, mentoring, and targeted development, the engineer will build expertise in AI security architecture, threat modeling, adversarial testing, governance controls, secure AI engineering, and AI-enabled cybersecurity capabilities.

The engineer will assess risks, identify vulnerabilities, help design and implement security controls, and work with business and technology teams to protect information and systems while preserving the functionality, usability, and business value of AI solutions.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Translate AI security policies, standards, and architecture requirements into practical engineering controls, reusable implementation patterns, test criteria, and evidence-producing processes.
  • Design and build AI-enabled cybersecurity solutions, workflows, and automation that improve detection, investigation, response, vulnerability reduction, and control validation.
  • Design, implement, and validate safeguards against AI-specific and traditional security threats, including prompt injection, data exposure, unsafe tool use, excessive agency, model abuse, identity misuse, and supply-chain risk.
  • Support AI development teams with secure build and implementation practices, including approved library and dependency management, secure MCP and tool-integration patterns, controlled data-access designs, identity and permission configuration, secrets handling, and approved security patterns.
  • Define and execute security validation methods for AI solutions, including threat modeling, adversarial testing, control testing, secure configuration review, and readiness checks before production deployment.
  • Establish logging, monitoring, alerting, and response capabilities so AI-related activity, risks, and incidents can be detected, investigated, contained, and improved over time.
  • Communicate AI security risks, options, trade-offs, and recommendations in clear business terms to support responsible AI adoption; stay current on AI technologies, threats, regulations, and standards and apply relevant developments to security controls and engineering practices.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE YOU'LL BRING

  • Bachelor's degree in cybersecurity, computer science, engineering, information systems, data science, artificial intelligence, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant education and practical experience.
  • 5+ years of relevant hands-on engineering experience in one or more areas such as application or software development, data engineering, cloud engineering, AI/ML, platform engineering, infrastructure, identity and access management, DevOps, or cybersecurity.
  • 5+ years of experience designing, building, supporting, testing, or securing enterprise technology solutions, applications, cloud services, data platforms, infrastructure, or security technologies.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCES AND SKILLS

  • Foundational understanding of cybersecurity principles such as identity and access management, data protection, secure application design, vulnerability management, cloud security, logging and monitoring, or risk management.
  • Familiarity with cloud services, APIs, application development, data platforms, scripting, infrastructure as code, CI/CD pipelines, AI platforms, or security tools.
  • Exposure to generative AI, agentic AI, machine learning, natural-language processing, data science, AI application development, or machine-learning operations.
  • Experience with one or more major AI or cloud ecosystems, such as Microsoft Azure AI and Copilot, OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, or comparable enterprise services.
  • Familiarity with security risks affecting AI-enabled solutions, including prompt injection, insecure tool use, excessive agency, sensitive-data disclosure, unsafe output handling, identity misuse, and third-party or supply-chain risk.
  • Strong communication, collaboration, analytical, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to explain technical risks, trade-offs, and recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Relevant professional certifications in cybersecurity, cloud, architecture, software development, data, or AI are valued but are not required for consideration.

This role embodies Intermountain values and focuses on establishing collaborative relationships with patients and fellow caregivers to deliver the highest level of customer/patient satisfaction. The PSR ensures a superior customer experience by identifying and resolving patient needs related to patient intake and care, which may include greeting and checking-in/out patients, as well as verifying information supplied by patients.

Join Our Team as a Patient Service Representative!


We are seeking an organized and compassionate Patient Service Representative to join our healthcare team. If you're passionate about providing exceptional care and want to work in an environment that values growth, we’d love to hear from you!

title: Clinical Procedure Card Services Analyst
description:
Job Description:

The Procedure Card Analyst maintains, standardizes, and analyzes operating room procedure cards across designated care sites, focusing on optimizing card content—equipment, instruments, medications, supplies, and procedure standardization—with timely updates and revisions. Collaborating with physicians and perioperative leadership, the Analyst ensures content aligns with patient safety, clinical standards, and cost-saving objectives, while working with the Perioperative Supply Chain to maintain accurate supply data. Through qualitative and quantitative process improvements, the Analyst upholds IH standards, vision, and guiding principles, leading efforts to standardize and centralize key operational functions, mitigating compliance issues, supporting stewardship, and facilitating business platform implementation. Maintaining clean procedure card data enhances caregiver and physician satisfaction, improves patient safety, optimizes working capital, and increases labor efficiency.

Essential Functions

  • Procedure Card Management: Oversees procedure card management to enhance patient safety, clinician satisfaction, and perioperative efficiency while reducing waste, errors, and uncredentialed usage through strict standardization and maintenance best practices.

  • Decision Making: Analyzes incomplete data to clearly define issues and integrate diverse perspectives. Prioritizes long-term, structured solutions and allocates resources for innovative, preventive measures while knowing when to act alone or consult with others.

  • Leadership Communication & Skills: Crafts targeted communication strategies for various stakeholders to ensure accountability and deliver constructive feedback. Aligns departmental actions with care site and IH strategic goals, fostering positive HR practices through mentoring, performance management, and coaching.

  • Management & Sustainment: Oversees daily updates to ensure accurate card content (equipment, instruments, supplies, positioning devices, and physician accreditation). Coordinates timely card updates and utilizes quality assurance tools and ServiceNow to maintain transparency and responsiveness.

  • Procedure Card Analysis: Regularly monitors and analyzes data with Tableau, Epic OpTime, and other platforms to ensure clinical data integrity and uncover standardization opportunities. Conducts periodic reviews and annual physician examinations to benchmark performance and enhance patient safety.

  • Physician Onboarding & Collaboration: Coordinates initial contact and onboarding for new providers, ensuring procedure cards are built for their cases. Partners with OR staff and surgeons to update cards, streamline case categories, and drive content improvement.

  • Perioperative Supply Chain Support: Meets weekly with the supply chain team to coordinate product conversions, update DPCs, validate Epic inventory data, and optimize supply utilization.

  • OR Support: Attends weekly OR leadership huddles to discuss projects, physician onboarding, and staff education. Provides training on procedure card processes, reviews scheduling reports to catch and resolve errors, and ensures all scheduled cases have the correct cards attached.

Skills

  • Communication

  • Clinical Knowledge

  • Facilitation

  • Taking Initiative

  • Accountability

  • Organization

Required Qualifications

  • AA Degree of Nursing or Graduate of a surgical technology program or equivalent experience/training required

  • Maintain current License or certification

  • Extensive acute operating room experience as a certified surgical technician or registered nurse across multiple service lines.

  • Demonstrated experience with physician procedure cards; operating room related billing, card maintenance, scheduling, and/or auditing.

  • Demonstrated knowledge/experience with operating room surgical equipment, instruments, positioning devices, medications, and/or supplies. Utilizing ERP for operating room procedure card systems (EPIC OpTime or Cerner preferred).

  • Current Basic Life Support Certification (BLS) for healthcare providers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of analytics: Tableau, Excel and Epic

  • Knowledge and deployment of Lean methodologies.

title: Senior Identity Governance Engineer
description:
Ready to be a Titan?

At ServiceTitan, we are building a next-generation identity fabric, and this role engineers the governance layer on top of it. Identity spans cloud environments, SaaS applications, data systems, machine identities, and now AI agents, which makes it one of the most sprawling attack surfaces in the enterprise. You will make sure every identity, whether a Titan, a third-party contractor, a service account, or an AI agent, has the right access, for the right reason, at the right time, and that we can prove it.


Corporate Engineering (IT) administer our identity platforms, including Okta and Lumos, and run lifecycle operations. InfoSec defines identity governance requirements and validates that controls work. You sit in InfoSec and engineer the governance layer: authentication and authorization design standards, entitlement models, access review automation, and audit-ready evidence. You administer Veza with Corporate Security, Security Architecture, Product Security, and Security Operations, work with Corporate Engineering and System Owners to put governance requirements into practice, and you will be a key owner of our ISPM and IGA program.


What you'll do:

You engineer identity governance: the tooling, automation, and design standards that make access reviewable and provable. Corporate Engineering and IT administer the identity platforms, and InfoSec GRC owns the policies and the review program.

  • Access Request Governance: Define governance requirements and design patterns for access request workflows across privileged systems (code repositories, databases, infrastructure), including role-based, time-bound, delegated, and just-in-time access, and measure adoption so access is not granted outside the governed workflow. Corporate Engineering and IT administer Lumos and implement the workflows; you specify the requirements, build the monitoring that detects bypass, and validate that they work.
  • Authentication & Authorization Design: Partner with Security Architecture to define authentication and authorization design standards (SSO, MFA and phishing-resistant requirements, OIDC/SAML/SCIM patterns, least-privilege role models) for enterprise tools, and review integrations against them.
  • Authorization Governance & Entitlement Design: Provide the technical design for authorization decisions on job functions and privileged data access, including critical systems such as ST Admin roles, Snowflake, Salesforce, and other high-risk entitlements. Build role models scoped to job function and normalize entitlement data across applications in Veza so access can be reviewed like for like.
  • Access Review & Lifecycle Automation: Build and operate the tooling and automation behind the user access review program (SOX ITGC, PCI DSS, SOC 1/2, ISO 27001), which InfoSec GRC owns, and behind joiner/mover/leaver control assurance, including leaver access-reversion evidence, reconciliation against the authoritative HR source, and orphaned account detection.
  • Privileged Access Governance: Build visibility into standing privileged access across core cloud infrastructure and the data platform and drive it down, moving toward time-bound elevation (PIM and JIT) with governed exceptions for the access that must remain.
  • Identity Fabric Architecture: Define the target-state governance architecture across Okta, Veza, and Lumos and the risk-based identity lifecycle it supports. You administer Veza in combination with Corporate Security, Security Architecture, Product Security, and Security Operations, building its data source integrations, policies, and alerts. Corporate Engineering and IT administer Okta and Lumos, and you partner with them on lifecycle and workflow integration.
  • ISPM & Continuous Governance: Add continuous monitoring to periodic certifications. Build identity analytics that detect over-privileged accounts, shadow identities, dormant access, and identity drift, and automate remediation workflows with named owners.
  • Non-Human Identity & AI Security: Build the inventory and governance workflows for service accounts, API keys, personal access tokens, and AI agents, including ownership, rotation, and attestation requirements, and drive remediation with owning teams. Ensure AI integrations are covered by rigorous entitlement management, in partnership with our AI governance review process.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with Corporate Engineering, the administrative owner of identity platforms and lifecycle operations, alongside Security Architecture and System Owners to ensure every enterprise tool is integrated with identity by design, while InfoSec GRC defines identity governance requirements and validates control effectiveness.
  • Compliance as Code & Audit Support: Provide the technical identity evidence for audit requests (SOX, PCI, ISO 27001, SOC 1/2), partnering with our SOX IT compliance team, who coordinate with auditors. Automate evidence collection so compliance is a byproduct of good engineering, not a manual chore.
  • Vendor Engagement: Partner with Corporate Engineering to engage our strategic identity vendors (Veza, Okta, Lumos). Hold vendors accountable to their commitments and service levels, influence their product roadmaps, and secure the implementation and adoption support we need to maximize our return on investment.

What you'll bring:

We are looking for deep identity experience, whether in governance, administration, engineering, or a mix of these, paired with hands-on technical skills. You build the tools that make governance work.

  • The Fundamentals: 5+ years in identity and access, with depth in Identity Governance & Administration. Broader experience in identity and access engineering (SSO, provisioning, directory or identity platform automation) is welcome alongside a governance background. You deeply understand lifecycle management (Joiner/Mover/Leaver), RBAC/ABAC and entitlement modeling, Separation of Duties, privileged access governance, and the Principle of Least Privilege, and you can design and automate access certification programs at enterprise scale.
  • The Modern Stack: Hands-on experience with modern IGA and identity discovery tools (e.g., Veza for authorization graphs and entitlement visibility, Lumos for SaaS governance and access requests, Okta for lifecycle orchestration and identity governance workflows). Experience administering an authorization graph platform such as Veza is especially valuable, since you will own it in partnership with other security teams.
  • Authentication & Authorization Design: Working knowledge of authentication and authorization standards and patterns (SSO, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, MFA, RBAC/ABAC) and the ability to review enterprise integrations against them.
  • NHI Governance: Proven experience governing non-human identities (service accounts, API keys, workload identities) in cloud-native environments (AWS/GCP), including inventory, ownership assignment, rotation and expiry requirements, periodic attestation, and risk exception handling. You can read cloud IAM and secrets management configurations and partner with the engineering teams who operate those platforms.
  • Security Posture: Understanding of ISPM principles, including detecting identity drift, excessive entitlements, orphaned accounts, and misconfigurations before they are exploited, and turning those findings into governed remediation.
  • Compliance Fluency: Ability to translate regulatory and audit requirements (SOX ITGC, PCI DSS, SOC 2, ISO 27001) into identity controls, automated workflows, and audit-ready evidence. You are comfortable working directly with internal and external auditors.
  • Automation & Engineering Skills: Proficiency in a scripting language (e.g., Python or Go), plus API integration experience and familiarity with workflow or low-code tooling, to automate access reviews, evidence collection, and remediation tracking.

Who You Are

  • A Systems Thinker: You understand the balance between People, Process, and Technology. You don't just fix a ticket; you fix the process that created the ticket.
  • An Enabler of Innovation: You believe security should be a tailwind, not a headwind. You build identity governance that lets Titans move faster and collaborate safely.
  • Data-Driven: You use identity analytics to find high-risk areas and prioritize work based on actual risk data.

Why This Role Matters

As ServiceTitan scales and integrates AI across our platform, identity governance is what keeps access defensible. Your work protects customer data, supports the trust our customers place in us, and lets our teams move faster with confidence.

Be Human With Us:
Being human isn’t about checking every box on a list. It’s about the experiences we have, people we meet, and the perspectives we share. So, if you have the skills but are hesitant to apply because of your background, apply anyway. We need amazing people like you to help us challenge the conventional and think differently about the problems that we’re solving. We’re in this together. Come be human, with us.


Use of AI Technology:

We use technology, including automated and AI-assisted tools, to support certain aspects of our recruitment process. These tools are designed to improve efficiency and enhance the candidate experience. AI tools are not used to make hiring decisions; all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams.


What We Offer:

When you join our team, you’re not just accepting a job. You’re making a career move. Here’s how we’ll support you in doing some of the most impactful work of your career:

  • Flextime, recognition, and support for autonomous work: Flexible time off with ample learning and development opportunities to continue growing your career. We offer a comprehensive onboarding program, leadership training for Titans at all levels, and other programs and events. Great work is rewarded through Bonusly, peer-nominated awards, and more.
  • Holistic health and wellness benefits: Company-paid medical, dental, and vision (with 100% employer paid options and 90% coverage for dependents), FSA and HSA, 401k match, and telehealth options including memberships to One Medical.
  • Support for Titans at all stages of life: Parental leave and support, up to $20k in fertility services (i.e. IUI and IVF), surrogacy, and adoption reimbursement, on demand maternity support through Maven Maternity, free breast milk shipping through Maven Milk, pet insurance, legal advisory services, financial planning tools, and more.

At ServiceTitan, we celebrate individuality and uniqueness. We believe that the convergence of fresh perspectives and experiences from all walks of life is what makes our product and culture so great. We strongly encourage people from underrepresented groups to apply. title: ENOA, Services Coordinator
description:
Job Title

ENOA, Services Coordinator

Hours Required

40

Job Description and Hours

Responsible for determining and monitoring the appropriate long term care needs of financially eligible clients over the age of 65 who are requesting or receiving assistance through home and community based services. Responsible for coordinating home and community based services to eligible participants by identifying their strengths and needs and incorporating formal and informal supports through a participant-centered approach to service planning and delivery. Responsible for completion of a comprehensive assessment to identify client strengths and needs. Responsible for providing participants with choices for safe independent living options and consumer-directed services that are cost efficient.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

1. Must report to work as scheduled on a regular and reliable basis.

2. Successfully complete all required pre-service orientation and training.

3. Must insure confidentiality of all client information and act in accordance with HIPAA regulations.

4. Ability to understand and comply with various laws, rules, regulations, policies and guidelines as they pertain to both ENOA and ENHSA.

5. Ability to communicate clearly, both orally and in writing and be able to establish effective working relationships with many different people, ranging from directors, coordinators, professionals, community representatives, support staff and the general public.

6. Be a strong team player with positive attitude toward working with staff and with clients and their formal and informal support systems.

7. Must have good computer skills with general knowledge of Microsoft office and have the ability to learn other computer systems.

8. Work with established standards for service coordination and employee’s professional discipline.

9. Basic knowledge of applicable state and federal laws, policies and regulations as they relate to the Nebraska Medicaid Program.

10. Knowledge of medical and psychiatric diagnoses, prognoses, needs, and expected outcome goals.

11. Ability to establish positive relationships, promote client/family autonomy while using a participant-centered approach to the service coordination process.

12. Assessment: A comprehensive assessment is the vital first step in the service coordination process. This assessment is the process of systematically and comprehensively identifying the strengths and limitations that influence the participant/client’s functional capacity. The assessment process includes a face to face interview with participant/client in their home environment, observations, and collateral contacts to confirm the Nursing Facility level of care determination and proceeds accordingly. The service coordinator uses a participant centered process in which the participant/client identifies strengths, needs, priorities, resources, and barriers. Each participant/client needs to be reassessed at least annually and upon any major biopsycho-social changes that influence their functional ability and safety.

13. Planning: The plan of services and supports is a collaborative, written document that is prepared with the participant/client and services coordinator. It is based on the findings from the comprehensive assessment, collateral data and the participant’s/client’s preferences. The plan of services and supports document includes: problem statements converted to measurable outcome goals, strengths, intervention/service objectives, units of service (formal and informal), timeframes and providers/contacts. The Service Coordinator and the participant decide on the level of services coordination and determine the role of the Services Coordinator and the participant in the plan implementation.

14. Implementation: The Services Coordinator and the participant identify formal providers and informal supports with focus upon participant preference and cost effectiveness.

15. Coordination: Services and care arrangements require a Service Coordinator to be the broker of high quality and cost effective services. A Service Coordinator must develop and maintain rapport and communications with the participant/family and caregiver/s so that important information regarding delivery of services and products impacting on the goals and outcome of the plan can be disclosed. Maintaining professional rapport and communication with the members of the team is essential so the plan can be discussed objectively, problems identified, and adjustments made to the plan as needed. The Service Coordinator for the participant is the “team leader” for said participant and initiates communication with other disciplines as needed for appropriate planning (e.g. joint assessments, care planning meetings, external professionals).

16. Monitoring: Careful follow-up that tracks whether or not the service was provided as requested and if it was satisfying; monitoring must occur in a timely manner via direct and telephone contact. Maintain regular communication with all providers delivering care, services, and products to the participant for quality assurance purposes. Ascertain that the outcomes of the plan are appropriate, understood, documented, and being met. Advise the providers of adjustments or revisions to be made in the plan.

17. Evaluation: Determining if the outcome goals and service objectives in the plan of services and supports produce beneficial results to the client and agency. This may include gathering statistical information to evaluate both client level outcomes and service utilization outcomes.

18. Advocacy: The Service Coordinator provides the client with information and training that promotes self-sufficiency. Advocacy is a process that occurs throughout the service coordination process and is an essential element to ensure participant centered care and empowerment.

19. Must have a valid driver’s license, reliable vehicle and state required car insurance.


OTHER JOB DUTIES:

1. Other job-related duties as assigned by the Division Director.


EDUCATION, TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE:

1. Baccalaureate degree in the field of human services, education or health/medical or Registered Nurse, currently licensed in Nebraska and a minimum of two years professional experience in long-term care, gerontology, rehabilitation, health/safety case management, children with special health care needs or health and medical. 2. Previous work experience and technical understanding of the psycho-physiological traits of aging and the older adult preferred.


SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

1. Possess good judgment, organizational ability and initiative.

2. Be detail oriented, flexible, multi-tasked, discrete and decisive with a strong ability to prioritize tasks and use critical thinking skills.

3. Independently organize and prioritize workflow, ensuring timeliness and professionalism, in all functions.

4. Familiarity and ability to drive through the five county geographic service area in a variety of road conditions.

5. Have a high standard of integrity and knowledge of professional ethics

6. Ability to work independently and complete required paperwork within specified timeframes.

7. Must have good computer and typing skills with general knowledge of Microsoft office and have the ability to learn other computer systems.

8. Must have the ability to use office equipment; such as fax, scanner, copier, printer, and other equipment as needed.


PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS:

1. Must be able to tolerate a variety of working environments.

But, this job description is not intended to be an inclusive list of qualifications, skills, efforts, duties, responsibilities or working conditions associated with the position and may be subject to revision.
