title: Network Security Engineer
description:
Company and Vision

PlanetArt’s vision is to be the leading seller of personalized and make-on-demand products worldwide. We provide consumers with unmatched tools and content and an unparalleled end-to-end customer experience that results in high-quality, meaningful finished products and memorable celebrations of life events.

The company’s brands include the popular FreePrints and FreePrints Photobooks apps and the industry leading SimplytoImpress card and stationery site, as well as Personal Creations, CafePress and ISeeMe! Visit to learn more about our brands.

We have more than 500 team members across multiple offices, primarily in Calabasas CA, San Diego CA, Woodridge IL, Minneapolis, MN and Pleasanton, CA. We also have team members in two company-owned offices in China, as well as in Europe.

Job Overview

PlanetArt is looking for a Network Security Engineer to support the company’s Security Department. The successful candidate will assess network and server security, monitor security events, and investigate alerts across Cisco technologies, Palo Alto firewalls, Windows and Linux servers, and endpoint security tools. This role requires an understanding of SIEM log collection and monitoring, EDR configuration, and SOC alert triage. The engineer will work with infrastructure teams to address security risks; direct configuration of network devices and firewalls is outside the scope of this position.

PLEASE NOTE: Candidates must be local to or willing to relocate to the (office) area as we operate on a hybrid work model (3 days onsite, 2 remote)

What You’ll Do

Key Responsibilities

  • Review Cisco and Palo Alto firewall policies, access controls, segmentation, VPNs, and security logs.
  • Assess Windows and Linux server hardening, patching, authentication, permissions, and audit logging.
  • Verify SIEM collection of firewall, network, server, and endpoint logs; investigate logging gaps.
  • Monitor SIEM and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) alerts for suspicious activity.
  • Triage alerts: validate detections, distinguish false positives, assess severity, and escalate incidents.
  • Correlate network, server, identity, and endpoint events to identify affected systems and timelines.
  • Configure EDR policies, detection settings, exclusions, and alerts through approved change procedures.
  • Coordinate incident containment and remediation with infrastructure teams; track issues to resolution.
  • Document investigations and response procedures; evaluate AI use in analysis and detection.
  • Develop, test, and maintain security tools for log analysis, alert triage, and automation.
  • Recommend security improvements to the teams responsible for network and server configuration.

Requirements

What You Should Have

Skills, Qualifications, and Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or equivalent experience.
  • 3–5 years of experience in network security, security operations, incident response, or a related role.
  • Working knowledge of Cisco technologies and Palo Alto firewalls, including interpreting configurations, policies, and logs; understanding of TCP/IP, DNS, NAT, VPNs, and segmentation.

  • Preferred: Splunk experience, including SPL searches, dashboards, and configuring and tuning alerts, thresholds, schedules, and notifications.

title: Revenue Integrity Auditor Full Time Days
description:
Job Summary :

The Revenue Integrity Auditor identifies billing and coding discrepancies, potential compliance violations, revenue leakage, overpayments, underpayments, documentation deficiencies, and operational control weaknesses. The role develops audit findings, recommends corrective and preventive actions, monitors remediation efforts, and collaborates with Revenue Cycle, Health Information Management (HIM), Coding, Patient Financial Services, Clinical Documentation Integrity (CDI), Compliance, Privacy, and Information Security teams to promote sustainable compliance and financial integrity.

Job Description

Essential Responsibilities:


  • Comprehensive Revenue Integrity Auditing:
    • Conduct routine, focused, retrospective, and risk-based audits across the healthcare revenue cycle, including patient registration, eligibility, authorization, charge capture, coding, billing, claims submission, payment posting, and account adjustments.
    • Perform end-to-end account audits to validate the accuracy and completeness of patient encounters, charges, supporting documentation, claim submission, reimbursement, and financial transactions.
    • Evaluate compliance with internal policies, standard operating procedures, payer contracts, reimbursement methodologies, and applicable regulatory requirements.
    • Identify revenue leakage, missed charges, duplicate charges, inappropriate write-offs, unsubstantiated adjustments, billing errors, and reimbursement variances.
    • Assess the effectiveness of revenue cycle controls and recommend improvements to reduce compliance risk and prevent recurring errors.
    • Develop and maintain audit plans, sampling methodologies, audit tools, workpapers, and supporting documentation.
  • Medical Coding, Clinical Documentation, Billing and Claims Compliance:
    • Audit ICD-10-CM/PCS, CPT, HCPCS Level II, and other applicable coding for accuracy, completeness, specificity, and consistency with supporting medical record documentation.
    • Evaluate appropriate assignment of diagnoses, procedures, modifiers, units of service, place of service, and other claim elements, as applicable.
    • Review compliance with official coding guidelines, National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI) edits, medically unlikely edits, and payer-specific billing policies.
    • Assess medical necessity, documentation sufficiency, and the appropriateness of billed services in accordance with applicable coverage and reimbursement requirements.
    • Identify potential upcoding, undercoding, unbundling, duplicate billing, unsupported services, and other coding or billing practices that may create compliance exposure.
    • Collaborate with coding and CDI teams to clarify documentation deficiencies, validate audit findings, and support education and corrective action.
    • Provide recommendations for coding corrections, claim adjustments, and other appropriate remediation in accordance with organizational policy and applicable law.
    • Review outpatient, inpatient, and facility claims, as applicable, for accurate charge reporting, coding, billing, and reimbursement.
    • Validate compliance with Medicare, Medicaid, commercial payer, and other applicable billing requirements.
    • Evaluate claim edits, denials, rebilling practices, late charges, and adjustments for accuracy and compliance.
    • Identify patterns involving inappropriate reimbursement, unsupported charges, missed revenue opportunities, and preventable claim denials.
    • Escalate potential improper payments, suspected fraud, waste, abuse, and significant billing compliance concerns through established reporting channels.
  • HIPAA Privacy, Regulatory Compliance, Risk Assessment, and Confidentiality Auditing:
    • Assess revenue cycle workflows for compliance with applicable HIPAA Privacy Rule and Security Rule requirements and organizational privacy and security policies.
    • Evaluate appropriate access to PHI, minimum-necessary practices where applicable, secure handling of medical records, and appropriate use and disclosure of information during billing, coding, auditing, and reimbursement activities.
    • Review audit processes involving electronic health records, billing systems, claim attachments, payer communications, and other systems containing PHI.
    • Identify potential privacy risks, inappropriate access, unauthorized disclosures, insecure information transmission, and deficiencies in the handling or retention of sensitive information.
    • Verify that audit documentation, supporting evidence, and reports containing PHI are accessed, stored, transmitted, and retained in accordance with applicable requirements and organizational procedures.
    • Coordinate suspected privacy or security incidents with the Privacy Officer, Information Security, and Compliance teams for appropriate investigation and follow-up.
    • Support privacy awareness and compliance education for revenue cycle personnel.
    • Maintain working knowledge of applicable CMS regulations, Medicare and Medicaid billing requirements, HIPAA, the False Claims Act, payer policies, and other relevant federal and state requirements.
    • Conduct risk assessments to identify high-risk billing practices, regulatory vulnerabilities, control deficiencies, and emerging compliance trends.
    • Evaluate adherence to organizational compliance policies, applicable coding standards, documentation requirements, and established internal controls.
    • Support compliance investigations, external audit requests, payer audits, governmental reviews, and other regulatory inquiries as assigned.
    • Prepare accurate, objective, and defensible audit workpapers documenting scope, methodology, evidence, findings, risk levels, and conclusions.
    • Escalate significant findings promptly to appropriate leadership and compliance personnel.
  • Continuous Improvement:
    • Prepare comprehensive audit reports summarizing findings, root causes, financial impact where quantifiable, compliance exposure, and recommended corrective actions.
    • Partner with operational leaders to develop corrective action plans, assign responsibilities, establish target completion dates, and define measurable outcomes.
    • Conduct follow-up audits and validation testing to confirm that corrective actions have been implemented and are effective.
    • Monitor recurring errors, audit trends, denial patterns, coding discrepancies, and other key performance indicators.
    • Develop and deliver targeted education to address identified knowledge gaps and recurring compliance issues.
    • Recommend process improvements, system edits, automated controls, and preventive measures to strengthen revenue integrity.
    • Maintain appropriate confidentiality, independence, and objectivity throughout the audit process.

  • I. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

    • Ability to conduct comprehensive, objective, and risk-based audits.
    • Working knowledge of HIPPA privacy and security requirements and appropriate PHI handling.
    • Strong analytical, investigative, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills.
    • Ability to interpret regulations, payer policies, medical records, financial data, and audit evidence.
    • Proficiency with electronic health records, billing platforms, spreadsheets, reporting tools, and audit tracking systems.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present findings to operational and executive leadership.
    • Ability to maintain confidentiality, exercise sound judgment, and handle sensitive compliance matters professionally.
    • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple audits, deadlines, and competing priorities.
    • Ability to work with associates to promote education, excellence, and job satisfaction among employees.
    • Ability to lead, promote long-term employment and implement new procedures.
    • Promote teamwork within the department and achieve overall department goals.
    • Interact with all associates, physicians, and general public appropriately.
    • Maintain emotional stability and calm disposition.
    • Possess a high level of loyalty, reliability, tactfulness, honesty, and discreetness.
    • Able to handle confidential information in a professional manner.
    • Adaptable to changes in work schedules and interruptions in work.
    • Strong Knowledge of healthcare revenue cycle operations, billing practices, and coding guidelines.

  • II. Education and Experience Required:

    • Bachelors required in Business, Finance, Nursing, or Health Information Management. Registered RN with current RN license and or a hospital Inpatient coder with a CCS certification preferred.
    • 5 + years of revenue cycle experience within integrated healthcare system, preferably within hospital revenue integrity department.
    • RHI/RHIT/CCS/BSH license required
    • Experience evaluating healthcare regulatory requirements, payer billing policies, and internal controls.
    • Familiarity with HIPAA privacy and security requirements and the handling of PHI.
    • Experience preparing audit reports, appeal letters, and identifying root causes.

title: Software Engineer
description:
Surescripts serves the nation through simpler, trusted health intelligence sharing, in order to increase patient safety, lower costs and ensure quality care. We deliver insights at critical points of care for better decisions — from streamlining prior authorizations to delivering comprehensive medication histories to facilitating messages between providers.

We're always interested in connecting with exceptional talent. This evergreen posting allows us to identify and engage candidates who may be a fit for current or future opportunities as our business grows. While there may not be an active opening at the time of your application, we'd love to learn more about you.


Please note: Because this is an evergreen posting, there may not be an immediate hiring timeline. Our recruiting team will reach out if your qualifications align with a current or upcoming opportunity.


Job Summary


Design, develop, assess, and troubleshoot software applications in an Agile environment for the one of the nation's largest and most trusted healthcare information network. Collaborate with architects, customers, product partners, and other engineers to solve complex engineering challenges by building high-volume applications that process millions of transactions a day, store multiple terabytes of data, and serve hundreds of thousands of customers. Software Engineers are expected to use approved AI tools to improve speed, quality, and outcomes while remaining fully accountable for results.


Responsibilities

  • Develop and troubleshoot software applications in an Agile environment, collaborating with others to produce high quality working tested software.
  • Contribute throughout the software development life cycle by estimating work, refining requirements, iterating on designs, delivering working software, communicating with partner teams, and supporting critical applications.
  • Lead or participate in design and code reviews; create and maintain automated tests; validate acceptance criteria; and monitor production systems to identify defects, incidents, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Apply shift-left quality practices to shorten feedback loops, reduce rework, prevent recurring defects, and ensure software is secure, reliable, observable, maintainable, and production-ready.
  • Cultivate and share application development, testing, troubleshooting, documentation, security, data privacy, and Agile best practices.
  • Use approved AI-assisted development tools across design, implementation, testing, debugging, analysis, and documentation; review all output and remain accountable for delivered software’s correctness, security, performance, and maintainability.
  • Continuously improve AI-assisted workflows based on measurable impact to delivery speed, quality, operations, and customer outcomes.

Qualifications

Basic Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in software engineering, computer science, a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 2+ years of experience in related, progressive software engineering roles.
  • Experience with multiple programming languages, such as C#, Java, Groovy, Scala, Python, TypeScript, or JavaScript.
  • Experience with current tools and platforms for developing, building, testing, deploying, and monitoring software systems.
  • Experience using modern AI-assisted software development tools to support coding, testing, debugging, documentation, and software delivery workflows.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively, communicate clearly, learn continuously, and ask for help or escalate issues when appropriate.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with high-volume, data-intensive applications.
  • Experience building web services and distributed systems.
  • Hands-on software troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and production support experience.
  • Familiarity with relational and non-relational database technologies.
  • Knowledge of application security, observability, data privacy, and responsible software delivery practices.
  • Healthcare technology industry experience.
  • Understanding of AI governance, security, privacy, compliance, quality, and responsible-use practices for software systems.
  • Experience effectively leveraging generative AI tools, such as GitHub Copilot, Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, or similar tools, throughout the software development life cycle.

Some of the technologies we use:

  • Languages: C#, Java, Groovy, Scala, Python, TypeScript, JavaScript
  • Frameworks: .NET Core, Spring/Spring Boot
  • Front-end technologies: Angular, Bootstrap, OpenID Connect
  • Infrastructure and data platforms: Kafka, Cassandra, InfluxDB, HashiCorp Consul, Docker, Jenkins, Ansible, Google Cloud Platform, BigQuery, Airflow, Composer, and Terraform

Surescripts embraces flexibility through its Flexible Hybrid Work model for most positions. This model allows employees to work virtually while still utilizing our offices as collaboration centers. With alignment and agreement from your leadership, you can come and go from the office as needed.

To be considered for employment, applicants must have a valid U.S. work authorization allowing work without restrictions with Surecripts in the U.S. At this time, we are unable to provide support or provide sponsorship for immigration benefits such as work visas. Additionally, we do not participate in academic training programs or work-study programs through an academic institution that require employer endorsement of F-1/CPT or F-1/STEM.

Why Wait? Apply Now


We’re a midsize company. This means you’re not just another employee ID number. Here, you can build real relationships and feel supported by truly awesome people with diverse backgrounds and talents in an innovative and collaborative work culture. We strive to create an environment where you can be yourself, share your ideas and work your way. Your base pay may vary within or outside of this range depending on a number of factors, including (but not limited to) your qualifications, skills, experience, and location.


Benefits include, but are not limited to, comprehensive healthcare (including infertility coverage), generous paid time off including paid childbirth and parental leave and mental health days, pet insurance, and 401(k) with company match and immediate vesting. To learn more, review the Keep You and Yours Healthy, Balancing Work and Life, and Where Talent Takes Shape links under the Better Benefits. Better Work. Better Life section of our careers site.

title: System Division Director of Maternal-Fetal Medicine
description:
The System Division Director of Maternal-Fetal Medicine (MFM) is the physician leader responsible for the clinical, operational, quality, academic, and strategic direction of Maternal-Fetal Medicine across Boston Medical Center Health System, including Boston Medical Center, BMC Brighton, and BMC South.


The System Division Director provides leadership for MFM physicians and other members of the multidisciplinary MFM team and is accountable for ensuring consistently high-quality, evidence-based, equitable maternal and fetal care across all sites. The Director establishes systemwide clinical standards and expectations for MFM care; oversees the quality, safety, effectiveness, and coordination of MFM services; and works with hospital, departmental, nursing, and administrative leaders to ensure that patients receive the appropriate level of care at the appropriate site.


The System Division Director also leads the academic mission of the MFM Division at Boston Medical Center and Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine, including faculty development, education, scholarship, and research. The Director will advance a systemwide vision for MFM that combines the capabilities of a tertiary academic medical center with strong community-based obstetric services, allowing patients to receive care close to home whenever appropriate while ensuring timely access and transfer to tertiary-level care when needed.


A central expectation of this position is the development of an integrated MFM program across Boston Medical Center Health System, with shared clinical standards, coordinated staffing and coverage, common approaches to quality and safety, and clear pathways for consultation, escalation, and maternal transfer among the three hospitals.


Reporting and Key Relationships

The System Division Director of Maternal-Fetal Medicine reports to the System Chair of Obstetrics & Gynecology.


The Director works in close partnership with:

● Vice Chair of Clinical Operations and Strategy

● Chiefs of Obstetrics & Gynecology at BMC Brighton and BMC South

● Director of the Antenatal Testing Unit

● MFM clinicians across the health system

● Obstetricians, Certified Nurse Midwives, Family Medicine physicians, and advanced practice providers providing obstetric care

● Nursing and administrative leaders at each hospital

● Neonatology, Anesthesiology, Critical Care, Genetics, Cardiology, and other medical and pediatric subspecialties involved in high-risk pregnancy care

● Quality, patient safety, risk management, and credentialing leadership

● Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine educational and research leadership


The System Division Director has authority for systemwide MFM clinical standards, professional practice expectations, quality and safety priorities, and MFM service strategy. Local operational implementation is carried out collaboratively with the OB/GYN Chief and administrative and nursing leadership at each hospital.


Duties and Responsibilities


1. System Leadership and Strategic Direction


● Develop and implement a comprehensive vision and strategic plan for Maternal-Fetal Medicine across Boston Medical Center Health System, in alignment with the priorities of the Department of Obstetrics & Gynecology and the health system.

● Lead the development of an integrated systemwide MFM service that appropriately distributes clinical expertise and services among BMC Main Campus, BMC Brighton, and BMC South.

● Establish clear expectations regarding the scope of MFM services provided at each hospital and criteria for consultation, escalation of care, and transfer to the tertiary academic medical center.

● Identify opportunities to expand access to high-risk obstetric care throughout the system while maintaining appropriate levels of maternal and fetal safety.

● Partner with departmental, hospital, and system leadership in strategic planning for obstetric and perinatal services, including anticipated changes in clinical volume, patient acuity, staffing, facilities, and technology.

● Represent MFM in systemwide planning regarding maternal and fetal health.


2. Clinical Operations


● Provide physician leadership and oversight for inpatient and outpatient MFM services across all three hospitals.

● Oversee clinical operations of the high-risk obstetric practice in the ambulatory setting.

● Oversee and provide mentorship for the department genetic counselors.

● Ensure that each hospital has appropriate MFM coverage based on its patient population, clinical capabilities, acuity, and designated scope of care.

● Develop and oversee coordinated physician staffing and coverage models for MFM services across all three sites, including ambulatory consultation, prenatal care, ultrasound and antenatal testing, inpatient consultation, Labor & Delivery support, and after-hours MFM availability.

● Establish systemwide expectations for timely MFM consultation and response to urgent maternal and fetal conditions.

● Ensure appropriate MFM participation in multidisciplinary management of complex pregnancies.

● Develop efficient systems for sharing MFM expertise across hospitals, including in-person consultation, telemedicine, remote review, and other models when clinically appropriate.

● In collaboration with the ATU Director, oversee standards for interpretation and timely review of obstetric ultrasound and fetal diagnostic studies performed throughout the health system.

● Work with clinical and operational leaders to improve patient access, scheduling, continuity, and efficiency of MFM services.

● Optimization of billing in collaboration with departmental administration

● Maintain an active clinical practice in Maternal-Fetal Medicine appropriate to the individual's expertise and leadership responsibilities.


3. Systemwide Clinical Standards and Care Integration


● Lead the development and implementation of consistent evidence-based clinical policies, guidelines, pathways, and standards for high-risk obstetric care across the health system.

● Establish standardized approaches to common high-risk maternal and fetal conditions while allowing appropriate adaptation to the resources and capabilities of each hospital.

● Define clinical criteria for patients who can safely receive care at community hospitals and those who should receive consultation, co-management, or transfer to Boston Medical Center.

● Develop and periodically review maternal and fetal transfer criteria and processes, including mechanisms for urgent physician-to-physician consultation.

● Ensure effective coordination between outpatient MFM care, inpatient obstetric services, Labor & Delivery, antenatal testing, and ultrasound services.

● Strengthen communication and continuity across sites when patients move between community-based and tertiary care.


4. Quality, Safety, and Clinical Outcomes


● Provide physician leadership for quality and patient safety in high-risk obstetric care across the health system in collaboration with quality and safety leadership

● In conjunction with department quality and safety leadership, establish and monitor systemwide MFM quality metrics and clinical outcomes, with particular attention to severe maternal morbidity, maternal mortality, fetal and neonatal outcomes, obstetric complications, transfers, and other measures relevant to high-risk pregnancy.

● In conjunction with department quality and safety leadership, identify unwarranted variation in clinical practice or outcomes among sites and lead improvement efforts when opportunities are identified.

● Ensure appropriate MFM participation in maternal morbidity and mortality review, obstetric case review, safety-event review, root-cause analysis, and other quality processes throughout the system.

● Ensure MFM participation in the development and review of maternal-child health policies and guidelines.

● Lead quality improvement initiatives addressing racial and other inequities in maternal morbidity and mortality and the complex medical and social needs of the populations served by Boston Medical Center Health System.

● Promote a culture of safety, transparency, learning, and continuous improvement across the MFM Division.

● Ensure compliance with relevant institutional policies, regulatory requirements, accreditation standards, and professional guidelines.


5. Faculty Leadership and Professional Development


● Provide professional leadership for MFM physicians and high-risk advance practice providers across Boston Medical Center Health System.

● Foster a culture of collaboration in which MFM physicians function as members of a unified system division while maintaining strong relationships with their individual hospital teams.

● Participate in recruitment, hiring, onboarding, retention, and succession planning for MFM faculty.

● Participate in annual performance evaluations and professional development planning for MFM faculty in collaboration with the Department Chair and appropriate site leadership.

● Mentor faculty in clinical excellence, education, scholarship, research, leadership, and academic advancement.

● Identify opportunities for individual faculty members to develop areas of clinical or academic expertise and assume leadership responsibilities within the division or health system.

● Address concerns regarding professional performance, quality of care, professionalism, or clinical competency in collaboration with departmental, medical staff, credentialing, and hospital leadership.

● Lead the department high-risk/perinatal committee.

● Participate in focused professional practice evaluation or other physician performance review processes when indicated.

● Promote faculty engagement, professional fulfillment, and a respectful and inclusive work environment.


6. Multidisciplinary and Cross-Site Collaboration


● Build effective partnerships with obstetricians, midwives, Family Medicine physicians, neonatologists, anesthesiologists, genetic counselors, sonographers, nurses, advanced practice providers, and other clinicians involved in high-risk pregnancy care.

● Develop multidisciplinary approaches to the management of complex maternal and fetal conditions.

● Facilitate regular communication among MFM clinicians and obstetric leadership across the three hospitals.

● Establish mechanisms for review of complex cases and system-level clinical issues involving more than one hospital.

● Serve as the senior MFM physician resource for difficult clinical, operational, or systems-of-care questions across Boston Medical Center Health System.

● Participate in or designate appropriate MFM representation on hospital and system perinatal, quality, safety, and clinical operations committees.


7. Education


● Provide leadership for the educational mission of Maternal-Fetal Medicine within the Department of Obstetrics & Gynecology.

● Ensure excellence in MFM education for OB/GYN residents and Boston University medical students.

● Participate in the clinical supervision and teaching of residents, medical students, fellows, faculty, and other learners.

● Develop educational opportunities that use the breadth of clinical environments within Boston Medical Center Health System.

● Support continuing professional education for physicians and other clinicians providing high-risk obstetric care at BMC Brighton and BMC South.

● Promote dissemination of new evidence, clinical guidelines, and best practices throughout the system.


8. Research, Scholarship, and Innovation


● Provide strategic leadership for the research and scholarly mission of the

MFM Division at Boston Medical Center and Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine.

● Foster an environment that supports clinical, translational, health-services, implementation-science, and other research relevant to maternal and fetal health.

● Mentor and support faculty in scholarly activity, research development, publication, presentation, and pursuit of extramural funding.

● Encourage collaborative research involving other divisions, departments, institutions, and health-system sites.

● Use the breadth of the health system as an opportunity to study and improve the delivery of high-risk pregnancy care across academic and community settings.

● Promote innovation in models of care, digital health, telemedicine, population health, and other approaches that improve access and maternal and fetal outcomes.


9. Health Equity


● Advance the Department's and health system's commitment to eliminating preventable disparities in maternal and fetal outcomes.

● Ensure that equity is incorporated into clinical standards, quality measurement, program development, access initiatives, and strategic decision-making.

● Use clinical and operational data to identify disparities in access, treatment, experience, and outcomes and develop interventions to address them.

● Work collaboratively with institutional health-equity initiatives and community partners to address structural barriers affecting patients with high-risk pregnancies.

● Promote respectful, culturally responsive, patient-centered care throughout the system.


10. Program Development and Stewardship of Resources


● Partner with departmental and administrative leadership to develop sustainable models for MFM services across the system.

● Evaluate clinical volume, demand, access, staffing, productivity, and resource utilization across sites and recommend changes as needed.

● Participate in development of annual goals and resource priorities for the Division.

● Support responsible stewardship of physician, staff, ultrasound, clinical-space, and other resources.

● Identify opportunities to improve clinical efficiency while preserving quality, safety, patient experience, and clinician well-being.

● Participate in business planning for new or expanded MFM services and programs.

● Monitor relevant clinical, operational, quality, access, and financial performance measures and develop improvement plans when goals are not met.


Qualifications and Experience Required


● MD or DO degree from an accredited medical school or equivalent.

● Completion of an accredited residency in Obstetrics & Gynecology and fellowship in Maternal-Fetal Medicine.

● Board certification in Obstetrics & Gynecology.

● Board certification in Maternal-Fetal Medicine.

● Eligibility for an unrestricted Massachusetts medical license.

● Academic accomplishments appropriate for appointment at Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine at the Associate Professor or Professor level, or demonstrated trajectory toward such appointment as appropriate.

● Demonstrated record of clinical excellence in Maternal-Fetal Medicine.

● Significant leadership experience within MFM, Obstetrics & Gynecology, or a related clinical program.

● Demonstrated ability to lead physicians and multidisciplinary teams and to work effectively across organizational and professional boundaries.

● Experience in clinical operations, quality improvement, patient safety, and program development.

● Strong written and oral communication skills and demonstrated organizational and management ability.

● Commitment to the mission of Boston Medical Center Health System and to providing exceptional, equitable care to all patients.


Preferred


● Experience leading clinical services across multiple hospitals, practice locations, or levels of care.

● Experience in an academic health system combining tertiary and community-based clinical services.

● Demonstrated success in faculty recruitment, mentorship, professional development, and performance management.

● Experience developing and implementing clinical pathways or standards across multiple sites.

● Record of academic scholarship, research, educational leadership, or extramural funding.

● Experience using quality, operational, and financial data to guide clinical program development.

● National or regional leadership within Maternal-Fetal Medicine or maternal health.

● Fluency in Spanish, French, Haitian Creole, or other languages commonly spoken by patients served by Boston Medical Center Health System is desirable but not required.

Measures of Success

The System Division Director will be evaluated on the ability to:

● Create a cohesive, collaborative systemwide MFM division.

● Provide reliable access to MFM expertise at all three hospitals.

● Establish clear and effective clinical standards, consultation pathways, and transfer criteria across the health system.

● Demonstrate improvement in maternal and fetal quality and safety outcomes and reduction in unwarranted variation among sites.

● Maintain strong physician and multidisciplinary engagement.

● Recruit, retain, mentor, and develop outstanding MFM faculty.

● Support excellence in resident and medical student education.

● Advance the Division's academic, scholarly, and research mission.

● Improve the effectiveness and efficiency of MFM clinical operations.

● Develop MFM services that are clinically excellent, operationally effective, and financially sustainable.

● Build strong working relationships among the academic medical center, community hospitals, and referring clinicians throughout Boston Medical Center Health System.


Administrative Support:


The System Division Director will receive protected administrative time appropriate to the scope and responsibilities of systemwide leadership. The amount of protected time will be established by the Chair of Obstetrics & Gynecology and reviewed periodically based on the size, complexity, and evolving responsibilities of the System MFM Division.


Applicants must have the ability to work collegially within a diverse environment and demonstrate a commitment to our institutional values regarding diversity, equity, and inclusion.


Consistent with our commitment to meet our patients’ desire for concordant care, BIPOC (Black/Brown, Indigenous, and other People of Color) applicants are encouraged to apply. Academic appointment will be at Boston University School of Medicine; rank is commensurate with experience and CV. We offer a competitive salary and an attractive benefit package.


Send CV and Cover Letter to: Carol Boudrot, Boston Medical Center, carol.boudrot@bmc.org


BMC/BUSM is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer

The base salary of the finalist selected for this role will be determined based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to clinical FTE, qualifications, experience, education, board certifications, specialty, training, and scope of practice. Any eligible incentive compensation is not included in the above compensation range and will be discussed during the interview process.

title: Data Governance Manager
description:
Discover Your Career at Emory University

Emory University is a leading research university that fosters excellence and attracts world-class talent to innovate today and prepare leaders for the future. We welcome candidates who can contribute to the excellence of our academic community.
Description

The Data Governance Manager administers a university-wide data governance program in consultation with university governance bodies. The data governance program includes but is not limited to Emory University administrative data, such as financial, human resources, student, IT, faculty, research, and advancement.

The Data Governance Manager works to bring people across the university together around the shared purpose of leveraging our data to achieve Emory's mission. Reporting to the Senior Director of Data Governance, works closely with senior administration and staff to set data priorities.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Forges shared agreements across schools and units on the definition, documentation, and appropriate use of Emory University data assets and works to ensure that Emory University stakeholders know where to find data, what the data represent, and understand how the data should be used.
  • Works with units across campus to tailor the data governance program to local needs while supporting university-wide organizational structures, policies, and processes.
  • Manages institutional data initiatives and processes, particularly those in support of institutional data quality, with analytics and IT professionals across a variety of university offices and divisions including data warehouse, business intelligence, and analytics teams.
  • Maintains the data stewardship structure at the university, including defining roles and providing support to data stewards. Priorities for the data governance program are established in high-level university governance bodies, from which the Data Governance Manager takes direction.
  • Oversees the university's data governance program to ensure the integrity and usefulness of university data assets by supporting their consistent definition, documentation, and appropriate use.
  • Manages and directs the development, implementation, administration, and evaluation of data governance initiatives.
  • Provides data governance training and support to Data Trustees, Data Stewards, Data Custodians, and Users.
  • Monitors trends and developments in the field of data governance and recommends strategic directions and priorities to Emory leadership.
  • Acts as the subject matter expert for the university regarding the interpretation, implementation and compliance with data governance policies and regulations.
  • Formulates and proposes policies to the university governance bodies.
  • Produces documentation, instructions, usage agreements and other guidance documents.
  • Represents the data governance program to university stakeholders, including schools and administrative units.
  • Represents Emory University in consortia with peer universities and through data governance professional organizations.
  • Manages working groups appointed by the Data Advisory Committee or other administrative entities to achieve articulated priorities.
  • Supervises data governance staff.
  • Performs related responsibilities as required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • A bachelor's degree in information systems, analytics, or related field and four years of systems support, data governance or related experience OR an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of data governance concepts, techniques, processes, and applications.
  • Knowledge of and experience with data architecture, business intelligence, and analytics.
  • Knowledge of higher education institutions and experience with enterprise data in a university context.
  • Excellent diplomacy, facilitation, and communication skills to work effectively across our highly decentralized institution.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communications skills with the ability to cultivate professional and business partnerships.
  • The ability to work independently and as part of a team, to be flexible and adapt to different stakeholder needs and organizational cultures.

NOTE: This role will be granted the opportunity to work from home regularly but must be able to commute to Emory University on a flexible weekly schedule based upon business needs. Schedule is based on agreed upon guidelines of department. This role requires residency in the state of GA. Emory reserves the right to change remote work status with notice to employee.

title: Senior Firewall Administrator
description:
The contractor shall provide IT Infrastructure support services, which includes Tier 1 Help Desk, Tier 2 End User Support, Tier 3 Server, Platform, and Network Infrastructure Support and Engineering. Services shall include, but are not limited to, technical assistance for hardware, software, and network issues; incident and problem resolution; service request management; infrastructure monitoring and support; hardware and software lifecycle support; and management of escalation across all tiers.

Position Description: Responsible for managing and maintaining the organization's (currently PaloAlto based) firewall infrastructure. This role involves overseeing the deployment, configuration, and support of PaloAlto firewall devices, ensuring optimal performance, security, and availability. This position requires strong knowledge of PaloAlto firewall technologies, excellent troubleshooting skills, and familiarity with network security solutions.

Requirements

  • Monitoring and optimizing the performance of the network, ensuring efficient resource allocation and minimal downtime.
  • Leading the installation, configuration, and maintenance of PaloAlto firewall devices as well as Cloud firewall configurations.
  • Manage Palo Alto firewall platforms and services, including PAN-OS, VPN, Prisma Access, and GlobalProtect, ensuring lifecycle support through end-of-support timelines.
  • Monitoring and optimizing the performance of firewall systems, ensuring efficient resource allocation and minimal downtime.
  • Diagnosing and resolving complex firewall issues, including connectivity, performance, and security problems.
  • Ensuring the security of the network by applying patches, updates, and security configurations to PaloAlto devices.
  • Maintaining comprehensive documentation of firewall configurations, procedures, and policies.
  • Working closely with other IT teams to support network security needs and integrate firewall solutions with other systems.
  • Providing guidance and mentorship to junior network and firewall administrators and other IT staff.

Required Skills:

  • 5 years of experience
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related field
  • Public trust security clearance
  • Firewall Administration: Expertise configuring, managing, and troubleshooting enterprise firewalls (e.g., Palo Alto, Cisco ASA/Firepower, Fortinet, Check Point, Juniper SRX).
  • Network Security: Strong understanding of network security principles, including segmentation, VPNs (IPSec/SSL), NAT, ACLs, and IDS/IPS.
  • Routing & Switching: Working knowledge of routing protocols (BGP, OSPF, EIGRP) and Layer 2 technologies.
  • Policy Management: Ability to design, implement, and optimize security policies, objects, and rulesets while maintaining compliance and minimizing overlap/conflicts.
  • Security Monitoring & Incident Response: Experience with log analysis, packet captures, and network traffic inspection for threat identification and remediation.
  • SIEM Integration: Familiarity with tools like Splunk, QRadar, or ELK for centralized event monitoring and alert correlation.
  • Operating Systems: Proficiency in administering Linux/Unix and Windows Server environments.
  • Change Management: Experience following structured change control processes and documentation in ITIL or ISO environments.
  • Scripting & Automation: Basic to intermediate scripting (Python, PowerShell, or Bash) for automating configuration or monitoring tasks.
  • Documentation: Ability to create and maintain detailed network diagrams, firewall rule documentation, and standard operating procedures.

Preferred Skills:

  • A PaloAlto Networks Certified Network Security Engineer (PCNSE) certification is preferred.
  • Cloud Security: Experience with cloud firewalls and network security configurations in AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
  • Next-Gen Firewall (NGFW) Technologies: Advanced knowledge of threat prevention, URL filtering, SSL decryption, application control, and user-ID mapping.
  • Zero Trust Architecture: Understanding of zero trust principles and micro segmentation strategies.
  • Network Access Control (NAC): Experience integrating firewalls with NAC solutions (e.g., Cisco ISE, Aruba ClearPass).
  • Load Balancing & Proxy Technologies: Familiarity with F5, Citrix Netscaler, or reverse proxy systems.
  • Certifications: Palo Alto Networks Certified Network Security Engineer (PCNSE) Cisco Certified Network Professional – Security (CCNP Security) Fortinet NSE 4–7 CompTIA Security+ / CySA+ / CASP+ Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) or equivalent
  • Experience in Regulated Environments: Understanding of compliance requirements (FISMA, FedRAMP, NIST 800-53, PCI-DSS, HIPAA).

Benefits

  • Medical
  • Dental
  • Vision
  • AD&D
  • STD
  • LTD
  • Company paid Life Insurance
  • 401k with employer contribution
  • Paid Time Off
  • Pet Insurance

Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

The Senior Manager – Systems & Verification Engineering will lead Systems and Verification & Validation organization supporting CVUS digital products across on-premises, cloud and hybrid environments. The role owns system integration, system-level verification, test strategy and automation capability for the Digital portfolio, including the CVUS Digital Viewer. As a functional leader, this person will build and develop a high-performing team, strengthen technical capability and improve product quality and release predictability through automation-first verification practices.


Roles and Responsibilities:

  • ·Own system requirements, interfaces, workflows, integration strategy, system behavior and verification approach.
  • Develop and execute system V&V strategies for on-premises, cloud and hybrid digital products.
  • Define and evolve scalable test automation frameworks, tools and infrastructure for continuous, regression and release testing.
  • Increase automation across API, integration, workflow, system, performance and end-to-end product testing.
  • Ensure requirements traceability from customer and system needs through verification evidence and release readiness.
  • Own system-level verification planning, execution, defect management, risk-based testing and quality assessment.
  • Partner with Software Engineering, Architecture, Product Management and Clinical teams to build testability and quality into product design.
  • Establish metrics for automation coverage, test effectiveness, defect leakage, regression health and release readiness.
  • Partner with Quality, Regulatory and Cybersecurity teams to ensure verification evidence supports design controls, risk management and regulatory expectations.
  • Build, hire, coach and retain strong Systems and V&V talent; own workforce planning, performance management, competency development and succession.
  • Collaborate with global CVUS teams and communicate system quality, verification status, risks and release readiness to engineering leadership.

Educational Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering or a related engineering discipline.

Required Qualifications:

  • 15+ years of progressive experience in software-intensive product development, systems engineering, verification and validation or related disciplines.
  • 5+ years of functional engineering leadership experience, including people management, talent development, performance management and organizational capability building.
  • Proven experience leading Systems Engineering and/or V&V teams for complex digital products.
  • Demonstrated experience defining test automation strategies and implementing scalable automation frameworks.
  • Strong experience in system requirements, interfaces, integration, verification planning, traceability, defect management and release-readiness assessment.
  • Experience testing complex products across on-premises, cloud and/or hybrid environments.
  • Strong knowledge of software development lifecycle, system architecture, APIs, distributed systems, CI/CD and automated testing.
  • Proven ability to build teams, develop technical talent and drive execution in a global matrix organization.
  • Strong leadership, communication, stakeholder-management and problem-solving skills.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Experience with medical-device, healthcare or other regulated digital products.
  • Knowledge of healthcare interoperability standards including DICOM, HL7 and FHIR.
  • Experience with Azure, AWS or GCP and cloud-based system verification.
  • Experience integrating automated verification into CI/CD and DevOps/DevSecOps pipelines.
  • Knowledge of IEC 62304, ISO 14971, IEC 62366-1, design controls and risk-based verification.
  • Experience modernizing manual V&V organizations towards an automation-first verification model.
  • Demonstrated success improving product quality and release predictability using engineering metrics, root-cause analysis and continuous improvement.

Common Engineering Expectations:

  • Cloud-native and hybrid cloud/on-premises product development using AWS services.
  • Containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code and production observability.
  • Secure engineering, identity and access management, encryption, secrets management and DevSecOps.
  • Performance, scalability, availability, reliability, fault tolerance and disaster recovery.
  • Automated unit, integration, API, system, performance and reliability testing.
  • Strong design, coding, debugging, root-cause analysis and technical documentation practices.
  • Integration challenges of third party and second party SaaS solutions.
  • Working with AI-DLC and software development acceleration.

Healthcare and Medical Device Context:

  • Experience in regulated healthcare or medical-device development is required for the Verification Lead and strongly preferred for senior architecture, automation and program roles.
  • Strong knowledge on SDLC, PRD process, Risks, FMEAs.
  • Awareness of patient-data privacy, cybersecurity and secure handling of clinical information.
  • Knowledge of healthcare interoperability standards such as DICOM, HL7 and FHIR.
  • Experience with real-time clinical data, device connectivity, patient monitoring or high-availability clinical applications is advantageous.

title: Application Security Analyst
description:
Company and Vision

PlanetArt’s vision is to be the leading seller of personalized and make-on-demand products worldwide. We provide consumers with unmatched tools and content and an unparalleled end-to-end customer experience that results in high-quality, meaningful finished products and memorable celebrations of life events.

The company’s brands include the popular FreePrints and FreePrints Photobooks apps and the industry leading SimplytoImpress card and stationery site, as well as Personal Creations, CafePress and ISeeMe! Visit to learn more about our brands.

We have more than 500 team members across multiple offices, primarily in Calabasas CA, San Diego CA, Woodridge IL, Minneapolis, MN and Pleasanton, CA. We also have team members in two company-owned offices in China, as well as in Europe.

Job Overview

PlanetArt is looking for an Application Security Analyst to support the company’s Security Department. The successful candidate will be responsible for securing our applications by managing vulnerabilities identified through Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), and other application security software (currently Snyk, with possible future use of Semgrep). This role will also oversee the Bug Bounty program, provide support for security notifications from the MSSP, conduct threat intelligence research, and contribute to governance, risk, compliance (GRC), cloud security, and third-party risk management activities. The analyst will use approved artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support security analysis and remediation, apply sound judgment to AI-generated outputs, and help assess the security of AI-enabled applications and development workflows.

PLEASE NOTE: Candidates must be local to or willing to relocate to the (office) area as we operate on a hybrid work model (3 days onsite, 2 remote)

What You’ll Do

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage vulnerabilities identified through SAST, DAST, and other application security tools.
  • Validate, prioritize, and assign vulnerabilities to Application Development (AppDev) teams; track remediation efforts and verify closure.
  • Oversee the Bug Bounty program, including triage, validation, and coordination with AppDev and external researchers.
  • Conduct threat intelligence research to identify risks to applications and the broader organization.
  • Support MSSP-provided security notifications through validation, triage, and assignment of issues.
  • Collaborate with AppDev to improve secure coding practices and provide remediation guidance.
  • Use approved AI tools to assist with vulnerability triage, code review, threat research, and remediation guidance; independently validate findings and recommendations before acting on them.
  • Review AI-generated code and AI-assisted development workflows for security weaknesses, and help AppDev teams apply secure coding and testing practices.
  • Assess AI-enabled applications and integrations for risks such as prompt injection, sensitive data exposure, insecure output handling, and excessive permissions in AI agents and connected tools.
  • Follow company policies for AI use, protect source code, credentials, and confidential data, and contribute to guidance for evaluating AI tools and third-party AI services.
  • Contribute to organizational GRC initiatives, audits, and compliance efforts.
  • Provide support for cloud security initiatives and third-party risk management reviews.

Requirements

What You Should Have

Skills, Qualifications, and Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or equivalent experience.
  • 3–5 years of experience in application security, vulnerability management, or related role.
  • Hands-on experience with SAST/DAST tools (Snyk required; Semgrep preferred).
  • Knowledge of OWASP Top 10, CWE, and secure development practices.
  • Practical experience using generative AI tools or AI-assisted security and development tools, including writing effective prompts, verifying outputs, and recognizing inaccurate or unsupported results.
  • Working knowledge of large language models (LLMs), common AI application security risks, and controls such as input and output validation, access restrictions, and protection of sensitive data.
  • Ability to evaluate AI-generated code and security recommendations using manual review and established testing tools; understanding of responsible AI use and data handling requirements.
  • Familiarity with bug bounty platforms and coordinated vulnerability disclosure processes.
  • Understanding of threat intelligence processes and incident response workflows.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to collaborate across technical and business teams.
  • Preferred: Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure), GRC frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2), and professional certifications (GWAPT, OSWE, GWEB, CEH, CISSP). Familiarity with security testing of LLM applications, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), AI agents, or AI service integrations is also preferred.

What You Can Expect

Working Conditions

  • Work is performed in an office environment with low to moderate noise levels.
  • Occasional lifting of up to 20 pounds.
  • Position requires regular, continuous use of computer.
  • Position requires regular sitting and standing.
  • Position requires regular interaction with team members through the following methods: in-person, phone, WebEx, Slack, or email.
  • May require occasional travel.
  • This is a hybrid position; employees are expected to be in the office three days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday) with the option of working remotely two days (Wednesday and Friday).

Benefits

PlanetArt offers a comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • Life Insurance
  • 401(k) with matching
  • Excellent Work/Life Balance – Paid Time Off, Sick Days, Paid Holidays, and Floating Holidays
  • Employee Product Discounts

title: Senior Technical Artist - AI & Creative Automation
description:
We’re looking for a Senior Technical Artist - AI & Creative Automation to help shape how AI is used across our creative production teams.

This role sits at the intersection of art, engineering, AI, and production. It is for someone who can recognize what great creative work looks like and build reliable systems that help teams create, evaluate, refine, and deliver that work at scale.

You’ll design and ship AI-powered tools, agents, automation, and production workflows used across our mobile games. You’ll work closely with artists, designers, animators, developers, and other technical partners to identify high-impact problems, prototype solutions quickly, and turn the best ideas into dependable production systems.

We’re looking for someone with exceptional artistic judgment, strong technical depth, and a practical understanding of modern AI. You understand how artists think and make creative decisions, and you can translate that understanding into tools and systems that preserve creative intent while increasing speed, quality, consistency, and team capability.

You should be curious about emerging technologies, but practical about what belongs in production. You know how to evaluate whether AI is actually the right solution, when conventional automation is better, and where human creative judgment must remain part of the process.

You’ll own your work from the first experiment through deployment, adoption, measurement, and ongoing improvement.

Show Us What You’ve Built

We want to see both your creative judgment and technical thinking.

Alongside your CV, please share a portfolio and two or three relevant projects. These might include production tools, AI agents, automated workflows, creative applications, model pipelines, custom integrations, or other systems you have built.

For each project, please tell us:

  1. What problem were you solving?
  2. What did you personally design or build?
  3. What did the final output or workflow look like?
  4. How did it improve the work or production process?

We’re especially interested in projects that moved beyond experimentation and were used by real people in production.

Demos, workflow breakdowns, before-and-after examples, architecture diagrams, code samples, evaluation approaches, and examples of real production use are all welcome.

Requirements

Artistic Skills & Creative Production

  • Professional experience in art, graphic design, animation, motion graphics, VFX, technical art, game art, or a closely related visual discipline.
  • Strong foundations in composition, color, lighting, perspective, visual hierarchy, and storytelling.
  • Practical experience with creative tools such as Photoshop, Illustrator, After Effects, Blender, Maya, or equivalent applications.
  • Ability to translate art direction into repeatable systems while preserving character identity, visual style, and brand guidelines.
  • Strong understanding of creative production pipelines, including ideation, feedback, revisions, delivery, integration, and technical constraints.

Programming & Technical Development

  • Strong practical skills in Python for automation, tooling, AI integration, and production workflows.
  • Experience building tools, services, integrations, or applications using modern development technologies.
  • Strong API integration skills, including asynchronous jobs, batch processing, structured outputs, retries, and failure handling.
  • Working knowledge of deploying and maintaining applications, including hosting, authentication, logging, monitoring, and troubleshooting.
  • Comfortable with Git, GitHub, open-source repositories, dependency management, and shared production codebases.
  • Ability to understand, review, debug, and maintain the code you ship, including code developed with AI assistance.

AI Models, Agents & Automation

  • Proven experience building AI-powered tools, agents, automations, or workflows used in real production.
  • Experience with agentic systems that use tools and APIs, manage multi-step tasks, validate results, and recover from failures.
  • Strong hands-on experience with generative image and multimodal AI workflows, with video and/or audio experience being valuable.
  • Ability to evaluate and switch between commercial APIs, hosted services, and open-source models based on production needs.
  • Strong understanding of prompt and context design, structured outputs, tool use, routing, validation, and failure handling.
  • Experience creating repeatable AI evaluation and benchmarking processes.
  • Familiarity with open-source AI ecosystems and node-based generative workflows such as ComfyUI or equivalent systems.
  • Proficiency with AI-assisted development tools such as OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, or equivalent systems, while maintaining ownership of code quality and technical decisions.

Experience & Ownership

  • Typically 5+ years of relevant experience across technical art, creative technology, production tooling, software development for creative teams, or adjacent disciplines.
  • Substantial recent experience applying AI and automation to creative or production workflows.
  • A track record of taking ambiguous problems from exploration through prototype, deployment, adoption, and support.
  • Evidence that you have built systems used by teams, not only personal tools or experiments.
  • Ability to balance experimentation with production reliability and know when a workflow is ready to scale.
  • Strong communication skills across creative, technical, production, and non-technical teams.

Exceptional candidates with less traditional tenure but strong evidence of production-scale impact, technical depth, artistic judgment, and ownership are encouraged to apply.

Nice to Have

You do not need to have every item below.

  • Strong JavaScript/TypeScript experience, including Node.js and/or modern frontend development.
  • Experience creating plugins, extensions, or automation for tools such as Photoshop, After Effects, Blender, Maya, Unity, or similar applications.
  • Experience with Unity scripting or game-engine pipeline development.
  • Experience fine-tuning, adapting, or customizing generative models.
  • Experience running GPU-based AI workloads or local/self-hosted models.
  • Experience with generative video, animation, voice, music, or audio pipelines.
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure, containers, model serving, queues, or scalable inference systems.
  • Experience working in mobile games, live-service games, or high-volume creative production environments.

Benefits

Why This Role Is Different

  • You’ll build production tools used by a team of 30+ creatives across six live games.
  • You’ll have the ownership to rethink workflows from the ground up and see successful ideas become part of everyday production.
  • You’ll work directly across art, engineering, AI, and production.
  • You’ll solve real production challenges with direct feedback from the people using what you build.
  • You’ll help shape how we use AI as a creative organization—from the technologies we adopt to the standards and responsible practices behind them.
  • Your success will be measured by production impact, not simply by the number of prototypes you create.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year, we expect you to have:

  • Shipped AI-powered or automated workflows that are actively used in production.
  • Reduced meaningful production bottlenecks or repetitive creative work.
  • Demonstrated measurable improvements in speed, quality, consistency, cost, or team capability.
  • Established reusable systems or approaches that can scale across multiple teams, games, or creative disciplines.

title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Networking
description:
Join NVIDIA’s Hyperscale Engineering team to develop networking solutions for large-scale AI infrastructure. You will work with customers and engineering teams to build, integrate, and improve software for BlueField and ConnectX platforms.

Your work will span software development, system integration, troubleshooting, and performance analysis, helping customers move from initial testing to production deployment.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Work with customers to understand their networking requirements and develop technical solutions.
  • Develop and integrate networking software for BlueField and ConnectX platforms.
  • Test and optimize RDMA and RoCE solutions for performance and reliability.
  • Investigate issues across applications, networking libraries, drivers, firmware, and switches.
  • Analyze packet drops, congestion, latency, and throughput to identify problems and recommend improvements.
  • Create test cases and automation to reproduce issues, validate fixes, and measure performance.
  • Collaborate with software, firmware, architecture, and product teams throughout development and deployment.
  • Document findings and communicate progress, technical decisions, and next steps.

What we need to see:

  • A degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8+ years of relevant software or systems engineering experience.
  • Experience programming in C and developing or debugging software on Linux.
  • Knowledge of networking protocols and experience with RDMA, RoCE, or other high-performance networking technologies.
  • Experience investigating technical issues and evaluating possible solutions.
  • Clear communication skills and the ability to work with customers and colleagues across teams.
  • An interest in learning new technologies and sharing knowledge.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience with BlueField, ConnectX, DOCA, DPDK, or RDMA verbs.
  • Knowledge of congestion control, QoS, PFC, or ECN.
  • Familiarity with AI workloads, NCCL, or CUDA.
  • Experience testing or deploying networking solutions at scale.
  • Python or shell scripting experience for diagnostics and automation.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 184,000 USD - 287,500 USD for Level 4, and 224,000 USD - 356,500 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until October 30, 2026.
