title: Resort Director of Engineering & Facilites
description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

At Valor, we are passionate Hotelitarians—driven, detail-obsessed professionals who go beyond service to deliver true hospitality. With a global perspective and a commitment to thoughtful hospitality and sustainable dining, we bring enthusiasm, creativity, and local flair to every property we support. We seek individuals who value relationships, embrace high standards, and create meaningful experiences for guests, teams, and owners alike. If you’re someone who notices the little things and strives to make a lasting impact, you’ll thrive here.

Please visit http://www.valorhospitality.com to learn more about our existing hotels, other exciting job opportunities and our company.

POSITION PROFILE

The Resort Director of Engineering & Facilities is responsible for the strategic leadership, administration, maintenance, safety, and preservation of all resort-owned facilities, infrastructure, building systems, and engineering operations across the McLemore resort campus. This position is responsible for protecting and enhancing the resort's physical assets while ensuring facilities are safe, reliable, efficient, exceptionally maintained, and consistently aligned with the standards of a luxury destination resort.

Reporting to the Cloudland General Manager and serving as a key member of the resort leadership team, the Resort Director of Engineering & Facilities provides oversight of maintenance operations, capital planning, utility management, risk mitigation, regulatory compliance, contractor management, and engineering team development across a diverse portfolio of hospitality, residential, food & beverage, and resort amenity assets. The Director partners closely with resort leadership and department heads to maintain asset quality, minimize operational disruptions, control operating costs, anticipate future capital requirements, and ensure the physical condition of the resort consistently supports an exceptional guest and owner experience.


McLemore is a mid-sized luxury golf resort featuring a full-service hotel, private and rental residences, restaurants and food & beverage outlets, spa and wellness facilities, retail operations, event facilities and other resort amenities. This position oversees all engineering and facilities functions throughout the resort campus while specifically excluding golf course maintenance, agronomy operations, and golf irrigation systems.



ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILTIES

Leadership & Team Development

  • Lead, develop, coach, and manage engineering and facilities personnel across the resort.
  • Establish departmental objectives, service standards, performance expectations, and accountability measures.
  • Recruit, train, schedule, mentor, and evaluate engineering and facilities team members.
  • Develop succession planning and technical training to strengthen departmental capabilities.
  • Foster a culture of safety, accountability, professionalism, responsiveness, hospitality, and continuous improvement.
  • Establish staffing and coverage plans sufficient to support resort operations, residences, restaurants, amenities, events, and emergency needs.
  • Maintain a visible leadership presence throughout the resort and develop strong working relationships with operational leaders.

Engineering & Facilities Operations

  • Direct all preventive maintenance, predictive maintenance, repairs, and engineering operations throughout the resort.
  • Ensure reliable and efficient operation of HVAC, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, structural, fire protection, life-safety, building automation, communications, and other facility systems.
  • Maintain buildings, roads and non-golf resort infrastructure, exterior lighting, drainage, utilities, support facilities, residential assets, and other property components within the department's assigned scope.
  • Develop and maintain comprehensive preventive-maintenance programs for all major equipment and building systems.
  • Oversee the resort's computerized maintenance management system and ensure work orders are appropriately prioritized, assigned, documented, and completed.
  • Establish response and completion standards for emergency, urgent, guest-impacting, and routine maintenance requests.
  • Analyze work-order history, equipment failures, and recurring maintenance issues to identify root causes and implement permanent solutions.
  • Prioritize and deploy resources effectively to address emergencies and operational or guest-impacting conditions.
  • Coordinate departmental coverage and on-call response appropriate to resort operating requirements.

Asset Preservation & Capital Planning

  • Maintain a comprehensive inventory and condition assessment of major resort assets, equipment, systems, and infrastructure.
  • Develop lifecycle replacement schedules for major HVAC, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, life-safety, roofing, structural, building-envelope, and other facility systems.
  • Develop multi-year repair and replacement strategies designed to reduce deferred maintenance and unexpected equipment failures.
  • Conduct routine property-condition inspections and identify potential deterioration before it materially impacts guest experience, operations, safety, or asset value.
  • Establish resort standards for equipment maintenance, warranty management, documentation, and replacement.
  • Maintain accurate equipment histories, warranties, operating manuals, drawings, inspection records, and related asset documentation.
  • Identify infrastructure vulnerabilities and recommend appropriate operational or capital solutions.

  • Develop and maintain a rolling three-to-five-year capital plan addressing asset preservation, equipment replacement, infrastructure, renovations, modernization, energy efficiency, and operational improvements.
  • Evaluate facility conditions and identify repair, replacement, renovation, and modernization requirements.
  • Develop capital project scopes, preliminary budgets, schedules, bid requirements, and recommendations.
  • Present capital needs and priorities to the General Manager and other executive leadership as appropriate.
  • Coordinate competitive bidding, contractor selection, contract administration, and project execution.
  • Oversee construction, renovation, infrastructure, and improvement projects from planning through completion.
  • Monitor capital expenditures against approved scope, schedule, and budget.
  • Ensure projects comply with applicable codes, regulations, resort standards, design requirements, and safety expectations.
  • Manage project turnover, commissioning, warranties, training, documentation, and closeout.
  • Identify deferred-maintenance exposure and prioritize investments based on safety, reliability, guest impact, operational importance, asset protection, and financial considerations.

Financial Management

  • Develop and manage departmental operating and capital budgets.
  • Monitor labor, repairs and maintenance, supplies, utilities, service contracts, and other departmental expenses against budget.
  • Forecast major maintenance and repair expenditures and communicate potential budget variances proactively.
  • Review and approve maintenance purchases, service agreements, contracts, and vendor expenditures within established authority.
  • Identify opportunities to improve operating efficiency and reduce costs without compromising guest experience, safety, reliability, or asset quality.
  • Manage utility consumption and develop energy and water conservation initiatives.
  • Evaluate repair-versus-replacement decisions based upon operating reliability, lifecycle costs, capital requirements, and long-term asset needs.
  • Maintain appropriate inventory and purchasing controls for critical parts, supplies, and equipment.

Safety, Compliance & Risk Management

  • Ensure compliance with all applicable local, state, federal, OSHA, environmental, and life-safety regulations.
  • Maintain all fire and life-safety systems in fully operational condition.
  • Conduct regular inspections, audits, and preventative testing of building systems and equipment.
  • Develop emergency response and business continuity procedures related to engineering and facilities operations.
  • Ensure proper documentation, permits, certifications, and compliance records are maintained.

Contractor & Vendor Management

  • Select, negotiate, and manage third-party vendors, contractors, consultants, and service providers.
  • Monitor contractor performance and ensure adherence to resort standards, safety requirements, and contract obligations.
  • Manage service agreements, warranties, inspections, and preventative maintenance contracts.
  • Coordinate specialized repairs and technical services when internal resources are insufficient.

RESIDENTIAL & RENTAL HOME FACILITIES

  • Oversee engineering and maintenance services supporting resort-managed rental residences and other residential assets within the department's assigned scope.
  • Establish property-condition and preventive-maintenance standards for managed residences.
  • Coordinate maintenance access and scheduling to minimize disruption to homeowners and resort guests.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of repairs, work performed, responsibilities, and associated costs.
  • Partner with residential operations, rental management, housekeeping, and guest services to ensure homes are maintained to established McLemore standards.
  • Assist in identifying long-term maintenance and capital requirements affecting resort-managed residential assets.

Guest & Owner Experience

  • Ensure the condition, reliability, appearance, and functionality of resort facilities consistently support McLemore's luxury positioning and guest experience.
  • Partner with resort leadership to proactively identify and resolve facility conditions that may negatively impact guests or owners.
  • Respond with urgency and professionalism to guest-facing or owner-facing engineering concerns.
  • Ensure hotel accommodations, rental homes, restaurants, public areas, amenities, and support facilities meet established resort standards.
  • Coordinate engineering activities to minimize noise, visual disruption, access limitations, or other impacts on guests and residents.
  • Ensure engineering employees and contractors working in guest-facing areas conduct themselves professionally and appropriately.

Administrative Responsibilities

  • Maintain accurate maintenance, inspection, asset, project, warranty, compliance, and equipment records.
  • Prepare departmental reports, forecasts, operational analyses, and capital-planning documents.
  • Utilize CMMS and facility-management technology to monitor maintenance activities, performance, trends, and asset history.
  • Maintain facility drawings, equipment records, manuals, warranties, vendor information, and other critical engineering documentation.
  • Communicate proactively with the General Manager and resort leadership regarding significant equipment failures, safety concerns, operational risks, capital needs, and guest-impacting issues.
  • Participate as a member of the resort leadership team.
  • Serve in Manager-on-Duty or other resort leadership functions as assigned.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Strong knowledge of hotel, resort, residential, and commercial facility operations.
  • Quore, PEP, Micros and IT experience preferred
  • Hilton Quality Assurance and Ecosure experience preferred
  • Comprehensive understanding of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, mechanical, structural, fire protection, and life-safety systems.
  • Demonstrated experience managing facilities across multiple asset types, including hospitality and residential properties.
  • Strong financial acumen with experience managing operating budgets and capital projects.
  • Ability to analyze technical problems and determine practical, cost-effective solutions.
  • Knowledge of applicable building codes, regulatory requirements, and safety standards.
  • Excellent project management, organizational, and prioritization skills.
  • Strong leadership capability with the ability to build and develop high-performing teams.
  • Exceptional communication and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced resort environment.
  • Proficiency with computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS), Microsoft Office, and facility management technology.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

-- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Facilities Management, Construction Management, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.

-- Professional certifications such as Certified Facilities Manager (CFM), Facilities Management Professional (FMP), Certified Hotel Administrator (CHA), or similar credentials are desirable.

-- Minimum of 5-10 years of progressive engineering, facilities, or property maintenance leadership experience.

-- Minimum of 5 years of senior-level management experience within a hotel, resort, mixed-use, residential, or hospitality environment.

-- Experience leading capital improvement projects and multi-building facilities operations required.

--Luxury resort or destination resort experience strongly preferred.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

  • Ability to lift, push, pull, and carry up to 50 pounds occasionally.
  • Frequent walking throughout the resort campus and residential areas.
  • Ability to climb ladders, access mechanical spaces, and inspect facilities.
  • Regular bending, kneeling, crouching, and standing.
  • Ability to respond to facility emergencies outside normal business hours when necessary.

  • Uniforms Provided for most positions

  • Benefits - Health, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, and other supplemental options

  • Paid PTO

title: E-commerce Account Specialist
description:
Are you passionate about e-commerce, sales and the digital world?


At Essity, we are looking for an E-commerce Account Specialist to join our Sales team at our office in Sant Joan Despí, Barcelona. This is a great opportunity to develop your e-commerce and sales expertise, with a strong initial focus on Amazon, while working with well-known consumer brands such as Colhogar, Demak’Up and TENA, and gaining broader exposure to the FMCG business.


About the Role


As an E-commerce Account Specialist, you will contribute to the development and execution of our e-commerce strategy for key pure-play customers. You will work across sales, promotions, pricing, performance analysis and online execution, while also supporting product content and digital merchandising activities. As you develop in the position, you may also gain exposure to regional and traditional customers, giving you the opportunity to build a broader understanding of FMCG sales beyond the e-commerce channel.


What You Will Do


  • Support the development and execution of e-commerce commercial initiatives, particularly for Amazon and other prioritized pure-play accounts.
  • Support assortment, pricing, merchandising and promotional activities across customer platforms.
  • Analyze sales and online performance data to identify trends, opportunities and areas for improvement.
  • Monitor competitors and market activities within the online channel.
  • Track key digital performance indicators, including search ranking, product content and availability.
  • Support the creation and maintenance of high-quality product content, images and digital shelf execution.
  • Prepare reports and performance analyses using Excel and other reporting tools.
  • Work closely with Sales, Marketing, Trade Marketing, Supply Chain and Finance to ensure successful execution of e-commerce projects and campaigns.
  • Build effective relationships with customer contacts together with the Sales team.
  • Over time, support selected regional/local accounts and gain exposure to traditional FMCG sales activities.

Who You Are


  • You hold a Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing or a related field.
  • You have approximately 2-3 years of experience in e-commerce, digital marketing, sales or account management
  • Previous experience with Amazon, marketplaces, pure players or FMCG would be a strong advantage
  • You are comfortable working with numbers and data and have good Excel skills
  • Knowledge of Amazon Vendor Central and/or Nielsen would be an advantage, but is not essential as training will be provided.
  • You have a strong commercial and customer-oriented mindset.
  • You are curious about technology and the digital environment and comfortable adapting to tools and platforms that evolve quickly.
  • You are proactive, detail-oriented and able to manage several activities simultaneously
  • You enjoy working collaboratively and are flexible and open to learning
  • You are fluent in English, as meetings and activities related to Amazon are regularly conducted in English
  • Spanish is required to effectively interact with local customers

What We Can Offer You


This role provides the opportunity to develop strong expertise in e-commerce and FMCG sales, combining commercial responsibilities with exposure to digital marketing, analytics and customer management.

The position follows a hybrid working model, typically with 3 days in the office and 2 days working from home, with flexibility based on business and team needs.

If you are analytical, commercially minded and excited about building your career in e-commerce while learning how a leading FMCG business operates across both digital and traditional channels, we would love to hear from you.

description:

The Branch Manager is also responsible for selecting, training and developing talented branch staff and for monitoring performance to achieve business results by leading the branch team in business development, compassionate service delivery, client satisfaction and retention. title: Senior Cloud DevOps Engineer - Jenkins, OpenShift & AWS
description:
Ready to take your career global?


Make your mark at one of the biggest names in payments. We’re looking for a talented Senior DevOps Engineer to join our ever evolving Checkouts team and help shape the future of global commerce.


What you’ll own

In this role, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining robust infrastructure and deployment pipelines across cloud and containerized environments. You will work closely with development, security, and operations teams to ensure the reliability, scalability, and security of our platforms.


Key Responsibilities

  • Cloud Infrastructure (AWS):
    • Design, deploy, and manage AWS infrastructure using best practices.
    • Extensive experience with AWS managed services, such as:
      • RDS/Aurora (provisioning, backups, scaling, monitoring)
      • S3 Buckets (data lifecycle management, permissions, encryption)
      • IAM (user/role/policy management, least privilege principles)

  • Containerization & Orchestration:

    • Implement best practices for container security, scaling, and monitoring.
    • Automate deployments and manage cluster resources efficiently.
  • CI/CD & Automation:
    • Build and maintain robust CI/CD pipelines using Jenkins and GitHub.
    • Automate testing, integration, and deployment workflows.
    • Troubleshoot and optimize build and deployment processes.
  • Collaboration & Support:
    • Work closely with development and QA teams to streamline release cycles.
    • Mentor junior engineers and promote DevOps best practices.
    • Participate in on-call rotation and incident response as needed.
  • Security & Compliance:
    • Implement and monitor security controls across cloud and containerized environments.
    • Ensure compliance with internal and external standards.

What you’ll bring

  • 5+ years of experience in a DevOps, Cloud Engineering, or Platform Engineering role
  • Strong hands-on experience with AWS and AWS managed services (RDS/Aurora, S3, IAM, Lambda, Secrets Manager, etc.)
  • Deep understanding of Terraform for infrastructure automation
  • Experience deploying and managing workloads on OpenShift and/or Kubernetes
  • Proficient with Jenkins and GitHub for CI/CD pipeline development and automation
  • Strong scripting skills (e.g., Bash, Python, or similar)
  • Solid understanding of networking, security best practices, and monitoring in cloud environments
  • Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills
  • Strong communication and collaboration abilities

It’s a bonus if you have

  • AWS certifications (e.g., Solutions Architect, DevOps Engineer)
  • Experience with monitoring and logging tools (e.g., CloudWatch, Prometheus, Grafana)
  • Experience in highly regulated environments or with PCI/DSS compliance

The people, the energy, the connections – it’s unmatched. Come and be part of an ever-evolving company and get dynamic opportunities that go beyond borders.

Globalpayers think like a client, act like an owner and win as one team. We’re curious and innovative – always finding better ways to deliver impact. We empower each other to make decisions, and it’s our passion that drives excellence in everything we set out to do.

description:
At T-Mobile, we invest in YOU! Our Total Rewards Package ensures that employees get the same big love we give our customers. Employees enjoy multiple wealth-building opportunities through our annual stock grant, employee stock purchase plan, 401(k), and access to free, year-round money coaches. That’s how we’re UNSTOPPABLE for our employees!

This role provides senior-level project and portfolio management support across site development and hard cost delivery activities within Field Technology Operations in Overland Park, Kansas. This Sr. Project Manager, Development serves as a key operational lead and first point of escalation for development-related activities, supporting leasing, zoning, permitting, regulatory compliance, construction coordination, vendor performance, project forecasting, and schedule adherence for new and modified telecommunications sites.

The role partners closely with RF, Operations, Construction, Real Estate, vendors, and market leadership to drive consistency, remove roadblocks, manage risk, and ensure timely and quality delivery of development and construction initiatives. While the position may directly manage assigned projects, its primary focus is broader portfolio oversight, operational rigor, reporting accuracy, issue resolution, and coordination of hard cost programs across multiple workstreams.

Success in this role requires a seasoned, self-directed professional who can quickly assess priorities, anticipate challenges, guide cross-functional partners, and elevate critical issues when appropriate. The position supports organizational goals by helping ensure development checkpoints, budget expectations, vendor deliverables, compliance requirements, and construction quality standards are met in support of network performance, customer experience, and market execution.

Base Job Responsibilities:

  • Lead and support planning, coordination, and execution of site development and hard cost activities across assigned market portfolio, including leasing, zoning, permitting, regulatory compliance, construction coordination, and site modification work.
  • Coordinate with RF, Operations, Construction, Real Estate, vendors, and other partners to align priorities, optimize resources, remove obstacles, and support successful delivery of development and construction programs.
  • Monitor project and portfolio progress against key checkpoints, schedules, forecasts, budgets, and deliverables; track and communicate status — including schedule updates, phase gate progression, risk, budget impacts, vendor performance, and forecast accuracy — to partners and project sponsors to help ensure timely, accurate, and quality execution of development initiatives.
  • Identify process gaps, project risks, reporting inconsistencies, and execution challenges; recommend solutions and help implement improvements that drive consistency, accountability, and operational efficiency.
  • Ensure development activities are completed in accordance with regulatory requirements, company standards, construction quality expectations, and applicable operational guidelines.
  • Serve as the first point of contact for development-related questions, risks, roadblocks, and critical issues from internal teams, vendors, and cross-functional partners, resolving issues where appropriate and calling out critical matters to management when needed; provide guidance and informal leadership to project teams to support issue resolution, process compliance, and successful project delivery.
  • Also responsible for other duties, programs, and projects as assigned by business management as needed.

Specific Job Responsibilities

  • Lead recurring vendor and internal deployment calls to review portfolio status, align on priorities, track checkpoint progress, identify blockers, confirm ownership of action items, and drive timely resolution of development, construction, and hard cost delivery issues.
  • Support management of vendor activities and deliverables to ensure adherence to scope, timelines, quality expectations, construction standards, and contractual requirements.
  • Assist with development of portfolio reporting, executive updates, management plans, process documentation, deliverable schedules, and other tools used to support team performance and business objectives.
  • Manage assigned projects or special initiatives as needed, while maintaining broader visibility and support across the full development and hard cost portfolio.

Education and Work Experience:

  • Bachelor's Degree plus 3 years of related work experience
    OR advanced degree with 1 year of related work experience
    OR combination of education and experience deemed equivalent (Required)
  • 5+ yrs experience in project management in a complex environment, preferably wireless. (Preferred)
  • Experience developing and delivering presentations to groups. (Preferred)


Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Site Development, Construction Coordination, and Hard Cost Delivery — Required
    Strong knowledge of wireless site development and construction execution activities, including leasing, zoning, permitting, regulatory compliance, site modifications, construction coordination, capital project delivery, and hard cost management. Ability to understand how construction checkpoints, cost drivers, dependencies, and field execution risks impact overall market delivery.
  • Construction Documentation and A&E Coordination — Required
    Experience collaborating with Architecture & Engineering teams, construction vendors, and internal partners to review construction drawings, redline documentation, validate approved changes, and ensure final construction documents accurately reflect project scope, field conditions, and delivery requirements.
  • Budgeting, Procurement, and Hard Cost Management — Required
    Experience supporting project budgets, purchase order processing, cost tracking, accrual awareness, invoice support, procurement workflows, change impacts, and hard cost management. Ability to identify budget risks, cost variances, and funding impacts that may affect development or construction execution.
  • Portfolio, Program, and Project Management — Required
    Demonstrated ability to manage an active portfolio of projects and programs from kick-off through deployment, with emphasis on development and construction delivery. Must be able to track multiple concurrent workstreams, understand key development and construction phase gates, manage competing priorities, and maintain visibility across scope, schedule, budget, quality, risk, and partner alignment.
  • Project Progress Reporting, Forecasting, and Schedule Management — Required
    Ability to build, maintain, and communicate accurate project and portfolio reporting, including checkpoint progression, construction readiness, schedule updates, forecast accuracy, risk items, budget impacts, vendor performance, and action item status. Experience developing and driving schedule execution, baseline timelines, checkpoint deliverables, and recovery plans.
  • Risk Management, Issue Resolution, and Escalation — Required
    Ability to proactively identify project, portfolio, vendor, budget, schedule, compliance, permitting, construction, and field execution risks. Must be able to assess impact, recommend solutions, drive resolution where appropriate, and call out critical issues to management with clear facts, options, and recommended next steps.
  • Leadership, Resource Management, and Informal Influence — Required
    Strong ability to provide guidance, direction, and informal leadership to vendors, peers, and cross-functional partners. Must be comfortable acting as a first point of contact for questions, blockers, and critical issues while coordinating internal and external resources across multiple projects or programs.
  • Partner Communication, Negotiation, and Alignment — Required
    Strong professional presentation skills, including the ability to lead internal and vendor deployment calls, deliver clear status updates, communicate risks and decisions, document action items, and collaborate effectively across a distributed team. Ability to support negotiations and issue resolution with property owners, landlords, municipalities, vendors, and internal partners on matters related to lease terms, rights-of-way, permitting, site access, deliverables, and project execution.
  • Construction Vendor Management and Field Execution Accountability — Preferred
    Ability to manage construction-related vendor deliverables, monitor performance, lead vendor discussions, drive accountability, resolve blockers, and ensure work is completed in accordance with scope, timelines, quality expectations, safety expectations, construction standards, and contractual requirements.
  • Process Discipline and Continuous Improvement — Preferred
    Ability to identify process gaps, reporting inconsistencies, recurring blockers, and execution challenges across development and construction workstreams. Must be able to recommend and help implement process improvements that drive consistency, accountability, operational efficiency, and portfolio execution.
  • Microsoft Office and Business Tools — Preferred
    Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Adobe Acrobat. Candidates should be comfortable building leadership-ready presentations, handling project documentation, maintaining trackers, and organizing complex information for decision-making. Familiarity with AI productivity tools such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar platforms is a plus.
  • Project Management Systems — Preferred
    Experience using Microsoft Project or similar project management tools. Candidates will be expected to work within Magenta Built or other internal project management platforms to build and maintain project timelines, track checkpoint deliverables, manage project data, and support active portfolio reporting.


Licenses and Certifications:

  • Project Management Professional (PMP) (Preferred)

Additional:

  • Must be at least 18 years of age
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States

Are you ready to help discover new medicines for people living with cardiovascular and metabolic diseases?   • Analyze data and document experiments accurately in the electronic laboratory notebook.
  • Present results at lab and department meetings.
  • Assist in writing research documents and scientific publications.
  • undefined

  • Strong communication and creative problem-solving skills, with the ability to work collaboratively in a matrixed team environment.
  • Exemplary laboratory practices and record-keeping skills.

You will work shoulder-to-shoulder with dedicated multi-functional engineering teams across vehicle subsystems — software, hardware, validation, and systems — to integrate their work into our autonomous DRIVE SW platform, while achieving or exceeding all relevant NVIDIA and automotive standards and guidelines. What sets this role apart: you bring real software engineering depth, specifically in embedded systems and platform software, driving engineering teams with credibility, attention to detail, and AI automation. The work is exciting, impactful, and fast-paced. We have customers and competition.


What you'll be doing:

  • Lead multiple, concurrent complex programs across the autonomous driving platform — from embedded platform bring-up through production release.
  • Drive new platform technologies across the full stack: embedded OS, platform drivers, middleware, sensor integration, and validation.
  • Run automotive software development and releases in a highly dynamic environment, maintaining quality across rapid release cadences.
  • Translate deep embedded and SW knowledge into actionable program structures — defining scope, roadmaps, schedules, and milestones.
  • Identify and resolve risks and issues that affect release scope, schedule, and quality, especially those spanning SW/HW boundaries.
  • Identify and lead multi-functional dependencies proactively, including those spanning global engineering teams.
  • Improve processes and procedures within the team; streamline day-to-day operations with an eye for scalable engineering workflow using AI.
  • Communicate regularly with team members to set shared expectations and provide timely updates on progress, risks, and decisions.

What We Need to See

  • BS/MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience).
  • 12+ years of proven experience, with at least 8 years in Technical Program Management driving software engineering programs and releasing commercial products.
  • Solid understanding of embedded systems software: OS fundamentals (Linux, QNX, or similar RTOS), platform drivers, sensor middleware, and SW/HW integration.
  • Strong technical competence to engage deeply with engineering teams, debug program-level issues, and make sound trade-off calls across SW and HW domains.
  • Consistent track record of delivering scalable, complex programs in fast-paced, multi-functional environments.
  • Strong communication, organizational, and leadership skills — you can translate deep technical complexity into streamlined executive updates and drive alignment across large organizations.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • You have shipped embedded software in automotive, robotics, or a related domain to get software running reliably on constrained, safety-relevant hardware.
  • Direct experience in autonomous vehicle platform development, including ADAS software integration, sensor fusion stacks, or platform validation.
  • Familiarity with automotive-grade software standards (ISO 26262, ASPICE, or equivalent) and how they interact with program execution.
  • Background leading global programs across time zones with geographically distributed engineering teams.
  • Expertise in Agile and Scrum methodology; PMP or Scrum Master certification is a plus, with proficiency with Jira and PMP tools with agility and scale.

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. If you want to help make autonomous vehicles a reality, we want to hear from you!

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 200,000 USD - 322,000 USD for Level 5, and 240,000 USD - 379,500 USD for Level 6.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

At ChristianaCare, excellence in patient care begins long before a procedure starts. We are seeking a Sterile Processing Technician to ensure surgical instruments and equipment are cleaned, assembled, packaged, and sterilized to support patient safety and clinical excellence.


This role performs instrument processing in compliance with CBSPD, AAMI, and HSPA standards while following evidence‑based practices and safety policies related to infection prevention and bloodborne pathogens. Technicians maintain knowledge of aseptic technique and basic microbiology and participate in ongoing training to stay current with evolving sterilization practices.



ChristianaCare Benefits

At ChristianaCare, we invest in you—professionally and personally.

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage available on your first day

Cleans and decontaminates surgical instruments and other medical equipment following established policy and procedure.

Inspects, assembles, packages and sterilizes medical devices following manufacturer’s recommendations and established procedure.

Assemble, wrap and label basic and especially specialty instruments and sets according to information in the CensiTrfac system for tracking purposes.

  • Partner with third‑party data management teams on schema changes and new solutions, including reviewing business requirements, writing technical specifications, and completing system testing.

title: Children's Health Executive Director of Philanthropy
description:
Job Description:

Our Story: More Than 150 Years of Bold Healing

Intermountain Health was built by people who refused to accept the impossible. In 1873, four Sisters of Charity of Leavenworth arrived in Denver with just $9 and a tiny wagon, raised money in saloons and mines, and opened Saint Joseph Hospital to care for anyone in need, regardless of ability to pay. In 1905, LDS Hospital opened its doors in Salt Lake City and was hailed as the finest hospital west of the Mississippi. In 1922, Primary Children’s Hospital was born from a simple, powerful conviction: every child deserves care. Today, it ranks among the nation’s top children’s hospitals.

In 1975, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints made an extraordinary gift, donating its 15-hospital system to the communities it served and launching Intermountain as an independent, nonprofit health system. What followed was five decades of relentless innovation, national recognition for high-quality care at lower cost, and the creation of Select Health. In 2022, Intermountain Healthcare and SCL Health came together, uniting two proud legacies of compassion. Today, Intermountain Health is one of the nation’s leading nonprofit health systems, with more than 60,000 caregivers and 33 hospitals and about 400 clinics across Utah, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, and Wyoming, all driven by one mission: helping people live the healthiest lives possible.

Philanthropy has fueled this story from the very beginning, and Intermountain Foundation carries that spirit forward every day. The Foundation builds relationships and partnerships that inspire generosity, turning donor vision into new hospitals, breakthrough technology, lifesaving research, and programs that reach families when they need it most. Its momentum is unmistakable: through Primary Promise, the largest philanthropic investment of its kind in Utah, donors surpassed a historic $600 million goal to build the nation’s model health system for children. For the next Children’s Health Executive Director of Philanthropy, this is more than a legacy to honor. It is a launchpad for what comes next.

The Children’s Health Executive Director of Philanthropy is a transformational leader who champions a bold vision for philanthropy across Intermountain Health’s Children's Health enterprise. As one of the Foundation’s most influential leadership roles, this position inspires, develops, and empowers a high-performing team of major, planned, and blended giving professionals while driving extraordinary philanthropic outcomes from individuals, corporations, and foundations.


Serving as a trusted advisor to the presidents of Primary Children’s Hospital campuses, the Executive Director helps shape and advance strategic fundraising priorities that accelerate innovation, expand access to world-class care, and transform the lives of children and families throughout the region. This leader provides visionary stewardship of the Children’s Health Cabinet, aligning volunteer leadership, community champions, physicians, and hospital executives around ambitious philanthropic goals that fuel system-wide priorities.


In close partnership with the Canyons Region Vice President of Philanthropy, hospital leadership, the Foundation Board, and regional development teams, the Executive Director cultivates a vibrant culture of philanthropy, inspires generosity, and deepens community engagement across multiple markets and locations. This role serves as a catalyst for growth, building meaningful relationships that translate into transformational investments supporting capital projects, breakthrough technology, innovative programs, medical research, and patient-centered initiatives.


As a frontline fundraising leader, the Executive Director manages a portfolio of highly engaged principal and major gift prospects, while strategically integrating physicians, executives, trustees, and volunteers into sophisticated cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies. The Executive Director leads by example, demonstrating excellence in donor engagement and creating opportunities for philanthropists to make a lasting impact on children’s health.

As the senior-most philanthropy leader for Children’s Health priorities, this individual mentors, coaches, and elevates a talented team of Philanthropy Officers, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and performance. Through data-driven decision-making, clear metrics, and industry-leading best practices, the Executive Director ensures exceptional execution and measurable results.


Most importantly, this leader serves as a visible and passionate ambassador for the Intermountain Foundation, inspiring donors, volunteers, caregivers, and community partners to rally around a shared mission: creating a healthier future for every child. Through visionary leadership, strategic partnership, and relentless passion for the mission, the Children’s Health Executive Director of Philanthropy helps shape the future of pediatric healthcare and philanthropy across the Intermountain system.

Summary


The Children’s Health Executive Director of Philanthropy is a key leadership, management and mentorship position at Intermountain Foundation, providing oversight, leadership, guidance, and motivation to assigned major, planned, and blended philanthropy for both individuals and corporations/foundations. The Executive Director serves as a liaison and provides counsel to the Primary Children's Hospital presidents regarding philanthropy. This position works with assigned Directors of Philanthropy and other Philanthropy Officers to utilize and manage the Children's Health Cabinet, and determines the vision, strategy, and operations of philanthropy across multiple locations and system priorities. In collaboration with the Canyons Region Vice President of Philanthropy, local hospital leaders, the Foundation's Philanthropy Board, and locally assigned Foundation development staff, this position instills a culture of philanthropy and deepens relationships in the community for the purposes of generating philanthropic revenue. The Children’s Health Executive Director of Philanthropy participates in Foundation strategic planning efforts for philanthropy to meet the capital, technology, project, program, and research funding priorities of the system. This position carries a significant portfolio of high-wealth donor prospects and works continually to integrate hospital leadership, physicians, and volunteers into a carefully planned program of cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship, while ensuring sound prospect management by participating in regular, ongoing, system-level gift-management meetings. The Executive Director acts as the most senior Philanthropy Officer within the assigned areas and system priorities, while mentoring, managing, measuring, and motivating assigned Philanthropy Officers. Using KPIs, metrics and data-driven decision making, ensures accountability and implementation of industry best practices. In addition, the Executive Director provides supervision of and motivation to Intermountain Foundation staff who are assigned to their local office but report to the Intermountain Foundation's Central Office. The Executive Director interacts directly with the Canyons Region Vice President to set and align team strategies for the team, as well as individual donors/prospects. The Executive Director acts as the face of the foundation for local and system wide fundraising initiatives.

Scope


This management position strategically interacts with multiple levels of the organization and the external community. The Executive Director of Philanthropy oversees the achievement of significant philanthropy revenue goals for assigned system priorities and areas; works with the Canyon Region Vice President to assure assigned business efficiency as measured by cost-to-raise-a-dollar benchmarks; assesses assigned Philanthropy Officer performance using standardized and tracked metrics and KPIs; works with the Canyons Region Vice President to develop and implement industry best practices. Effectively leads assigned Director(s) of Philanthropy to set vision and strategic direction for the Children’s Health Cabinet. Ensures high-levels of donor-prospect engagement for entire team through effective leadership and mentorship, as well as successful achievement of campaign and financial targets; and provides leadership to staff, to achieve highest professional standards. This position reports to the Canyons Region Vice President of Philanthropy, and in that reporting partnership, consistently represents and works to advance the interests, ambitions, alignment, and collaborative spirit of Intermountain Foundation with a One Intermountain approach.

Job Essentials


1. Develops and implements major, planned and blended gift strategies for self and major gift team for achieving annual philanthropy revenue targets.

2. Collaborates with the Canyons Region Vice President of Philanthropy, local hospital administrators, system leaders, physicians, board members, and staff to achieve high-level donor-prospect engagement and common fundraising objectives.

3. Using Foundation metrics and performance measurements, develops and manages a personal portfolio of major-gift prospects to achieve annual performance and financial targets. Ensures development of portfolio and proper management for assigned development officers.

4. Using Foundation metrics and performance measurements, manages a team of gift officers to achieve annual performance and financial targets.

5. Develops and manages a comprehensive fundraising program with emphasis on major and planned gift support from area individuals, families, foundations, organizations and corporations including a systematic process of identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship.

6. Oversees the development of local gift proposals and agreements, consistent with Foundation policies, procedures, and guidelines.

7. Regularly participates in leadership meetings and is a high-impact contributor to Foundation strategic planning.

8. Oversees the implementation and management of system and special funding campaigns. Serves as a respected member of facility leadership team as an enthusiastic extension and representative of Intermountain Foundation.

9. Recruits, retains, develops, and mentors a team of Gift Officers to ensure achievement of local and system-level fundraising targets.

10. Provides day-to-day supervision of Foundation staff who may sit locally, but report to the Foundation's Central Office. Provides direction and resources to inspire and continually strengthen the Foundation Board in their quest to carry out Intermountain's mission.

11. Collaborates with Intermountain's Governance Office to achieve optimal engagement and management of campaign committees and assigned Philanthropy Boards, consistent with established roles and responsibilities.

12. Develops appropriate case statements for research, capital, project, and program funding priorities.

13. Manages resources to accomplish appropriate funds-raised-to-expense ratio.

14. Collaborates with Central Office Operations/Finance & Administration to build and manage assigned annual budget.

15. Collaborates with Central Office Operations and Intermountain Capital and Program Planning teams to establish funding priorities consistent with Intermountain's priorities. Adheres to continual improvement, facilitating and championing change as we go and grow.

16. Serves as a public speaker on behalf of Intermountain Healthcare as requested.

17. Actively engages in the community.

18. Pursues continued professional development through the Association of Healthcare Philanthropy, The Advisory Board and other industry groups to enhance and increase fundraising skills, and to stay abreast of industry trends and best practices, related taxes, and other regulatory developments.

19. Serves as a subject matter expert and resource to others on issues related to healthcare philanthropy.

Minimum Qualifications


  • Bachelor's degree in non-profit management, philanthropy studies, public administration, public relations, communications, marketing, English, business, or other related degree. Education must be obtained through an accredited institution. Degree will be verified.
  • Seven years of experience as an accomplished fundraising professional with demonstrated success in achieving financial goals and performance standards through major and planned gifts using metrics and measurement tools.
  • Experience successfully leading teams or projects.
  • Effective and motivating interpersonal skills, including relationship building and communication, in-person, over the phone, and via email with diverse groups of people (e.g., volunteers, civic and business leaders, board members, patients and their families, hospital staff).
  • Demonstrated success in organizing and effectively utilizing volunteer leadership (e.g., boards, committees) in effective foundation or fundraising practices.
  • Strong project planning and management skills, demonstrating detail orientation, timeliness, and ability to work under pressure.
  • Advanced writing skills that produce clear, accurate, and persuasive communications (e.g., proposal materials, letters, presentations).
  • Effective public speaking and presentation skills.
  • Success in collaborating with colleagues in a complex matrix organization.
  • Experience using common software programs including Raiser's Edge, donor records systems, Internet research tools, and social media applications.
  • A commitment to Intermountain's inspiring spirit and strong values and the traditions that have built its reputation and its mission.


Preferred Qualifications


  • Master's degree in Business or related field.
  • Association for Healthcare Philanthropy (AHP) certification as CFRE and/or FAHP.
  • Fundraising experience in a healthcare environment.
  • Demonstrated history of increased responsibility and progression in the fundraising profession.
  • A demonstrated history of activity and awareness with local community needs and dynamics.

Facilitates open, professional (verbal, nonverbal, written) communication which includes active listening and teaching to achieve mutual understanding, role modeling by example.

SERVICE ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Maintains and accurately communicates updates for surgeon preference cards within the applicable service line.

Cleans and prepares instruments for terminal sterilization, following surgical procedure. Assists other members of the team with terminal cleaning of the room.

description:
TPC Summerlin is a private par-72, 7,243-yard golf course located in Las Vegas, Nevada. Carved from a magnificent swath of rugged desert terrain by renowned golf course architect Bobby Weed, TPC Summerlin creates one of the most visually stunning tests of golf in Nevada.

Tee up your career as a part of our team with the TPC Network!

title: Quality Management System Auditor
description:
Location: Salt Lake City, United States of America

Thales people architect solutions that are relied upon to deliver operational advantage at every decisive moment throughout the mission. Defence and armed forces customers rely on us to deliver the full range of defensive systems for land, sea, and air. From early warning, to threat neutralisation, our platforms cover all levels from very short-range systems, to extended protection across the entire battle-space including Airspace Mobility Solutions, Vehicles and Tactical Systems and Missile Defence, Optronics, and Radar.

Quality Management System Auditor

Salt Lake City, UT (Fully Onsite)

Position Summary

Thales is looking for a Quality Management System Auditor to assess the effectiveness of its quality management system and evaluate compliance with applicable standards and established procedures.


In this position, you will plan and conduct quality management system audits, review processes and supporting documentation, and identify nonconformities and opportunities for improvement. You will communicate audit findings, work with teams to follow up on corrective actions, and assess their effectiveness to support continuous improvement.


Referral Bonus Eligibility: Tier 1 - $2,500



Regulatory Compliance Requirements


  • Must be a US Person as defined in applicable law.
  • Must be a U.S. Person as defined in applicable law, or otherwise authorized or eligible for authorization, to access to hardware, software, technology or technical data controlled under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and/or the Export Administration Regulations (EAR).

Key Areas of Responsibility


  • Contribute to the internal audit schedule and independently plan assigned audits by reviewing prior findings, process performance, changes, risks, quality management system documentation, and corrective action records; define the scope, criteria, evidence requirements, and timing with relevant stakeholders.
  • Conduct internal process and quality management system audits through interviews, observation, document review, and objective evidence sampling; perform assigned external supplier assessments supporting qualification, ongoing monitoring, and corrective action verification while maintaining objectivity, confidentiality, and independence.
  • Evaluate audit evidence against applicable requirements, document clear, factual findings and opportunities for improvement, classify identified gaps using established criteria, and escalate significant quality or compliance concerns to the Quality Manager.
  • Facilitate opening and closing meetings and prepare and present audit reports communicating scope, findings, supporting evidence, applicable requirements, and required follow-up to process owners and management; support assigned customer audits and external certification assessments by coordinating evidence and following up on findings.
  • Coordinate corrective action follow-up with process owners, evaluate proposed actions, monitor commitments, verify implementation and effectiveness, document closure recommendations, and escalate overdue or ineffective actions.
  • Maintain accurate audit records and metrics on audit completion, findings, corrective action status, and recurring issues; analyze results to identify trends and recommend improvements to processes, procedures, and audit practices.



Minimum Qualifications


  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Quality, or a related discipline, with a minimum of two years of relevant experience in quality assurance, quality management systems, or auditing; or ASQ Certified Quality Engineer certification with a minimum of four years of relevant internal auditing experience.
  • Demonstrated experience independently conducting process or quality management system audits, including planning, evidence evaluation, reporting, and corrective action follow-up, with the ability to manage assigned audits and competing priorities within established schedules and procedures.
  • Experience applying ISO 9001:2015 and/or AS9100 Revision D requirements in a manufacturing or production environment, along with completion of recognized internal auditor training for ISO 9001 and/or AS9100 and demonstrated ability to apply the relevant standards during audits.
  • Ability to interpret quality management system requirements and evaluate compliance using objective evidence, with strong analytical skills and professional judgment to identify gaps, assess their significance, and recognize recurring issues; working knowledge of root cause analysis, corrective action processes, and methods for verifying corrective action effectiveness.
  • Strong listening, interviewing, written communication, and presentation skills, including communicating findings clearly and constructively when evidence or conclusions are challenged; ability to collaborate effectively with employees, suppliers, and leaders across functions and organizational levels in a matrixed and geographically diverse business environment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and tools used to maintain audit records, track corrective actions, and report metrics.



Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer at the time of hire. This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship or for assuming sponsorship of an employment visa now or in the future.




Special Position Requirements


  • Ability to perform assigned duties while sitting or standing and to lift up to 25 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Ability to travel approximately 10–15% annually.

Experience with cloud network and hybrid connectivity preferred.

  • Leadership skills with the ability to mentor junior engineers and lead cross-functional teams.

title: Solid Propulsion Engineer
description:
Lieu : Herstal, Belgium

MISSION

Thales is a world leader in precision guided rocket system for helicopters and jet aircraft.

As a Solid Propellant Engineer at Thales, you will face a wide variety of challenges including all aspects of energetic materials, from propulsion to initiation and pyrotechnical compositions. You will be responsible for the development, design and testing of solid rocket motors (SRM) used in defense applications, including their mechanical or electronical sides. You will work closely with customers, system engineering, ballistics team, design office, industrial methods, production and suppliers to ensure that SRM meet performance, safety, and quality requirements. You will be part of a multidisciplinary team and will have the opportunity to work on cutting-edge technologies.

RESPONSABILITY

· Develop and improve rocket motor, from concept to production, covering all main sub components (propellant grain, igniter, casing, nozzle, etc.)

· Work closely with customers (internal or external) to understand their needs and requirements (performance, environmental, lifecycle, etc.), develop solution architecture and product specifications accordingly

· Work closely with ballistics simulation team in order to convert operational performance requirements into proper propellant grain and overall SRM specifications.

· Specify requirements to suppliers and manage their development, production and quality control

· Conduct simulation, testing and evaluation of components, both in-house and at external test facilities

· Evaluate final product’s overall performance, reliability and safety

· Develop and maintain pyrotechnic-related documentation such FMECA, safety, reliability analysis

· Support production of in-service SRM, including resolving quality issues and developing improvements

· Participate in technical reviews: design reviews, engineering change boards and failure investigations

· Perform detailed documentation to track project development and design process

· Stay current with industry trends and technological advancements related to solid propulsion for defense applications

PROFILE

· Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in Engineering, Aerospace, Mechanics, Physics or related field

· Min 5 years of proven experience in solid propulsion design and pyro products in aerospace & defense industry

· Knowledge of avionics, external & internal ballistics of propellant grain, thermal analysis, fluid dynamics, mechanical design, simulation tools (ANSYS, MATLAB, etc.), formulations and related manufacturing processes

· Experience with design and execution of a full lifecycle product development (simulation, design, develop, test prototypes, manufacture and implement)

· Strong project management and problem-solving skills

· Excellent written and verbal communication skills

· Ability to work independently and collaboratively with cross-functional teams

· Familiarity with industry standards and regulations related to energetic and aerospace materials

· You are self-motivated and like to take initiatives.

· English (spoken and written)

· French (spoken and written) is a plus

description:
Position Summary:

At Securian Financial, we are committed to providing exceptional service and delivering on our promises to customers, beneficiaries, employers, and business partners. As a Claims Examiner, you will investigate, evaluate, and adjudicate claims while balancing accuracy, timeliness, compliance, risk management, and customer experience. description:
WHY PATIENTS NEED YOU

Join one of Pfizer's top revenue drivers globally at a defining moment and help shape the future for patients living with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM).


WHAT YOU WILL ACHIEVE
Vyndaqel (Vyndamax in the US) is the standard of care for ATTR-CM, a rare and fatal cardiac disease with an average life expectancy of about three years when untreated. Launched around the world roughly seven years ago, Vyndaqel transformed care as the first treatment to show a significant mortality benefit for patients.

Our early focus was driving suspicion and diagnosis of this underdiagnosed disease. Today, that work continues alongside a growing emphasis on differentiation in an increasingly competitive market.


This role reports to the Global Vyndaqel Lead and partners closely with the global ATTR-CM cross-functional team, including ICO, Medical, the US organization, and a broad range of other functions.


The ideal candidate brings strong HCP marketing experience, proven leadership, strategic thinking, and agility. You communicate clearly, think analytically, execute with attention to detail, and have a track record of building collaboration across functions.


While this role is a secondment, there is a potential for it to become a full-time position.


HOW YOU WILL ACHIEVE IT

The Global Vyndaqel HCP Lead owns the global HCP strategy and the tactics that bring it to life. Key responsibilities include:


Brand strategy and positioning

  • Oversee brand strategic planning competitive differentiation, and KOL engagement.
  • Define and evolve a compelling long-term Vyndaqel narrative as the competitive and scientific landscape changes, ensuring Pfizer continues to lead this disease space.
  • Assess impact using insights in partnership with ICO, and work closely with regional and local colleagues to evolve our approach based on market needs and customer response.

Execution and tactics

  • Oversee development of compelling HCP promotional resources that deliver on strategy, tailored to physician segments.
  • Work with Global Marketing, Medical, & PMG to integrate strategies into our congress and Med Ed presence.
  • Partner with ICO and US teams to ensure strategies are pulled through at the local level.

Cross-functional leadership and business planning

  • Ensure strategic pull-through across all aspects of the team’s work, setting priorities for the team & driving efficiency in work processes.
  • Lead the Brand Strategy Refresh (BSR) process for the cross-functional team, including ICO, Medical, and US teams.
  • Own global business performance commentary, ensuring alignment with the US and ICO teams.

Must-Have

  • Extensive HCP marketing experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead an x-functional team effectively in developing and implementing marketing strategy.

Team Overview

The Product TPM team operates at the intersection of business, technology, and delivery, enabling the successful development and rollout of scalable, customer-centric solutions. At the Consultant (P03) level, the team is composed of Technical Product Managers who own feature-level delivery while collaborating closely with engineering, design, and business stakeholders.
The team functions within an Agile framework, ensuring continuous delivery of high-quality product increments through iterative development, sprint cycles, and regular feedback loops. Each TPM is responsible for managing specific product modules or features, contributing to the broader product roadmap while aligning execution with organizational goals and customer needs.

This is a hybrid position and involves regular performance of job responsibilities virtually as well as in-person at an assigned TU office location for a minimum of two days a week.

Role Overview And Core Responsibilities

Role Overview And Core Responsibilities

1. Product Ownership

  • Own and manage assigned product features or modules from concept to delivery
  • Define detailed user stories, acceptance criteria, and maintain the product backlog
  • Prioritize deliverables based on business value, customer impact, and feasibility

2. Product Strategy & Roadmap Support

  • Contribute to product roadmap planning and execution
  • Align feature development with overall product vision and business objectives
  • Incorporate stakeholder input, user feedback, and analytics insights

3. Technical Collaboration

  • Translate business requirements into clear technical specifications
  • Work closely with engineering teams on solution design and implementation
  • Assess technical trade-offs, dependencies, and constraints
  • Ensure adherence to scalability, security, and performance standards

4. Agile Delivery Execution

  • Actively participate in Agile ceremonies (sprint planning, grooming, stand-ups, retrospectives)
  • Ensure timely and high-quality delivery of product increments
  • Support continuous improvement in development and delivery processes

5. Stakeholder Management

  • Collaborate with business, engineering, and UX/design teams
  • Act as the primary point of contact for owned features
  • Communicate progress, risks, and outcomes effectively

6. Data-Driven Decision Making

  • Define and track KPIs for product features
  • Use product analytics and user insights to drive improvements
  • Optimize product performance, usability, and adoption

7. Product Lifecycle Support

  • Support the full product lifecycle including requirement gathering, development, testing, and release
  • Assist in documentation, training, and user adoption initiatives
  • Ensure smooth rollout and continuous enhancement of features

Required Knowledge And Experiences


The Technical Platform Manager (TPM) is responsible for driving the strategy, roadmap, adoption, governance, and delivery of enterprise platform services that enable secure, scalable, and efficient software development and infrastructure operations across the organization.
